capabilities.name: Authentication
capabilities.rationale: Protects the system secret from being leaked via network analysis.
capabilities.description: Secures API endpoints using bearer tokens and constant-time comparisons to prevent timing attacks.

features.name: Bearer Verification
features.rationale: Defends against timing attacks that could reveal the secret token.
features.description: Verifies bearer tokens with a constant-time algorithm to prevent secret leakage.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents statistical analysis from leaking the secret token bits.
behaviors.summary: Uses constant-time comparison to verify bearer tokens.
behaviors.detail: The system extracts the token from the request header and compares it against the secret. Instead of using a standard inequality check, it utilizes a specialized constant-time function to ensure the comparison duration does not depend on the number of matching characters.

features.name: Token Management
features.rationale: Maintains secure session state without re-authenticating every request.
features.description: Handles the lifecycle of bearer tokens including retrieval, storage, and clearing.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures unauthorized access is blocked before any data transfer.
behaviors.summary: Retrieves and stores the operator's bearer token for subsequent requests.
behaviors.detail: The system stores a unique bearer token in local storage to persist the active operator session. If the storage key is missing, the client is considered unauthenticated.

behaviors.rationale: Allows seamless API calls without repeating the login process.
behaviors.summary: Stores the bearer token retrieved from the system or user input.
behaviors.detail: Upon successful authentication or manual token entry, the system writes the token to local storage for reuse.

features.name: Bearer Auth
features.rationale: Protects the bus from credential theft and timing attacks.
features.description: Validates incoming requests using a constant-time comparison against a configured secret.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures no unauthorized agent can join the fleet.
behaviors.summary: Rejects requests without a valid Bearer token.
behaviors.detail: All HTTP endpoints require an 'Authorization: Bearer <secret>' header or a query string token (for browser SSE). The system checks the token against the TUBEMAIL_SECRET environment variable. If the token is missing or malformed, a 401 Unauthorized error is returned. The check uses constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks.

capabilities.name: Error Handling
capabilities.rationale: Auxiliary surface — error responses keep the product usable but are not the core value
capabilities.description: Catches exceptions from handlers and returns standardized JSON-RPC error responses with internal error codes.

features.name: Crash Recovery
features.rationale: Prevents unhandled exceptions from breaking the connection.
features.description: Catches exceptions raised during handler execution and sends an error response with details about the failure.

behaviors.rationale: Provides visibility into server-side failures.
behaviors.summary: Sends an error response when a handler crashes.
behaviors.detail: Catches any Exception, logs the exception details, and sends a response with code -32603 and a message describing the internal error.

behaviors.rationale: Clearly identifies protocol contract violations.
behaviors.summary: Sends a specific error for a missing method.
behaviors.detail: Catches a JsonRpcError exception (code -32601) when no handler exists for the requested method and responds accordingly.

features.name: Auth Error Handling
features.rationale: Maintains consistent timing responses to hide authentication logic.
features.description: Responds to invalid tokens without revealing if the token is missing or wrong.

behaviors.rationale: Hides information about token validity to prevent reconnaissance.
behaviors.summary: Responds consistently to missing and invalid bearer tokens.
behaviors.detail: Whether the request lacks a bearer token or provides one that does not match the secret, the system returns the same error code. This consistency prevents attackers from deducing the format or presence of the secret token through timing analysis.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents a single failure from crashing the entire agent.
behaviors.summary: Logs exceptions from hub operations and continues operation.
behaviors.detail: If the hub registration or forwarding fails, the exception is logged at an error level, and the channel continues trying to pump events until the process terminates.

behaviors.rationale: Alerts the operator to system failures.
behaviors.summary: Shows an error message when a request to fetch permissions fails.
behaviors.detail: If the fetch request fails (e.g., network error, API error), the component displays the error message in the inbox. It does not prevent the operator from acting on cached data if available.

behaviors.rationale: Alerts the operator to action failures.
behaviors.summary: Shows an error message when resolving a permission action fails.
behaviors.detail: If the resolve action (approve/deny) fails (e.g., worker offline), the component displays the error message. The queued action remains until manually cancelled or the error resolves.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents a single network issue from halting the entire interface.
behaviors.summary: Catches fetch errors and logs them without breaking the UI.
behaviors.detail: If the request to /health fails, the error is caught and logged to the console. The version display remains empty, and the rest of the sidebar functions normally.

behaviors.rationale: Immediate feedback allows users to address connection issues promptly.
behaviors.summary: Detects and displays WebSocket errors to the user.
behaviors.detail: If the WebSocket connection fails or encounters an error, the system sets the error state and displays an error message. The pane enters a disconnected state, preventing further interaction until reconnected.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents resource leaks and race conditions in the WebSocket layer.
behaviors.summary: Prevents zombie connections on reconnection attempts.
behaviors.detail: Before initiating a new connection, the system closes any existing WebSocket to avoid multiple concurrent connections or orphaned handlers that could cause data loss.

capabilities.name: Core MCP
capabilities.rationale: Seed the must-be surface: CRUD, data model, primary API contract — the tools without which the product is broken.
capabilities.description: Core MCP tools. Must-be functionality (Kano 2).

features.name: Fleet Monitoring
features.rationale: Allows operators to track active agent states in real-time.
features.description: Provides a live view of the status and health of all managed AI workers.

behaviors.rationale: Provides visibility into the entire fleet state.
behaviors.summary: The system exposes current status of all registered workers to authorized clients.
behaviors.detail: The platform maintains a live registry of local worker instances and broadcasts their operational status over WebSocket.

behaviors.rationale: Required to maintain visibility in a distributed environment.
behaviors.summary: The system reports the current state of all connected agents.
behaviors.detail: The system queries the internal state store and returns aggregated metrics regarding worker uptime, current task load, and resource consumption.

features.name: Terminal Operations
features.rationale: Provides direct access to the agent execution environment.
features.description: Execute commands and view logs for the active agents.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains a clutter-free terminal view focused on output.
behaviors.summary: Controls the terminal pane output, refresh, and navigation without a footer.
behaviors.detail: The Terminal Pane utilizes icons such as 'RefreshCw', 'RotateCw', and 'X' for control actions. It operates without a footer, placing focus on the terminal output, though it may include a 'v0.1.0' version identifier in the sidebar.

features.name: tm_recording_status
features.rationale: Communicates critical system states like recording activity or security warnings.
features.description: Visual cues for recording status and system alerts.

behaviors.rationale: Standardizes state communication across the interface.
behaviors.summary: Uses specific icon sets to denote recording toggles, help, and security alerts.
behaviors.detail: The system uses 'Circle' and 'CircleDot' for recording toggle states. It also employs 'CircleCheck', 'CircleX', 'ShieldAlert', and 'Loader2' to indicate various operational states, ensuring a unified visual language.

features.name: Worker Stats
features.rationale: Allows operators to distinguish between idle, busy, and stuck agents.
features.description: Reports detailed per-worker process statistics and activity levels.

behaviors.rationale: Granular visibility is necessary to troubleshoot individual agents.
behaviors.summary: Delivers specific metrics for individual agents through a tool interface.
behaviors.detail: The system retrieves and displays process-level details such as current CPU load, memory usage, and task duration for a selected worker.

features.name: Worker Ticketing
features.rationale: Enables secure remote control of local workers via standardized HTTP tokens.
features.description: Issues secure, time-bound access tokens for connecting to specific worker nodes.

behaviors.rationale: Primary mechanism for granting remote access control to agents.
behaviors.summary: Issues a valid WebSocket upgrade ticket for a target worker with an expiration timestamp.
behaviors.detail: Upon receiving a request for a worker, the system validates the token format using a silent drop fix for concurrency issues and issues a ticket bound to a specific worker ID. The ticket includes metadata such as expiry time and scope to prevent cross-worker access attempts.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures that scope isolation between different workers is strictly enforced.
behaviors.summary: Prevents unauthorized access by rejecting tickets issued for incorrect workers.
behaviors.detail: The system cross-checks the requested worker ID against the ticket's bound ID. If a request is made for worker B with a ticket issued for worker A, the system rejects the upgrade attempt immediately to enforce scope isolation.

features.name: Telemetry Streaming
features.rationale: Allows operators to observe agent behavior in real-time without polling.
features.description: Provides a persistent stream of event data for active workers.

behaviors.rationale: Provides low-latency visibility into agent execution.
behaviors.summary: Delivers a continuous SSE stream of worker events.
behaviors.detail: When a client subscribes to a worker's stream, the system forwards relevant telemetry events (logs, commands, errors) from the worker process to the client's endpoint.

features.name: Worker Delegation
features.rationale: Facilitates complex workflows by allowing distributed task offloading.
features.description: Enables agents to forward tasks to other agents in the fleet.

behaviors.rationale: Supports multi-host agent-to-agent delegation scenarios.
behaviors.summary: Routes external requests to specific worker endpoints.
behaviors.detail: The system accepts a delegation request with a target worker ID, forwards the payload to that worker's address, and returns the response to the initiator.

features.name: Agent Status Query
features.rationale: Enables operators to know if a worker is idle or processing.
features.description: Query the current operational state of a specific agent worker.

behaviors.rationale: Allows operators to wait for completion before retrying tasks.
behaviors.summary: Returns 'idle' or 'busy' status for a worker based on its last known activity.
behaviors.detail: The system returns 'idle' when a worker has no pending tasks or has completed a recent task, and returns 'busy' when a worker is actively processing a recent inbound work order without a completed reply yet.

behaviors.rationale: Signals to the orchestrator that the worker is available for new delegation.
behaviors.summary: Returns 'idle' when the worker has completed its last task.
behaviors.detail: When the last event on the worker's timeline is an outbound reply, the status is reported as 'idle', signaling availability for new work.

features.name: Worker Discovery
features.rationale: Allows operators to see fleet capacity before delegation.
features.description: Lists available AI workers and their connection status.

behaviors.rationale: Matches /api/workers endpoint contract.
behaviors.summary: Serves a list of online workers with metadata.
behaviors.detail: Returns a JSON array of worker objects containing status indicators and identifiers.

features.name: Agent Connection
features.rationale: Enables the control bus to reach the distributed worker fleet.
features.description: Establishes secure communication channels to local Claude Code workers.

behaviors.rationale: Prerequisite for all remote orchestration tasks.
behaviors.summary: The system establishes a persistent connection to a specified worker.
behaviors.detail: The system authenticates and creates a WebSocket endpoint for a local Claude Code worker, allowing for bidirectional communication of tasks and telemetry.

features.name: Task Dispatch
features.rationale: Core orchestration mechanism for driving agent workloads.
features.description: Sends instructions and data packets to active agents.

behaviors.rationale: Essential for performing agent duties remotely.
behaviors.summary: The system executes a request on the targeted agent.
behaviors.detail: Upon receiving a dispatch command, the system queues the task for the specified agent and waits for the completion callback or status update.

features.name: Multi-Host Delegation
features.rationale: Differentiates the product by decoupling logic from specific machines.
features.description: Routes work across multiple agents regardless of host location.

behaviors.rationale: Enables flexible, host-independent agent workflows.
behaviors.summary: The system forwards a task from one agent to another.
behaviors.detail: The system identifies the target agent based on the task metadata and relays the execution request, regardless of the source or destination host.

behaviors.rationale: Security is paramount to prevent unauthorized cross-host interference.
behaviors.summary: Authenticates an incoming delegation request from a remote agent.
behaviors.detail: The system validates the caller's identity and scope against a trusted registry of authorized agents before routing the request to the local target worker.

features.name: Agent Registry
features.rationale: Enables operators to see which agents are online and ready for work.
features.description: Maintains the roster of active workers and their current states.

behaviors.rationale: Allows visibility into the fleet.
behaviors.summary: Retrieves the current roster of connected workers.
behaviors.detail: The system queries the internal state to list all workers, including their unique identifiers, status, and current load.

features.name: Command Dispatch
features.rationale: Enables remote control and task assignment of AI workers.
features.description: Relays user-defined commands to specific agents or the fleet.

behaviors.rationale: Enables task execution.
behaviors.summary: Sends a command to a single worker via JSON-RPC.
behaviors.detail: The system accepts a command payload, validates the target worker is active, and forwards the request to the worker's stdio interface.

features.name: Event Relay
features.rationale: Keeps the hub updated with real-time agent activity.
features.description: Forwards worker events like status changes or completions.

behaviors.rationale: Provides real-time feedback.
behaviors.summary: Receives and broadcasts worker status updates.
behaviors.detail: The system listens on the worker's stdio for JSON-RPC notifications and pushes them to subscribed web clients via SSE.

features.name: Command Console
features.rationale: Allows users to interact with agents directly.
features.description: Provides a form to input and dispatch commands to specific workers.

behaviors.rationale: Enables manual control.
behaviors.summary: Accepts a command string and target worker ID for dispatch.
behaviors.detail: The user selects a worker and enters a command in a text field, which is then sent to the MCP layer for execution.

features.name: Ping
features.rationale: Enables quick health checks to confirm the server is reachable.
features.description: A lightweight tool to verify the MCP server connection is active.

behaviors.rationale: Validates the connection without incurring overhead.
behaviors.summary: Returns a 'pong' response to confirm server reachability.
behaviors.detail: The tool accepts no parameters and immediately returns the string 'pong'. This confirms that the MCP endpoint is operational and ready to handle requests.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents silent failures during initialization.
behaviors.summary: Handles unexpected connection errors gracefully.
behaviors.detail: If the server is not running or unreachable, the tool will fail with a standard network error rather than a malformed response, allowing the client to retry.

features.name: whoami
features.rationale: Provides immediate context about the server's state to the orchestrator.
features.description: Reports the server's identity, current health state, and operational metrics.

behaviors.rationale: Allows the operator to debug connection issues.
behaviors.summary: Returns server name, broken status, and operation counters.
behaviors.detail: The tool returns a dictionary containing the server name, a boolean indicating if the server is currently broken, and counters for how many times it has been broken or healed.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures state visibility aligns with actual server health.
behaviors.summary: Reflects real-time state changes from control endpoints.
behaviors.detail: The response data updates immediately if control endpoints like '/control/break' or '/control/heal' modify the internal state of the server.

features.name: refresh_tools
features.rationale: Updates the client interface to reflect new tools.
features.description: Notifies all connected clients that the list of available MCP tools has been updated.

behaviors.rationale: Updates client view of tools.
behaviors.summary: Sends a notification that the tool list has changed.
behaviors.detail: The system generates a ToolListChangedNotification and returns a confirmation message to the client.

features.name: Core Management
features.rationale: Defines the must-have functionality for the control bus.
features.description: Essential tools for monitoring, managing, and orchestrating local agent workers.

behaviors.rationale: Provides visibility into the connected agent fleet.
behaviors.summary: Displays a list of available MCP servers.
behaviors.detail: When the user invokes the MCP command, the system queries the available servers and renders a list of registered agents for inspection.

capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Every core tool must be idempotent-safe and return valid JSON on success and failure.

capabilities.name: Channel Transport
capabilities.rationale: Core product value: connects remote agents and workers without shared process memory.
capabilities.description: Bidirectional event bus between an MCP-driven orchestrator and a worker's session, enabling work delegation, prompt approval, and terminal observation.

features.name: tm_send
features.rationale: Enables remote agent execution from a single management session.
features.description: Allows an orchestrator agent to send commands and prompts to remote worker sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Fundamental job-to-be-done: sending work remotely.
behaviors.summary: Orchestrator sends a command payload that triggers execution in a specific worker session.
behaviors.detail: The client transmits a structured command object over the WebSocket connection. The server routes this payload to the target worker's event loop, which acknowledges receipt and begins execution.

features.name: Inbound Prompt Approval
features.rationale: Safeguards the fleet by allowing human-in-the-loop oversight of tool usage.
features.description: Mechanism for an orchestrator to review and approve/reject tool calls from worker sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Essential for security in untrusted or multi-agent environments.
behaviors.summary: Worker proposes a tool call; orchestrator receives a request and responds with a decision.
behaviors.detail: The worker session captures a tool invocation intent and pushes a pending request to the bus. The orchestrator reads this request and replies with 'approve', 'reject', or 'modify'. The worker then acts accordingly.

features.name: Terminal Observation
features.rationale: Provides visibility into worker execution context and debugging information.
features.description: Streams real-time terminal output from worker sessions to the orchestrator.

behaviors.rationale: Enables monitoring and debugging of remote worker processes.
behaviors.summary: Streams raw pty output from the worker to the orchestrator in real time.
behaviors.detail: The worker captures the output from its attached pseudo-terminal (PTY) and streams it as text events over the socket. The orchestrator renders this text as if it were a native terminal output.

features.name: tm_restart
features.rationale: Ensures workers remain responsive and resources are released when idle.
features.description: Controls the start, stop, and restart state of worker sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Allows dynamic scaling and cleanup of agent fleets.
behaviors.summary: Orchestrator sends a signal to start or stop the underlying worker process.
behaviors.detail: Commands like 'start', 'stop', or 'restart' are interpreted by the server logic. This action triggers the provisioning or termination of the background process and associated resources.

features.name: Permission Relay
features.rationale: Ensures only authorized orchestrators can control specific workers.
features.description: Manages security tokens and authentication required for agent-to-agent delegation.

behaviors.rationale: Critical security boundary for fleet management.
behaviors.summary: Validates incoming requests against a permission model before allowing access.
behaviors.detail: The transport validates the incoming bearer token or handshake payload against a configured allowlist. Access is granted only if the principal is mapped to the target worker.

behaviors.detail:

features.name: Channel Management
features.rationale: Maintains the underlying transport for multi-agent delegation.
features.description: Manages persistent connections and subscriptions between agents.

behaviors.rationale: Establishes the transport layer for agent communication.
behaviors.summary: Handles the subscription of a new agent to a communication channel.
behaviors.detail: The system creates or updates a channel connection, managing the lifecycle of the subscription and ensuring data flow.

capabilities.name: Worker Orchestration
capabilities.rationale: Essential functionality for managing worker lifecycle and execution states.
capabilities.description: Core tools to create, monitor, and control AI worker instances across a fleet.

features.name: Ticket Exchange
features.rationale: Enables secure, temporary access between agents without long-lived secrets.
features.description: Generates and manages short-lived credentials for secure agent delegation.

behaviors.rationale: Short-lived tokens reduce the impact of credential compromise.
behaviors.summary: Issues new bearer tokens with a configurable Time-To-Live (TTL) for delegation.
behaviors.detail: The system generates a cryptographically random token and associates it with the requesting worker. The token includes an expiration timestamp and is stored in memory. It is rate-limited per bearer token to prevent brute-force issuance.

behaviors.rationale: Limits the blast radius of a leaked operator token.
behaviors.summary: Rate-limits token issuance to prevent abuse by a compromised operator.
behaviors.detail: The system tracks how many tokens a bearer has issued within the last 60 seconds. If the limit is exceeded, further issuance requests are rejected until the window resets.

features.name: Agent Lifecycle
features.rationale: Direct control over agent instantiation and termination.
features.description: Provisions and manages the lifecycle of individual worker agents.

behaviors.rationale: Standardizes agent creation across different environments.
behaviors.summary: Starts a new Claude Code worker instance via secure delegation.
behaviors.detail: The orchestrator sends a start command which initializes a local Claude Code session, establishes necessary pty bridges, and registers the agent into the central bus for subsequent interaction and monitoring.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures resource efficiency and controlled termination.
behaviors.summary: Stops and cleans up active worker sessions.
behaviors.detail: Receives a termination signal and gracefully shuts down the underlying Claude Code session, revoking pty access and releasing system resources associated with that worker.

features.name: Command Relay
features.rationale: Centralized logic decouples user intent from worker execution.
features.description: Routes user commands to specific workers and aggregates results.

behaviors.rationale: Enables multi-host delegation without shared state.
behaviors.summary: Delegates commands from one host to another host's agents.
behaviors.detail: Captures an action request (e.g., code generation, file read) from an upstream agent or operator, validates permissions, and routes the payload to the target worker to execute the action.

features.name: Session Discovery
features.rationale: Operators need to see what workers are running and their connection health.
features.description: Enumerates all active worker sessions, grouping them by project context and showing online/offline status.

behaviors.rationale: Provides complete visibility into the worker fleet at a glance.
behaviors.summary: Lists all worker sessions with their current connection status and grouping information.
behaviors.detail: Returns a formatted table showing all workers with their project grouping, online status, and optional stale entries when requested. Ecosystem projects are always shown regardless of active workers.

features.name: Command Dispatch
features.rationale: Operators need to issue instructions and control commands remotely.
features.description: Sends commands, messages, or keystrokes to specific workers to interact with their sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Enables remote execution of tasks through command injection.
behaviors.summary: Dispatches a command string to a target worker session.
behaviors.detail: Takes a worker target and command payload, routing the input through the forwarder to the worker's pty process. Handles both direct commands and messages for the caller's own timeline.

behaviors.rationale: Provides fine-grained control for interactive terminal scenarios.
behaviors.summary: Routes keystrokes to a worker's terminal session.
behaviors.detail: Sends raw keystroke sequences to a worker's pty, enabling direct terminal interaction for scenarios requiring simulated user input.

behaviors.rationale: Enables task chaining without manual conversation cleanup.
behaviors.summary: Atomically clears worker conversation and dispatches new task.
behaviors.detail: Resets the worker's conversation context and immediately sends a new task payload, ensuring clean slate for new operations.

features.name: Meta Operations
features.rationale: Support operations for maintaining MCP server consistency and understanding system usage.
features.description: Provides auxiliary operations like refreshing tools and getting usage instructions for the system.

behaviors.rationale: Helps operators and agents understand system usage.
behaviors.summary: Returns system usage instructions and recommended workflows.
behaviors.detail: Provides documentation on how to use TubeMail's MCP tools, including best practices and workflow recommendations.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures tool registry is up to date.
behaviors.summary: Refreshes available tools in the MCP server.
behaviors.detail: Updates the tool registry in the MCP server to ensure the latest tools are available for discovery and use.

capabilities.name: Agent Fleet Orchestration
capabilities.rationale: Core control surface for managing agent fleets without imposing platform orchestration logic.
capabilities.description: Commands and manages AI agent workers, allowing operators to launch, stop, and monitor tasks across multiple hosts.

features.name: Task Submission
features.rationale: Delivers the core workload instructions to the fleet.
features.description: Sends messages and instructions to active worker agents.

behaviors.rationale: Primary method of directing agent behavior.
behaviors.summary: Delivers a message payload to a specific worker.
behaviors.detail: Given a worker is running, When the operator sends a message via the control bus, Then the worker receives the message and begins execution.

features.name: tm_status
features.rationale: Enables visibility into fleet utilization.
features.description: Determines the current operational status (busy, idle, or waiting) based on recent events.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures accurate status reflects actual recent activity.
behaviors.summary: Returns 'busy' if an inbound event occurred recently, 'idle' otherwise.
behaviors.detail: The system maintains an event log. If the most recent event was of kind 'inbound' and occurred within a configured decay threshold, the status is reported as 'busy'. If the elapsed time since the last inbound event exceeds the threshold (default 600 seconds), the status decays to 'idle'. If no inbound events have occurred, it defaults to 'idle'. The method accepts an optional timestamp parameter to support deterministic testing.

behaviors.rationale: Prioritizes administrative state over time-decay.
behaviors.summary: Returns 'waiting_permission' if the agent is pending approval.
behaviors.detail: The system checks pending permissions for the agent. If any permissions are currently pending, the status is immediately reported as 'waiting_permission', overriding the time-decay logic.

features.name: tm_stop
features.rationale: Provides essential lifecycle control for individual agent instances.
features.description: Executes commands to start, stop, screenshot, and clear the state of specific workers.

behaviors.rationale: Operators need to know which agents are available for assignment.
behaviors.summary: List available workers with status metadata.
behaviors.detail: Returns a list of registered workers including their names, online status, and permission state. Supports optional filtering and sorting by status or name.

behaviors.rationale: Allows remote agents to interact with the user environment on behalf of the operator.
behaviors.summary: Send input commands to a worker session.
behaviors.detail: Accepts a stream of text keystrokes or shell commands to execute on the worker. Supports optional parameters for behavior (allow/deny) and timeout.

behaviors.rationale: Bridges the local agent with the fleet controller for advanced capabilities.
behaviors.summary: Connect MCP tools to a worker session.
behaviors.detail: Establishes a persistent MCP connection to a specific worker, enabling rich tool invocation and state sharing.

features.name: Fleet Orchestration
features.rationale: Allows operators to view status and trigger actions on distributed workers.
features.description: Tools to monitor and control a fleet of Claude Code workers.

behaviors.rationale: Operators must verify worker availability before issuing commands.
behaviors.summary: Returns the operational status of a specific fleet or individual worker.
behaviors.detail: The system queries the internal state of the control bus to retrieve real-time metrics such as CPU usage, active context, and connection health for a requested resource identifier.

behaviors.rationale: Operators need immediate control to halt expensive or misbehaving agents.
behaviors.summary: Executes a management command on a specific worker.
behaviors.detail: The system translates the incoming command payload into an internal action that is dispatched to the target worker's process via the established secure transport channel.

behaviors.rationale: Provides the visual context for the entire agent fleet.
behaviors.summary: Renders the list of active workers.
behaviors.detail: The dashboard fetches the current list of registered workers from the backend and renders their status cards, updating automatically as states change.

behaviors.rationale: Provides immediate visual feedback on system state.
behaviors.summary: Renders a list of active workers with their current state.
behaviors.detail: The UI lists all connected agents, showing their ID, last activity time, and health status indicators.

behaviors.rationale: Maps backend data to UI lists.
behaviors.summary: The dashboard shows a list of active workers.
behaviors.detail: The UI requests worker status from Core MCP and renders the list of agents.

capabilities.name: Claude Code Channel
capabilities.rationale: Enables essential agent-to-agent delegation and event relaying.
capabilities.description: Provides the core bidirectional communication link between the Claude Code worker and the TubeMail hub via stdio.

features.name: Session Initialization
features.rationale: Establishes trust and protocol compatibility immediately.
features.description: Negotiates the connection and declares available experimental capabilities upon startup.

features.rationale: Keeps the fleet state synchronized and events flowing without blocking.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the worker always has the latest state from the central hub.

behaviors.detail: Upon receiving an initialized confirmation, the channel starts a background task that listens to the hub for updates and simultaneously reads from stdin, relaying messages back and forth.

features.name: Reply Tool
features.rationale: Enables agents to report progress, ask questions, or deliver results.
features.description: Allows the agent to send text messages back to the orchestrator with optional metadata.

behaviors.rationale: Provides a mechanism for human-in-the-loop feedback.

behaviors.detail: When invoked via tools/call, it sends the provided text and optional meta object to the hub, returning a success confirmation to the agent.

features.name: Acknowledgment Tool
features.rationale: Allows for quick, low-overhead confirmations.
features.description: Provides a lightweight way to acknowledge interrupts or inbound events without a full text payload.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces noise and bandwidth for simple confirmation events.
behaviors.summary: Sends a minimal ack signal to the hub.
behaviors.detail: When called with no arguments, it posts an outbound message kind 'ack' to the hub to signal receipt of a notification without generating a text response.

features.name: Ping Handler
features.rationale: Maintains liveness and allows health checks.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the orchestrator knows the worker is reachable.

behaviors.rationale: Supports security reviews and debugging.

features.name: State Machine

features.description: Backend logic tracking agent lifecycle states.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures data consistency between UI and backend.
behaviors.summary: Transitions agents between states like idle, busy, and error.
behaviors.detail: The manager process updates the state when events occur (e.g., job queued, task finished). The UI queries this state to update the roster.

behaviors.rationale: Remote orchestration.

behaviors.detail: MCP tools allow external agents to create, run, list, and delete flow templates, enabling complex orchestration.

features.description: Handles incoming requests for tool execution permissions.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents unauthorized tool calls on the local system.
behaviors.summary: Hub presents pending tool requests to the operator for decision.
behaviors.detail: When a worker requests access to a tool, the hub persists the request with a preview and description. The operator reviews the request and sends a response to allow or deny the action.

features.description: Handles tool permission prompts by surfacing pending requests and allowing remote approval/denial.

behaviors.detail: Accepts a permission request ID and action (approve/deny), updating the worker's authorization state.

features.name: List Permissions
features.rationale: Enables security operators to manage access control centrally.
features.description: Retrieves all pending permission requests across the active worker fleet.

behaviors.rationale: Critical for maintaining secure access control.
behaviors.summary: Returns pending permission requests.
behaviors.detail: The endpoint fetches permission requests, filtering out 'zombie' requests from crashed workers that can no longer respond. Only online workers are considered.

features.name: Permissions Empty State
features.rationale: Clarifies that a blank screen means the system is up to date.
features.description: Indicates when no permissions are pending approval on the permissions page.

behaviors.rationale: Provides reassurance that the system is functioning correctly.
behaviors.summary: Shows a clean 'All Caught Up' message when no permissions are pending.
behaviors.detail: If no tools request approval, the page displays a status message instead of a blank div. It informs the user that they can return later for new requests.

features.name: tm_pending_permissions
features.rationale: Prevents operators from being alerted by zombie permissions from dead agents.
features.description: Shows permissions awaiting human review, excluding those from crashed sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Filters out stale data from terminated sessions to avoid noise.
behaviors.summary: Counts pending permissions only for currently online workers.
behaviors.detail: When a worker disconnects without re-registering, any pending permission requests associated with it are discarded. The metric reflects only actionable items from active sessions.

capabilities.name: Agent Pty Bridge
capabilities.rationale: Core control bus for agent-to-agent delegation and human oversight.
capabilities.description: Secure WebSocket channel for bidirectional stream between browser and manager's pseudo-terminal instance.

features.name: Secure Stream Attachment
features.rationale: Prevents unauthorized hijacking of agent sessions.
features.description: Establishes a single-use, TTL-bounded secure connection to a specific worker's pseudo-terminal stream.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures session integrity and worker context.
behaviors.summary: Verifies client origin against allowlist and consumes valid ticket before accepting WebSocket connection.
behaviors.detail: The system validates the Origin header against an allowlist to prevent cross-tab hijacking. If valid, it consumes a single-use ticket scoped to the specific worker. If the ticket is invalid, expired, or missing, or if the origin is not allowed, the connection is refused immediately.

features.name: tm_keystroke
features.rationale: Allows human operators to interact directly with the agent environment.
features.description: Forwards binary keystrokes from the browser client to the manager's pseudo-terminal process.

behaviors.rationale: Enables direct manual intervention.
behaviors.summary: Relays binary keystroke data sent by the client to the manager's pseudo-terminal process.
behaviors.detail: The system receives binary frames from the client. These frames are treated as raw terminal input (keystrokes) and are forwarded to the manager. The manager then handles the input as if it were typed directly into its pseudo-terminal, enabling real-time control.

features.name: ping
features.rationale: Keeps the session state synchronized and responsive.
features.description: Exchanges control events (resize, ping, close) between the browser and the manager.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains session fidelity.
behaviors.summary: Sends text frames containing control events like resize or ping to the manager.
behaviors.detail: The client sends text frames with JSON control events. For example, a resize event includes column and row dimensions. The manager updates its pseudo-terminal size and triggers a redraw. Similarly, a ping event is sent to keep the connection alive, and a close event is sent when the session ends.

features.name: Stream Termination
features.rationale: Releases resources and cleans up the agent environment.
features.description: Gracefully closes the stream when the ticket expires or the manager signals closure.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents resource leaks.
behaviors.summary: Sends a text frame with a close reason before terminating the connection.
behaviors.detail: When the ticket expires or the manager decides to close the stream, it sends a text frame with a 'closed' kind and a reason. The browser closes the WebSocket connection upon receiving this sentinel. If the client disconnects unexpectedly, the server also closes the connection and notifies the manager.

features.name: PTY Bridge
features.rationale: Operators require direct keystroke-level access to execute commands.
features.description: Establishes secure, interactive terminal sessions between operators and workers.

behaviors.rationale: One-time use tokens prevent unauthorized re-connection if credentials leak.
behaviors.summary: Authenticates WebSocket connections via single-use tickets to establish pty sessions.
behaviors.detail: Upon connection, the server validates a bearer token or ticket. If valid and within TTL, the worker is linked to the session. Upon consumption, the ticket is invalidated to prevent replay attacks, and the session allows bidirectional data flow.

behaviors.rationale: Keystroke data must never traverse unencrypted networks.
behaviors.summary: Strictly enforces TLS-only and Origin whitelisting for pty traffic.
behaviors.detail: The server rejects any WebSocket upgrade requests over unencrypted HTTP or from origins not in the allowlist. If TLS is missing, the server returns a 426 Upgrade Required error with a JSON body explaining the policy.

behaviors.rationale: Automatic cleanup prevents resource exhaustion.
behaviors.summary: Automatically cleans up expired session tickets to prevent resource leaks.
behaviors.detail: A background task runs periodically to identify and remove tickets that have expired. This ensures memory usage remains bounded and prevents denial of service via ticket accumulation.

behaviors.rationale: Replaces the need for separate window management.
behaviors.summary: Streams output from the agent process to the browser xterm.js pane.
behaviors.detail: The system captures stdout/stderr from the manager's Pty and pipes them into the UI buffer with low latency. Resizing the window updates the underlying process dimensions to maintain formatting integrity.

behaviors.rationale: Enables direct command execution via the web interface.
behaviors.summary: Accepts keyboard input and handles copy/paste operations.
behaviors.detail: Keystrokes sent via the WebSocket bridge are written to the process input buffer. Paste operations invoke the bracketed paste capability of the Ink TUI renderer if available, or fall back to raw byte streaming.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the UI is the primary interaction point for the operator.
behaviors.summary: Transmits user input to the backend process and streams output back to the UI in real-time.
behaviors.detail: The system establishes a bidirectional stream where keystrokes typed in the web terminal are forwarded to the running process, and STDOUT/STDERR from that process is rendered in the UI. This ensures the web UI is the operator's primary interaction surface for at least 3 of the 5 most-used workers by end of dogfood week 2.

behaviors.rationale: Securely identifies the session before allowing process access.
behaviors.summary: Opens a bidirectional stream to the worker's pseudo-terminal using an exchange ticket.
behaviors.detail: Given a valid exchange ticket, When the client connects via the WebSocket URL, Then multiplex read, write, and resize operations on that socket.

behaviors.rationale: Initiates the core communication channel for command delegation.
behaviors.summary: Establishes a persistent connection between the browser terminal and the worker process.
behaviors.detail: The system initializes a WebSocket connection to the worker endpoint. It streams standard input/output lines and manages the pseudo-terminal allocation for the remote process. The connection state is monitored to detect disconnection events for the UI banner.

behaviors.rationale: Handles transient network failures to maintain worker availability.
behaviors.summary: Restores connection to a worker when the underlying bridge disconnects.
behaviors.detail: When the WebSocket connection drops (e.g., network interruption), the UI displays a disconnected banner with a single reconnect button. Upon clicking this button, the system attempts to re-establish the bridge to the same worker instance.

behaviors.rationale: Respects mobile UX constraints to prevent bad typing experiences.
behaviors.summary: Prevents local input on small screens where keyboard usage is poor UX.
behaviors.detail: On mobile devices (screens < 768px), the terminal pane is locked in read-only mode. The system prevents local typing and displays a banner instructing the user to open the tool on a desktop for full access.

behaviors.rationale: Provides immediate feedback on interface state changes.
behaviors.summary: Displays font size status immediately after zoom adjustment.
behaviors.detail: When the user changes the terminal font size using keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+=/Ctrl+-), a small indicator appears in the bottom-right corner showing the current size. This indicator persists for 1 second before auto-hiding.

capabilities.name: Worker Lifecycle
capabilities.rationale: Allows operators to maintain a healthy, dynamic fleet of agents.
capabilities.description: Handles registration, updates, and permanent removal of agent workers from the system.

features.name: Purge Worker
features.rationale: Allows cleanup of orphaned or decommissioned agent slots.
features.description: Permanently removes a worker's entry from the system registry.

behaviors.rationale: Essential for managing fleet resources effectively.
behaviors.summary: Deletes a worker from the registry.
behaviors.detail: The endpoint validates the worker name and removes the associated registry entry. This action is permanent and cannot be undone within the session.

features.name: State Decoding
features.rationale: Distinguishes between active processing, idle, and crashed states.
features.description: Interprets raw process activity signals to determine worker status.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the roster remains accurate even if the manager disconnects.
behaviors.summary: Hub determines worker state by evaluating authority signals against event timelines.
behaviors.detail: The hub prioritizes authoritative signals from the manager (observed_active). If the manager is stale, it falls back to analyzing event timelines and activity decay thresholds to determine if the worker is busy or idle.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents false-positive crash alerts for normal terminations.
behaviors.summary: Hub handles workers that exited cleanly versus those that crashed.
behaviors.detail: The hub tracks if a worker closed its connection gracefully. It distinguishes between a clean shutdown and a crash, updating the exit state accordingly to inform the user.

features.name: Context Monitoring
features.rationale: Provides visibility into model context limits and memory usage.
features.description: Tracks the context window usage percentage for connected workers.

behaviors.rationale: Alerts operators to approaching context limits.
behaviors.summary: Hub tracks context window usage percentage from the worker's TUI.
behaviors.detail: The manager pushes updates to the hub whenever the context percentage changes. The hub persists this value and displays it in the UI, rendering a placeholder if the worker lacks support for this metric.

features.name: Worker Lifecycle Management
features.rationale: Enables operators to control worker instances dynamically.
features.description: Starts, stops, and restarts AI agent workers on specific hosts.

behaviors.rationale: Fundamental requirement to execute AI tasks.
behaviors.summary: Initiates a worker process and establishes a connection for monitoring.
behaviors.detail: Given the operator sends a request to start a worker, When the system receives the command, Then the worker process launches and reports its readiness status.

behaviors.rationale: Provides diagnostic information for fleet management.
behaviors.summary: Gets the current state and health information for a worker.
behaviors.detail: Returns detailed status including process health stats, online state, and manager connection status for a specific worker.

behaviors.rationale: Enables emergency stop and task cancellation.
behaviors.summary: Sends interrupt signal to stop current worker activity.
behaviors.detail: Dispatches an interrupt event to halt ongoing work in the worker's session, allowing graceful or forced termination of operations.

behaviors.rationale: Recovers from hung or stuck worker states.
behaviors.summary: Force restarts a worker's Claude process through its manager.
behaviors.detail: Re-executes the worker's manager Python process to restart the Claude instance, clearing any hung states or memory issues.

behaviors.rationale: Allows immediate cleanup of problematic workers.
behaviors.summary: Force-stops a worker and terminates its manager process entirely.
behaviors.detail: Completely terminates both the worker process and its associated manager process, removing the worker from the registry.

behaviors.rationale: Enables cleanup of terminated workers.
behaviors.summary: Permanently removes a worker from the system registry.
behaviors.detail: Delegates to the stop function to completely remove a worker from the registry after confirming permanent deletion.

behaviors.rationale: Self-healing capability for connection issues.
behaviors.summary: Reconnects a failed MCP server on a worker automatically.
behaviors.detail: Attempts to re-establish MCP server connections on a worker that experienced connection failures without requiring manual intervention.

behaviors.rationale: Provides visual monitoring of worker sessions.
behaviors.summary: Captures screenshot of worker's terminal display.
behaviors.detail: Takes a visual snapshot of the worker's current terminal screen state for monitoring and debugging purposes.

behaviors.rationale: Enables audit and debugging through output capture.
behaviors.summary: Toggles recording of pty output for a worker session.
behaviors.detail: Enables or disables recording of terminal output for a specific worker, with options to filter and retrieve recorded frames later.

behaviors.rationale: Enables audit trail and debugging through recorded output.
behaviors.summary: Retrieves recorded terminal output frames filtered by criteria.
behaviors.detail: Returns recorded text frames from a worker's pty output, with support for time range and regex filtering.

behaviors.rationale: Enables hot-reloading of code and configuration.
behaviors.summary: Updates worker's manager to pick up source changes.
behaviors.detail: Re-executes the worker's manager Python process to reload updated source code and configuration changes.

behaviors.rationale: Enables the first connection event of a worker agent.
behaviors.summary: Registers a new worker with a specified command working directory and forwarder version.
behaviors.detail: The worker must be registered via a POST request to /tubemail/<worker>/register with a valid Bearer token. The system validates the worker name against a whitelist pattern allowing alphanumeric characters and basic symbols. Upon successful registration, the system returns a unique cursor representing the initial position in the event stream for that worker. The worker name must not contain double dots (..) to prevent path traversal attacks.

behaviors.rationale: Cleans up resources for agents that terminate unexpectedly.
behaviors.summary: Deregisters an active worker from the bus.
behaviors.detail: An active worker is removed from the system state by sending a POST request to /tubemail/<worker>/unregister. This endpoint stops the system from pushing new events to this worker and cleans up its state. The worker name is validated to ensure it matches the expected format and does not contain path traversal characters.

capabilities.name: Worker Monitoring
capabilities.rationale: Enables operators to see if workers are active, idle, or offline.
capabilities.description: Core MCP tools for real-time visibility into worker health and status.

features.name: Online/Offline Indicator
features.rationale: Instantly tells users if a node is reachable.
features.description: Displays whether a worker is connected to the control bus or disconnected.

behaviors.rationale: Differentiates crash from clean shutdown for accurate diagnostics.
behaviors.summary: Distinguishes between network-outage offline and graceful-exit offline.
behaviors.detail: The badge displays different icons and labels depending on the worker's connection state. If a worker has not reported in within a timeout, it is marked offline. If a worker previously reported in but subsequently exited the loop cleanly, it is marked as exited cleanly rather than just offline.

behaviors.rationale: Reflects the operational state of the running agent.
behaviors.summary: Shows worker status for connected nodes.
behaviors.detail: When a worker is connected and running, the badge reflects its current logical state. The badge updates to show 'idle' when the worker is ready for tasks, 'busy' when executing a task, or 'waiting' when blocked.

behaviors.rationale: Signals to operators that the worker is blocked, not broken.
behaviors.summary: Displays waiting status for permission requests.
behaviors.detail: If a worker is waiting for permission to execute a task, the badge specifically indicates 'waiting' and shows an alert icon.

behaviors.rationale: Allows operators to estimate how long a task has been running.
behaviors.summary: Shows busy status with elapsed time counter.
behaviors.detail: When a worker is busy, the badge displays the label 'busy' and includes a timer showing how long the worker has been active.

features.name: Time Duration Formatter
features.rationale: Provides human-readable time units like minutes or hours.
features.description: Calculates and formats the duration a worker has been in the 'busy' state.

behaviors.rationale: Human-readable time prevents confusion over raw timestamps.
behaviors.summary: Formats duration into seconds, minutes, or hours.
behaviors.detail: The system calculates the elapsed time since the worker last reported in. If the duration is less than a minute, it shows seconds. If under an hour, it shows minutes and seconds. For longer durations, it formats hours and minutes.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents negative time values from appearing on screen.
behaviors.summary: Handles edge cases in time calculation.
behaviors.detail: If the calculated duration is negative (clock reset or error), the system defaults to showing 0 seconds to avoid misleading displays.

features.name: Visual Icon Indicator
features.rationale: Visual cues are faster to interpret than text alone.
features.description: Uses distinct icons to represent each worker state for quick visual scanning.

behaviors.rationale: Standard icons are intuitive and recognizable.
behaviors.summary: Assigns specific icons to each worker state.
behaviors.detail: An idle worker shows a checkmark. A busy worker shows a spinning loader. A waiting worker shows an alert shield. Offline workers show an X or dashed circle.

behaviors.rationale: Dashed line visually implies a graceful transition.
behaviors.summary: Uses dashed circle for clean exits.
behaviors.detail: When a worker exited cleanly, a dashed circle icon is shown to visually distinguish it from a hard disconnect.

capabilities.name: Live Worker Metrics

features.name: Worker Online Status

features.description: Displays the exact count of workers currently subscribed to the hub.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures metric reflects only live operational state.
behaviors.summary: Returns count of workers with active SSE subscriptions only.
behaviors.detail: The system reads only workers where a subscription is active. It excludes workers listed in disk state files that have since disconnected, ensuring the count reflects real-time availability.

features.name: Metrics
features.rationale: Provides quantitative data to assess system health and identify bottlenecks.
features.description: Tracks system performance metrics and error rates.

behaviors.rationale: Critical for identifying performance issues and system health.
behaviors.summary: Tracks metrics such as attached bridges, fan-out events, and latency.
behaviors.detail: The system emits metrics for the number of attached bridges, total events fanned out, and latency measurements. These metrics are stored in a time-series database for analysis and visualization.

capabilities.name: MCP Tooling
capabilities.rationale: Enables multi-agent delegation without platform-imposed logic.
capabilities.description: Core and auxiliary tools for agent management, orchestration, and performance monitoring.

features.name: Auxiliary Orchestration
features.rationale: Supports extended use cases without affecting core stability.
features.description: Advanced tools for detailed configuration and external agent interaction.

behaviors.rationale: Allows cross-agent communication and delegation.
behaviors.summary: Handles incoming requests from external agents.
behaviors.detail: When an external agent sends a request, the system processes it via auxiliary tools and returns the result to the caller.

features.name: Core Tools
features.rationale: Must-be functionality for the system to function correctly.
features.description: Essential functionality for managing local Claude Code workers.

behaviors.rationale: Allows clients to dynamically discover available capabilities.
behaviors.summary: Returns available tool definitions from the current agent instance.
behaviors.detail: The system returns a list of JSON-RPC tool schemas available to the client. This list reflects the currently running tools in the instance.

behaviors.rationale: Enables the primary function of interacting with managed agents.
behaviors.summary: Executes a specific tool call with provided arguments.
behaviors.detail: The system invokes the named tool with the provided arguments and returns the result of the execution.

features.name: Auxiliary Tools

behaviors.rationale: Helps operators monitor fleet health and troubleshoot issues.
behaviors.summary: Retrieves the status of a specific worker or channel.
behaviors.detail: The system returns detailed status information about a requested worker or channel, including health and recent activity.

capabilities.name: Orchestration Hub

capabilities.description: Core tool routing and permission relay enabling agents to send, receive, and list workers across sessions.

features.name: Worker Routing
features.rationale: Enables cross-session job dispatching.
features.description: Routes incoming tasks between orchestrator and worker sessions via the tubemail channel.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures tasks reach the correct worker instance.
behaviors.summary: Forwards tasks from the orchestrator to specific worker sessions over the TCP channel.
behaviors.detail: The system accepts a task description and destination worker ID from an orchestrator session, establishes or reuses an existing connection on the designated port, and injects the payload into the target worker's event loop.

behaviors.rationale: Allows many agents on one network interface.
behaviors.summary: Manages connections to worker sessions on the same port.
behaviors.detail: The system maintains a single TCP listener on the configured port, multiplexing multiple agent-to-agent communication streams, and distinguishes flows by the channel or session ID in the payload headers.

features.name: Permission Relay
features.rationale: Validates and propagates authorization context.
features.description: Relays capability grants and token assertions between the orchestrator and worker sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures workers act only on authorized requests.
behaviors.summary: Re-issues access tokens to workers after orchestrator validation.
behaviors.detail: When the orchestrator validates a user or agent identity, the hub generates a new access token for that identity and forwards it to the specific worker session, ensuring workers only execute tasks authorized by the orchestrator.

features.name: Worker Discovery
features.rationale: Allows agents to know which workers are ready.
features.description: Maintains a registry of active local worker sessions available for delegation.

behaviors.rationale: Enables intelligent load distribution.
behaviors.summary: Lists all currently active worker sessions reachable via the hub.
behaviors.detail: An orchestrator can request a list of active workers. The hub queries its internal connection pool and returns the identifiers and current status (active/idle/busy) for each registered worker session.

capabilities.name: Permission Handling
capabilities.rationale: Enforces granular control over what agents can do.
capabilities.description: Manages requests for tool execution permissions and allows operators to grant or deny access.

features.name: Permission Requests
features.rationale: Allows operators to review and approve agent actions before they occur.
features.description: Displays pending permission requests from agents attempting to use new tools.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents unauthorized tool execution by default.
behaviors.summary: Lists all pending permission requests awaiting operator decision.
behaviors.detail: The response contains a list of requests specifying the worker, tool name, and request context.

features.name: Permission Decisions
features.rationale: Grants or revokes agent capabilities based on operator judgment.
features.description: Processes operator actions to allow or deny specific tool requests.

behaviors.rationale: Dynamic control over agent capabilities.

behaviors.detail: Upon submission of a decision, the system resolves the specific request and updates the agent's capability set.

features.name: Permission Handling
features.rationale: Enables secure execution of privileged actions requiring approval.
features.description: Handles requests for human or automated permissions and records resolution actions.

behaviors.rationale: Triggers the approval workflow for privileged operations.
behaviors.summary: Records a permission request from a worker requiring approval.
behaviors.detail: A worker requests permission (e.g., to delete a file) by posting to /tubemail/<worker>/permission-request. The system validates the token, generates an event ID, and makes the request visible to operators. The worker can then wait for a signal before proceeding.

behaviors.rationale: Closes the loop on security-critical authorization decisions.
behaviors.summary: Records a locally-resolved permission response to a request.
behaviors.detail: After a human operator or hook approves/denies a request, the worker posts the resolution to /tubemail/<worker>/permission-response. The system validates the request ID, records the behavior (allowed/denied), and updates the request state accordingly.

behaviors.rationale: Provides accurate status reporting for operator dashboards.
behaviors.summary: Records a clean shutdown signal from a worker.
behaviors.detail: When a user types 'exit' or the process dies cleanly, the worker posts to /tubemail/<worker>/goodbye. This distinguishes clean exits from crashes, ensuring the operator UI can display the worker as 'exited cleanly' rather than 'crashed' or 'unknown'.

behaviors.rationale: Resolve delegation requests.
behaviors.summary: Displays pending permissions list.
behaviors.detail: The inbox shows a cross-worker list of pending permission requests. Users can view requests grouped by the requesting worker. Bulk actions like allow or deny are supported as one-shot operations rather than persistent rules.

capabilities.name: Stdio Transport
capabilities.rationale: Enables robust out-of-process communication without external SDK dependencies.
capabilities.description: Manages line-delimited JSON-RPC messages over stdin/stdout with a serialized write queue to prevent interleaved bytes.

features.name: Handler Registration
features.rationale: Decouples wire format logic from agent business logic for full control.
features.description: Registers request and notification handlers for specific methods and provides fallbacks for unknown methods.

behaviors.rationale: Enables pluggable logic for specific protocol actions.
behaviors.summary: Registers a handler for a specific JSON-RPC method name.
behaviors.detail: Stores the provided asynchronous callback function in a dictionary keyed by the method name, allowing the transport to route incoming messages to the correct business logic without relying on third-party SDKs.

behaviors.rationale: Provides a safety net for future protocol extensions.
behaviors.summary: Registers a handler for an unknown JSON-RPC method.
behaviors.detail: Stores the provided asynchronous callback function to be invoked when the transport encounters a method that has not been explicitly registered with on_request.

features.name: Asynchronous Sending
features.rationale: Ensures data integrity on line-delimited streams regardless of write concurrency.
features.description: Serializes messages and writes them to the output stream using an async lock to prevent concurrent calls from interleaving data.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents race conditions on multi-threaded or concurrent senders.
behaviors.summary: Sends a JSON-RPC message to the stdout stream safely.
behaviors.detail: Encodes the dictionary message into a compact UTF-8 string, acquires an exclusive write lock, writes the bytes to the buffer, and flushes to ensure the data is physically sent before returning.

behaviors.rationale: Allows testing without actual standard output streams.
behaviors.summary: Handles injected test writers in non-production environments.
behaviors.detail: Checks for a write/drain method on the writer object; if present, it invokes the write method and awaits the drain result to flush the buffer before returning.

features.name: Response Handling
features.rationale: Standardizes protocol responses for consistent agent-server communication.
features.description: Constructs and sends JSON-RPC 2.0 response objects with results or errors, including error code and data fields.

behaviors.rationale: Confirms successful execution to the client.
behaviors.summary: Sends a successful JSON-RPC 2.0 response.
behaviors.detail: Creates a response object with jsonrpc version and request ID, sets the result to the provided value or an empty object, and writes it to the output stream.

behaviors.rationale: Standardizes error reporting per JSON-RPC 2.0 spec.
behaviors.summary: Sends an error response for a specific JsonRpcError.
behaviors.detail: Creates a response object with jsonrpc version and request ID, sets the error property to a dictionary containing code and message, and optionally includes data.

capabilities.name: Worker State Classification
capabilities.rationale: Enables users to know exactly when their agents are available for new tasks.
capabilities.description: Determines if a worker agent is busy processing work or idle.

features.name: Active Signal Detection
features.rationale: Eliminates false positives where an agent appears busy after finishing a silent task.
features.description: Monitors the agent's terminal to detect if it is actively processing tokens or in tool calls.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures immediate visibility of ongoing work regardless of event history.
behaviors.summary: The system marks a worker as busy only when the terminal shows active processing activity.
behaviors.detail: The backend inspects the agent's terminal output (TUI) to detect spinner labels and running timers. If the manager detects active processing, it immediately notifies the hub to update the worker's state to busy. This takes precedence over event-based decay timers to ensure real-time accuracy.

behaviors.rationale: Corrects false 'busy' states caused by the lack of immediate completion signals.
behaviors.summary: The system marks a worker as idle after detecting a period of silence from the terminal.
behaviors.detail: The backend monitors the last timestamp when the manager detected active processing. If no new activity signal is received for a configurable duration (freshness threshold), the system considers the agent idle. This handles cases where the agent finishes a task silently without emitting specific completion events.

features.name: Event-Based Decay Fallback
features.rationale: Maintains functionality for legacy agents or cases where the manager signal is lost.
features.description: Uses event timestamps to estimate worker state when direct terminal signals are unavailable.

behaviors.rationale: Provides a safe default behavior that prevents premature idling of agents.
behaviors.summary: The system marks a worker as busy if the most recent inbound event is recent and no older inbound event is visible.
behaviors.detail: If the manager signal is unavailable or silent for longer than the freshness threshold, the system falls back to analyzing event timestamps. If the most recent inbound event occurred within the decay window (e.g., 10 minutes), the worker is marked busy. Once this window passes, the worker is considered idle.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures accurate representation of agents that have no pending or recent work.
behaviors.summary: The system considers an agent idle if there are no inbound events within the decay window.
behaviors.detail: If no inbound events have occurred recently (older than the decay window), or if the trailing event is not an inbound, the worker is immediately considered idle. This prevents agents from being stuck in a 'busy' state indefinitely when they are simply not being assigned new work.

behaviors.detail: The worker sends a POST request to the register endpoint. The payload includes the working directory (cwd), process ID (pid), and the forwarder version string extracted from the package. The hub validates the input and returns a success confirmation to the worker.

features.name: Worker Registration
features.rationale: Creates the entry point for tracking agent activity.
features.description: Allows a new worker process to announce itself to the control bus.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the worker is trackable immediately.
behaviors.summary: Accepts and persists new worker state on registration.
behaviors.detail: When a worker registers, the engine stores its state in memory and creates a corresponding JSON file on the configured data directory path.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents path traversal and naming ambiguities.
behaviors.summary: Enforces strict naming conventions for workers.
behaviors.detail: The engine rejects any registration attempt where the worker name contains 'l', 'o', or '..' sequences, raising an error.

behaviors.rationale: Guards against directory escape attacks via path injection.
behaviors.summary: Validates worker names to prevent directory escape attacks during registration.
behaviors.detail: The system accepts a request to register a worker and validates the provided name against a strict alphanumeric pattern, rejecting any path traversal sequences like '..'. If valid, a state file is written to the isolated workers directory. If invalid, the operation fails with a 400 error.

behaviors.rationale: Creates the entry point for tracking a new local agent.
behaviors.summary: Hub accepts a registration request and assigns a unique identifier to the worker.
behaviors.detail: The hub registers a new worker using the provided working directory and process ID. It validates the forwarder version and stores the initial state in the worker's persistent state record, including a cursor for event streaming.

capabilities.name: API Integration
capabilities.rationale: Provides the raw data needed to display worker states.
capabilities.description: Interface to retrieve worker data from the control bus.

features.name: Worker Data Retrieval
features.rationale: Supplies the necessary props for badge rendering.
features.description: Fetches worker state, online status, and exit status from the hub.

behaviors.rationale: All needed state bits are included in the response.
behaviors.summary: Returns complete worker state object.
behaviors.detail: The API call returns a data object containing the worker's current state, online flag, and clean-exit status.

behaviors.rationale: Timestamps enable duration calculation in the UI.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents connection dropouts during normal restart cycles.
behaviors.summary: Maintains an SSE subscription that persists through agent restarts.
behaviors.detail: When the process exits and restarts, the manager maintains its connection to the hub using an SSE subscription tied to the session ID.

capabilities.name: State Persistence
capabilities.rationale: Prevents path traversal attacks and ensures state integrity for operator trust.
capabilities.description: Securely manages worker state files on disk with strict validation to prevent unauthorized writes and state corruption.

features.name: State Loading
features.rationale: Handles filesystem changes safely without crashing on unexpected files.
features.description: Reads all files from the workers directory into memory and validates their format.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents application crashes from malformed state files on disk.
behaviors.summary: Safely loads state from disk while ignoring invalid or suspicious files.
behaviors.detail: The system reads every JSON file in the workers directory. It silently skips files that fail schema validation or parsing. Crucially, it ignores any file that does not match the allowed naming convention, even if it exists on disk.

behaviors.rationale: Mitigates path traversal risks by rejecting files in unauthorized locations.
behaviors.summary: Ignores files with suspicious names to block unauthorized state injection.
behaviors.detail: The system validates the filename of every file found in the workers directory. If a file is found with a name containing slashes or dots that violate the strict naming policy, it is ignored immediately.

capabilities.name: Worker Monitor

capabilities.description: Lists and inspects live status of connected AI workers.

features.name: tm_list_workers

features.description: Fetches current roster of active and idle workers.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the dashboard reflects the live fleet.
behaviors.summary: Loads and refreshes the list of available workers.
behaviors.detail: The system queries the MCP server to retrieve a list of all registered workers. On mount or SSE event, it updates the display to show current status, name, and health.

capabilities.name: Worker Teardown
capabilities.rationale: Prevents zombie entries in the agent fleet roster.
capabilities.description: Notifies the hub to remove a worker from the roster upon shutdown.

features.name: Worker Unregister
features.rationale: Maintains roster hygiene when agents terminate.
features.description: Sends an unregister signal to clean up the worker entry.

behaviors.rationale: Allows best-effort cleanup without blocking shutdown.
behaviors.summary: Hub processes unregister request and removes worker entry.
behaviors.detail: The worker sends a POST request to the unregister endpoint. The hub attempts to remove the corresponding worker entry from its state. If the entry is already gone, the hub handles the error gracefully without interrupting the worker shutdown process.
