features.rationale: Initiates the access control workflow for new agent actions.
features.description: Submits a tool permission request to the hub for approval.

behaviors.rationale: Tracks pending access requests centrally.
behaviors.summary: Hub receives and acknowledges a permission request with a unique ID.
behaviors.detail: The worker sends a POST request to the permission-request endpoint. The payload includes a unique request ID, the target tool name, a human-readable description, and a preview of the input. The hub validates the input and assigns a request ID, returning a success response to the worker.

behaviors.rationale: Finalizes access control decisions.
behaviors.summary: Hub processes permission response and updates agent's access status.
behaviors.detail: The worker sends a POST request to the permission-response endpoint. The payload contains the request ID and the behavior string representing the decision (e.g., allow or deny). The hub updates the agent's authorization state and logs the decision pattern for future auto-approval heuristics.

capabilities.name: Flow Definition
capabilities.rationale: Simplifies repetitive agent management tasks.
capabilities.description: Allows saving and re-running sequences of worker commands.

features.name: Flow Storage
features.rationale: Enables creation of reusable automation templates.
features.description: Persists a list of commands and their targets.

behaviors.rationale: Enables reuse of complex command sequences.
behaviors.summary: Saves a set of commands and configuration to storage.
behaviors.detail: Given a user creates a flow with a list of steps, When the user saves the flow, Then the system stores the steps with metadata.

behaviors.rationale: Fundamental requirement for user-defined automation tasks.
behaviors.summary: Allows users to save a flow configuration, list available flows, and trigger execution of specific runs.
behaviors.detail: Users can invoke MCP tools to persist a flow definition to a JSON store, list all stored flows with their metadata, and initiate a run which generates a unique execution token and status log. The system validates the flow syntax before persistence to prevent corrupted state.

behaviors.rationale: Critical for debugging and monitoring asynchronous agent tasks.
behaviors.summary: Retrieves the detailed execution log for a specific flow run.
behaviors.detail: When a flow execution is requested, the system aggregates output events from the manager node and returns a consolidated stream to the client, allowing the user to monitor progress and errors in real-time without polling.

behaviors.rationale: Operators need to track workflow execution history and select specific flows to edit or run.
behaviors.summary: Displays a list of saved flows with last-run metadata and status indicators.
behaviors.detail: The flow list displays each saved workflow's name, the assigned target worker, and the timestamp of the last execution. Each row shows a status indicator (e.g., last run time) and allows selection to load the flow into the editor.

behaviors.rationale: Correctly assigning active workers ensures flows execute on capable infrastructure.
behaviors.summary: Selects a target worker for a specific flow.
behaviors.detail: Each flow entry includes a dropdown to assign or change the target worker. This component reuses the roster row's state-badge to visually indicate if the selected worker is idle or busy before execution.

behaviors.rationale: Operators need to initialize new automation tasks from the management view.
behaviors.summary: Creates a new flow from scratch.
behaviors.detail: A [+ New Flow] button allows the creation of a new workflow definition within the list interface.

behaviors.rationale: Execute pre-defined automation.
behaviors.summary: Runs saved flows from UI.
behaviors.detail: Users can select a saved flow template and trigger it from the interface. The system logs the run and makes logs available for inspection after completion.

features.name: Flow Creation
features.rationale: Allows setup of pre-defined agent routines.
features.description: Defines and registers new workflow definitions.

behaviors.rationale: Matches /api/flows POST contract.
behaviors.summary: Persists a new flow definition to the store.
behaviors.detail: Validates name and stores the flow for later execution.

behaviors.rationale: Stores reusable automation logic.
behaviors.summary: Saves a new flow definition to the system.
behaviors.detail: The operator provides a name and body for the flow, which is persisted with a default worker assignment.

features.name: Flow Tracking
features.rationale: Allows debugging and auditing of automated jobs.
features.description: Retrieves the detailed log of a specific flow execution run.

behaviors.rationale: Provides audit trail for automation outcomes.
behaviors.summary: Retrieves the detailed log of a specific flow execution run.
behaviors.detail: The response includes the full event timeline, timestamps, and content changes for a specific run ID.

features.name: Flow Registration
features.rationale: Defines reusable workflow templates.
features.description: Registers new flow definitions for orchestrator consumption.

behaviors.rationale: Enables persistent workflow templates.
behaviors.summary: Registers a new flow in the flow store.
behaviors.detail: Accepts a flow definition and adds it to the FlowStore for use in future orchestration.

features.name: Flow Status
features.rationale: Provides visibility into ongoing workflows.
features.description: Returns the current status of a running flow.

behaviors.rationale: Monitors flow execution progress.
behaviors.summary: Returns status of a flow execution.
behaviors.detail: Accepts a flow id and returns current execution state and progress.

features.name: tm_save_flow
features.rationale: Allows defining reusable work-order templates persistently.
features.description: Stores a named template of outbound messages and metadata for later execution.

behaviors.rationale: Successful persistence of a new template.
behaviors.summary: Saves a flow template with optional defaults and metadata.
behaviors.detail: The system persists a named work-order template, storing the message body, an optional default worker assignment, and metadata dictionary. If the name already exists, an error is returned.

behaviors.rationale: Associating a default target for convenience.
behaviors.summary: Saves a flow with a default worker assignment.
behaviors.detail: The system stores the flow template and associates it with a specific worker ID as the default target for executions. This default can be overridden at runtime.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents accidental overwrites without explicit handling.
behaviors.summary: Fails to save due to duplicate name.
behaviors.detail: When the provided name already exists in the store, the operation fails with a ValueError containing a descriptive message.

behaviors.rationale: Allows cleanup without losing audit history.
behaviors.summary: Deletes a flow template and preserves its history.
behaviors.detail: The system removes the named flow template from the store. However, all event logs from past runs of this flow are preserved.

behaviors.rationale: Handles invalid references gracefully.
behaviors.summary: Fails when flow does not exist.
behaviors.detail: If the provided flow name is not found, the system returns an error indicating the flow was not found.

features.name: tm_list_flows
features.rationale: Provides visibility into available work-order templates.
features.description: Retrieves a summary list of all saved flow templates.

behaviors.rationale: Enables discovery of available templates.
behaviors.summary: Lists all flows with summaries and metadata.
behaviors.detail: The system returns a list of all saved flows, displaying the name, a truncated preview of the message body, the default worker (if set), and timestamps for creation, update, and last run.

behaviors.rationale: Correctly handles the 'no items' state.
behaviors.summary: Handles empty flow store gracefully.
behaviors.detail: If no flows have been saved, the system returns an empty list without error.

features.name: Run Flow
features.rationale: Triggers the orchestration of a pre-defined task.
features.description: Executes a saved flow template against a specified or default worker.

behaviors.rationale: Allows targeted execution of templates.
behaviors.summary: Executes a flow against a specified worker.
behaviors.detail: The system queues the flow body to the specified worker, overriding any default assignment. It returns a run_id for tracking and the ID of the first event created.

behaviors.rationale: Enables 'fire and forget' execution where appropriate.
behaviors.summary: Executes a flow using the default worker.
behaviors.detail: If no worker is provided, the system looks up the default_worker associated with the flow and executes the flow against that worker.

behaviors.rationale: Enforces requirement for a valid target.
behaviors.summary: Fails when no worker is available.
behaviors.detail: If the flow has no default and no worker is specified, the system returns an error stating that a target worker must be set.

behaviors.rationale: Handles invalid references gracefully.
behaviors.summary: Fails when flow does not exist.
behaviors.detail: If the provided flow name is not found in the store, the operation fails immediately with a not-found error.

behaviors.rationale: Enables task initiation.
behaviors.summary: Triggers tm_run_flow from UI selection.
behaviors.detail: When a user selects a flow and a worker (or relies on default) and clicks run, the UI calls tm_run_flow.

features.name: tm_get_run_log
features.rationale: Allows operators to inspect execution results and agent interactions.
features.description: Retrieves the real-time event timeline for a specific flow run.

behaviors.rationale: Provides visibility into the completed task outcome.
behaviors.summary: Returns the event log for a completed run.
behaviors.detail: The system retrieves all events associated with the run_id, including outbound replies and permission prompts. Events are lazy-populated from the worker's state up to the current time.

behaviors.rationale: Allows monitoring of in-progress tasks.
behaviors.summary: Returns active run log with partial events.
behaviors.detail: If the run is not yet marked as finished, the log contains events from the start up to the last received event, omitting the finished_at field.

behaviors.rationale: Handles invalid references gracefully.
behaviors.summary: Handles missing run_id gracefully.
behaviors.detail: If the run_id provided does not exist in the store, the system returns an error indicating the run was not found.

behaviors.rationale: Enables inspection of task outcomes.
behaviors.summary: Renders event log from tm_get_run_log.
behaviors.detail: The UI calls tm_get_run_log with a run_id and displays the list of events in a timeline view.

features.name: tm_finish_run
features.rationale: Allows operators to explicitly close long-running or paused tasks.
features.description: Manually marks a flow run as finished to stop further log updates.

behaviors.rationale: Explicitly terminates the log collection.
behaviors.summary: Marks a run as finished.
behaviors.detail: The system updates the run's state to finished, timestamping the completion. Future calls to get_run_log will stop appending events.

behaviors.rationale: Handles invalid references gracefully.
behaviors.summary: Handles missing run_id gracefully.
behaviors.detail: If the run_id provided does not exist, the system returns an error indicating the run was not found.

features.name: Flow List View
features.rationale: Visualizes available work-order templates.
features.description: Displays a table of saved flows with summaries and last run status.

behaviors.rationale: Provides initial overview of templates.
behaviors.summary: Renders list of flows from MCP data.
behaviors.detail: The UI fetches data from tm_list_flows and renders a table showing flow name, message preview, default worker, and timestamps.

features.name: Flow Edit Form
features.rationale: Enables creation of new templates.
features.description: Allows users to create or edit flow templates via a form.

behaviors.rationale: Enables template creation.
behaviors.summary: Captures form inputs to save a new flow.
behaviors.detail: The UI collects name, message body, default worker, and metadata from the form and invokes tm_save_flow.

features.name: Flow Definition & Management
features.rationale: Centralizes templates for reusable agent actions and context injection.
features.description: Allows creation, retrieval, and deletion of named flows that encapsulate a target worker and message body.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures flows are stored persistently and initialized with correct metadata.
behaviors.summary: Operators can create a new flow with a unique name, optional target worker, body content, and metadata.
behaviors.detail: When creating a flow, the system validates the name against a specific regex pattern to ensure safe filesystem paths. It assigns a unique timestamp for creation and updates the internal tracking immediately. The default worker can be set, but individual runs can override this setting.

behaviors.rationale: Provides read-access to flow definitions for inspection and modification.
behaviors.summary: Operators can retrieve an existing flow by name, returning its full definition or null if not found.
behaviors.detail: The system checks the filesystem for a JSON file matching the requested flow name. If the file exists, it parses the JSON and returns the Flow object. If the name is invalid, it silently returns null without creating anything.

behaviors.rationale: Allows cleanup of outdated or unwanted flow templates.
behaviors.summary: Operators can delete a flow by name, removing the associated template from the system.
behaviors.detail: The system validates the name format before attempting deletion. If the file exists, it is removed atomically. If the name is invalid or the file is missing, the deletion is reported as a failure.

behaviors.rationale: Provides discovery capability for available flow templates.
behaviors.summary: Operators can list all available flows with their metadata.
behaviors.detail: The system iterates through all JSON files in the flows directory, validates each name, and parses the content. Invalid files are skipped with a warning logged. Only valid flows are returned in the sorted list.

capabilities.name: Event Streaming
capabilities.rationale: Enables low-latency monitoring of fleet events.
capabilities.description: Provides a server-sent events (SSE) stream for pushing real-time events from the hub to clients.

features.name: Live Event Feed
features.rationale: Delivers server-pushed data to forwarder clients instantly.
features.description: Yields parsed JSON events from the hub via a persistent SSE connection.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains visibility into live hub activity.
behaviors.summary: Hub emits SSE events on GET /stream; client parses and yields data.
behaviors.detail: The client establishes a GET request to the stream endpoint. As the hub emits events, they arrive as Server-Sent Event frames. The client parses the JSON payload from each frame and yields a dictionary containing the event type and data. On a connection loss, the client automatically reconnects with exponential backoff, ensuring continuous monitoring.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures high availability of the monitoring feed.
behaviors.summary: Client reconnects on stream failure with backoff.
behaviors.detail: If the SSE connection drops due to network errors or hub restarts, the client logs a warning and retries the connection. The retry delay starts at 0.5 seconds and doubles on each failure, capped at 10 seconds. Before reconnecting, the client re-registers to ensure its presence is updated in the hub state.

features.name: Per-Worker Event Fan-Out
features.rationale: Supports scalable monitoring from many clients.
features.description: Manages multiple subscribers per worker to handle concurrent SSE connections.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains stream integrity for one client.
behaviors.summary: Delivers events to subscribed queues without race conditions.
behaviors.detail: The engine uses a separate asyncio.Queue for each subscriber to ensure that each client receives events in order without contention.

features.name: Event Streaming
features.rationale: Operators need to observe fleet status and worker actions instantly.
features.description: Provides a real-time feed of worker activity and system events to connected clients.

behaviors.rationale: Clients must be notified of all state changes via a consistent channel.
behaviors.summary: Emits structured events for all worker activities to global SSE subscribers.
behaviors.detail: The system captures events from the bridge engine and forwards them to subscribers via Server-Sent Events (SSE). Each event includes a worker identifier and data payload, ensuring clients stay synchronized with fleet status.

behaviors.rationale: Provides immutable audit trail of agent actions.
behaviors.summary: Accepts and records outbound events produced by a worker.
behaviors.detail: When a worker generates an event (e.g., a log line or metric), it posts a payload to /tubemail/<worker>/outbound. The system validates the worker name and assigns a unique event ID and timestamp. The response includes this ID for client-side tracking of the event's lifecycle.

capabilities.name: Flow Execution
capabilities.rationale: Automates sequences of operations defined by the user.
capabilities.description: Runs a saved list of commands across the fleet.

features.name: Sequential Execution
features.rationale: Allows chaining of independent agent tasks.
features.description: Executes stored steps one by one across designated workers.

behaviors.rationale: Implements the sequential logic of a flow.
behaviors.summary: Executes the first step and waits for completion.
behaviors.detail: Given a saved flow exists, When the user triggers execution, Then the system runs the first step and waits before the next.

features.name: Run Log Generation
features.rationale: Enables full auditability and tracing of agent interactions and state changes.
features.description: Automatically generates unique run IDs for each flow invocation and persists a chronological log of all events occurring during that specific run.

behaviors.rationale: Establishes a unique tracking context for each execution instance.
behaviors.summary: When a flow is invoked, the system generates a unique run ID and creates a new run log entry.
behaviors.detail: The system generates a cryptographically secure random string as the run ID to prevent injection. It initializes a new log entry with the flow name, target worker, start timestamp, and the first event ID. This entry is written atomically to ensure data integrity.

behaviors.rationale: Guarantees data consistency and prevents corruption from failed writes.
behaviors.summary: The system atomically writes run logs to ensure data integrity even during crashes.
behaviors.detail: All writes to the run log use a temporary file followed by a rename operation. This ensures that even if the process crashes mid-write, the file on disk is either valid or does not exist, never partial.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains up-to-date execution history for each flow template.
behaviors.summary: When a run completes, the system updates the associated flow with the last run timestamp.
behaviors.detail: Upon successful completion of a run, the system retrieves the original flow definition, updates its last_run_at field with the run's start time, and persists this change atomically.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures run IDs are safe and cannot be crafted to break security assumptions.
behaviors.summary: Run IDs are validated to prevent injection attacks and ensure only valid executions are recorded.
behaviors.detail: The system validates incoming run IDs against a strict pattern allowing only alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Invalid IDs are rejected with an error, preventing potential security exploits.

features.name: Flow Execution
features.rationale: Automates the running of saved procedures.
features.description: Triggers defined workflows for agents.

behaviors.rationale: Matches /api/flows execution logic.
behaviors.summary: Executes a specific flow against the agent fleet.
behaviors.detail: Runs the registered workflow and logs results.

behaviors.rationale: Executes automation logic asynchronously.
behaviors.summary: Initiates the execution of a specific flow on a selected worker.
behaviors.detail: The system takes a flow name and optional worker target, then returns a run ID for tracking.

behaviors.rationale: Runs pre-defined workflow logic.
behaviors.summary: Initiates execution of a registered flow.
behaviors.detail: Accepts a flow id and optional parameters, triggering the flow execution chain.

capabilities.name: Saved Flows
capabilities.rationale: Adds repeatability and orchestration capabilities to the control bus.
capabilities.description: Stores and executes named sequences of commands or templates to automate worker tasks.

features.name: Flow Template
features.rationale: Allows operators to save complex interactions for future execution.
features.description: Creates a reusable script or command sequence stored for later use.

behaviors.rationale: Enables creation of custom automation routines.
behaviors.summary: Saves a sequence of commands or a template for a specific task.
behaviors.detail: The user inputs a name and the sequence of operations to be performed. This is stored in a persistent store and can be referenced by ID or name in future requests.

features.name: Override Triggering
features.rationale: Supports Quartermaster or other systems to initiate complex actions.
features.description: Enables specific users or systems to trigger materialized flows like overrides.

behaviors.rationale: Streamlines manual intervention into the system.
behaviors.summary: Authorized users can initiate pre-defined workflow overrides.
behaviors.detail: The system validates user identity and executes the saved flow when an override condition is met.

capabilities.name: Update Manager
capabilities.rationale: Ensures fleet consistency and allows version management for workers.
capabilities.description: Facilitates the safe updating of workers or agent versions from the hub.

features.name: Version Update
features.rationale: Maintains the health and compatibility of the agent fleet.
features.description: Pushes or triggers updates to the agent environment on target workers.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the fleet runs the latest supported versions.
behaviors.summary: Coordinates the process to update a worker's code or environment.
behaviors.detail: The system checks for available updates or applies a new image/layer. It manages the state change from running to updating to healthy.

features.name: tm_update_manager
features.rationale: Enables hot-reloading of agent logic without stopping the worker process.
features.description: Re-executes a worker's manager process to refresh its context or configuration.

behaviors.rationale: Core maintenance action for keeping agents updated.
behaviors.summary: Re-executes a specific worker's manager if idle.
behaviors.detail: The request dispatches an event to the engine to re-run the manager process for the specified worker. The operation fails if the worker is not in an 'idle' state unless explicitly forced via a query parameter.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents corruption of active agent state.
behaviors.summary: Refuses to update a running worker.
behaviors.detail: If the worker is busy executing tasks, the endpoint returns an error. The error message indicates the current state and suggests using a force flag to override.

capabilities.name: Event Bus
capabilities.rationale: Enables asynchronous event-driven monitoring.
capabilities.description: Provides event stream subscriptions via WebSocket for real-time monitoring.

features.name: Event Subscription
features.rationale: Pushes event updates to subscribed clients.
features.description: Accepts WebSocket connections for streaming server events.

behaviors.rationale: Enables real-time event push.
behaviors.summary: Accepts WebSocket connection for event streaming.
behaviors.detail: Establishes a WebSocket connection and streams events as they occur.

capabilities.name: Event Delivery
capabilities.rationale: Ensures reliable data streaming without silent loss of critical events.
capabilities.description: Delivers state changes and stream data to connected subscribers with robust queue handling.

features.name: Fan-out Delivery
features.rationale: Ensures all observers receive the same state updates simultaneously.
features.description: Sends event updates to all connected subscribers efficiently.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents silent data loss and ensures the subscriber knows to disconnect.
behaviors.summary: Handles slow subscribers by logging and closing the connection gracefully.
behaviors.detail: The system pushes events to a queue for each subscriber. If the subscriber cannot keep up, the queue fills. Instead of dropping events silently, the system logs the condition and sends a sentinel message to signal the subscriber to terminate cleanly.

capabilities.name: Fleet Context Analysis
capabilities.rationale: Performance dimension for optimizing fleet efficiency.
capabilities.description: Calculates and exposes the context percentage utilization metrics for workers.

features.name: Context Percentage Calculation
features.rationale: Provides visibility into resource consumption.
features.description: Computes and exposes the percentage of available context currently in use per worker.

behaviors.rationale: Enables monitoring of context utilization levels.
behaviors.summary: Polls and exposes the context percentage via a dedicated endpoint.
behaviors.detail: The backend engine updates the context percentage regularly. This value is exposed via a specific API endpoint (e.g., /context-pct) which the management UI polls. The value is calculated based on the ratio of used context to total available context.

capabilities.name: Rate Limit Handling
capabilities.rationale: Maintains throughput during API throttling by pausing and retrying after safe intervals.
capabilities.description: Detects Anthropic rate limits and implements backoff strategies to keep agents operational during API restrictions.

features.name: Transient 429 Recovery
features.rationale: Resumes agent work automatically when rate limits are lifted.
features.description: Detects rate limit markers and backoff timers to resume operation after temporary API limits.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents hammering the API during transient throttling.
behaviors.summary: Backs off and retries after detecting a rate limit marker.
behaviors.detail: When the output buffer contains a rate limit marker, the manager waits for progressively longer durations (15s, 30s, 60s, 120s) before the next attempt to inject a continue command.

behaviors.rationale: Allows rapid recovery when API access normalizes.
behaviors.summary: Resets backoff timer after a successful execution period.
behaviors.detail: If the process runs cleanly for 20 seconds without another rate limit, the manager resets its backoff counter to the initial value.

capabilities.name: Reconnect Logic
capabilities.rationale: Linear-satisfaction dimension ensuring resilience against simulated network interruptions.
capabilities.description: Handles the restoration of connectivity after a failure via internal reconnection capabilities.

features.name: tm_reconnect_mcp
features.rationale: Automates recovery procedures following a simulated failure event.
features.description: Mechanism to restore functionality after the server has been forced into a broken state.

behaviors.rationale: Enables rapid recovery from temporary outages.
behaviors.summary: Restores service after a break command.
behaviors.detail: When the 'broken' flag is set and the 'heal' control endpoint is triggered, the server clears the broken state, resets counters, and allows subsequent MCP calls to succeed.

capabilities.name: Recording Stream
capabilities.rationale: Enables debugging after-the-fact for agent behavior.
capabilities.description: Captures and streams session data for post-analysis and debugging.

features.name: Recording Playback
features.rationale: Enables post-session review of agent interactions for debugging and training.
features.description: Displays recorded terminal output for review and analysis of agent sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Provides audit trail for agent interactions and debugging.
behaviors.summary: Streams recording data to the hub for playback and analysis.
behaviors.detail: The recording stream forwards PTY output bytes from the manager to the hub via SSE. This works reliably for workers with attached browser tabs but may be inconsistent for browser-less workers due to subscriber eviction issues. Files rotate at the configured size limit with automatic garbage collection.

capabilities.name: Server Discovery
capabilities.rationale: Enables clients to identify server capabilities and data identity programmatically.
capabilities.description: Provides essential metadata about the TubeMail server to clients for discovery and contract understanding.

features.name: server_info
features.rationale: Allows clients to discover server category and identity constraints.
features.description: Returns category metadata and identity information for the MCP server.

behaviors.rationale: Exposes server contract to client.
behaviors.summary: Returns JSON metadata describing the TubeMail MCP server.
behaviors.detail: Returns a JSON string containing server name, version, category, data identity, and lists of meta/cross-repo tools.

capabilities.name: Context Visibility
capabilities.rationale: Gives operators insight into agent health and workload without polling.
capabilities.description: Provides real-time status indicators like context usage and active processing markers.

features.name: Active Status Detection
features.rationale: Allows the hub to know if the agent is busy or idle without guessing from logs.
features.description: Detects whether the agent is mid-request by analyzing the pty output.

behaviors.rationale: Accurately reflects agent workload to external viewers.
behaviors.summary: Detects if the agent is actively processing using pty output patterns.
behaviors.detail: The manager scans the last screen buffer for patterns like 'Mulling', 'thinking', or '(Xs' to determine if the agent is busy.

capabilities.name: Permission Channel
capabilities.rationale: Supports specific security constraints or access control workflows.
capabilities.description: Extends the standard channel with specific permission-related experimental capabilities.

features.name: Permission Declaration
features.rationale: Indicates the channel supports advanced permission checking.
features.description: Advertises the existence of the permission capability to the client.

behaviors.rationale: Allows clients to opt-in to permission-based flows.
behaviors.summary: Includes permission capability in the initialization response.
behaviors.detail: During initialize, the channel declares 'experimental.claude/channel/permission' as a supported capability, though the current implementation does not define specific tools for it.

behaviors.rationale: Enables visibility into security approval workflow.
behaviors.summary: Lists pending tool approval prompts across workers.
behaviors.detail: Returns all pending permission requests from workers waiting for operator approval to execute certain tools.

behaviors.rationale: Enables security control over tool execution.
behaviors.summary: Responds to pending permission prompts with allow or deny.
behaviors.detail: Processes a permission request from a worker and either approves or denies the requested tool access.

capabilities.name: Agent Delegation
capabilities.rationale: Facilitates complex multi-agent workflows without platform logic.
capabilities.description: Allows agents to request actions from other agents across different hosts.

features.name: Cross-Host Routing
features.rationale: Supports distributed agent coordination.
features.description: Routes messages to the appropriate worker regardless of host location.

behaviors.rationale: Enables multi-host agent collaboration.
behaviors.summary: Delivers a message to the correct worker on the correct host.
behaviors.detail: Given a message targets a specific worker, When the system routes the message, Then the worker receives the message even if it is on a different host.

behaviors.rationale: Supports distributed deployment topologies.
behaviors.summary: Hub routes inbound events to the correct worker regardless of host.
behaviors.detail: When an inbound message is destined for a worker, the hub ensures it reaches the local forwarder. This applies even if the worker is on a different host than the operator.

features.name: Agent Delegation
features.rationale: Supports secure agent-to-agent handoffs across different hosts.
features.description: Facilitates multi-host delegation of tasks between agents without platform orchestration.

behaviors.rationale: Enables distributed processing without central logic.
behaviors.summary: An agent can securely request and receive tasks from remote agents.
behaviors.detail: Agents establish secure out-of-process HTTP/WebSocket connections to delegate execution tasks to other agents.

behaviors.rationale: Validates security and routing logic.
behaviors.summary: Accepts incoming tasks and forwards them to targets.
behaviors.detail: Validates session and bearer tokens before routing work requests.

behaviors.rationale: Enables a multi-agent ecosystem to share workload management.
behaviors.summary: Processes requests from external agents to manage worker state.
behaviors.detail: The hub exposes tools that accept input from external agents and return status or logs, allowing a decentralized network of managers to operate a single fleet.

capabilities.name: Worker Recording
capabilities.rationale: Provides audit trails and debug capabilities for long-running sessions.
capabilities.description: Captures terminal output from active worker sessions for post-session debugging.

features.name: Session Capture
features.rationale: Recording is needed to preserve the execution context for later review.
features.description: Configures and activates recording for specific workers to capture their execution.

behaviors.rationale: Enables the creation of a recording for later analysis.
behaviors.summary: Activates recording state for a target worker.
behaviors.detail: The system updates the internal state to begin capturing frames for the specified worker session.

features.name: Recording Retrieval
features.rationale: Operators need access to the captured session frames to debug issues.
features.description: Fetches recorded session data from the system store.

behaviors.rationale: Retrieval allows the operator to inspect the recorded execution.
behaviors.summary: Retrieves recorded frames for a specific worker session.
behaviors.detail: The system queries the storage backend and returns the sequence of captured frames for the requested worker.

behaviors.rationale: Provides audit trails.
behaviors.summary: Toggles the recording state (on/off) for a worker via an icon.
behaviors.detail: The toggle sends a POST request to the recording endpoint. The UI updates to reflect the new enabled state.

features.name: Worker Listing
features.rationale: Gives operators a global view of the managed AI fleet.
features.description: Retrieves a live list of all registered workers and their current states.

behaviors.rationale: Provides the foundational data for all fleet management tasks.
behaviors.summary: Fetches the list of all workers and their current attributes.
behaviors.detail: The endpoint returns an array of worker objects including their name, state (idle, busy, waiting), and activity metrics.

behaviors.rationale: Enables operators to distinguish active, idle, and failed agents.
behaviors.summary: Reports detailed status and health metrics for each worker.
behaviors.detail: Each worker entry includes state, pending task count, last activity timestamp, and connection health indicators.

behaviors.rationale: Direct control over fleet instances.
behaviors.summary: Manages the lifecycle of individual worker agents.
behaviors.detail: Allows users to initialize a worker, retrieve its current logs, and terminate the process gracefully via HTTP endpoints.

behaviors.rationale: Establishes the foundational connection for all subsequent management.
behaviors.summary: Registers a new worker and initializes its communication channel.
behaviors.detail: The system receives a registration request containing worker metadata, creates a persistent entry in the hub state, and establishes the initial HTTP/WebSocket connection for telemetry and command delivery.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains real-time visibility into agent fleet health and activity.
behaviors.summary: Updates worker status and health metrics.
behaviors.detail: The system continuously updates the worker record with heartbeat data, current command execution status, and resource utilization metrics as they arrive from the agent process.

behaviors.rationale: Enables the core 'command bus' functionality for remote orchestration.
behaviors.summary: Executes remote commands on registered workers.
behaviors.detail: The system accepts external instructions and queues them for delivery to the specific target worker via the established communication channel.

behaviors.rationale: Scripts require non-interactive command access.
behaviors.summary: Invokes MCP tools to list and manage workers.
behaviors.detail: The CLI wraps the MCP tool calls for listing workers and their status. It outputs JSON-formatted data or readable text depending on flags.

behaviors.rationale: Provides immediate visual feedback on worker availability.
behaviors.summary: Shows active or idle indicators for each monitored worker.
behaviors.detail: The UI renders an indicator (e.g., pulsing dot or text) that reflects the 'busy' or 'idle' state of the underlying MCP tool for the selected worker.

features.name: Restart
features.rationale: Updates worker without losing context.
features.description: Re-executes the Python manager wrapper while preserving the active Claude session.

behaviors.rationale: Applies updates without downtime.
behaviors.summary: Restarts the manager process for a selected online worker via a dedicated icon.
behaviors.detail: Clicking the restart icon triggers a POST request to update the manager. The underlying Claude session is preserved, and the worker re-registers with the latest commit SHA.

features.name: Purge
features.rationale: Cleans up dead endpoints.
features.description: Deletes a disconnected or unwanted worker from the fleet.

behaviors.rationale: Manages fleet size dynamically.
behaviors.summary: Removes a worker from the roster after user confirmation.
behaviors.detail: Clicking the trash icon on a worker row requests a DELETE API call. A confirmation step prevents accidental deletion of active agents.

features.name: Screen Tees
features.rationale: Manages storage footprint while enabling deep inspection capabilities.
features.description: Switches screen recording on or off for specific workers.

behaviors.rationale: Allows on-demand archiving of agent sessions.
behaviors.summary: Hub toggles the recording stream for a worker's process.
behaviors.detail: The hub accepts a toggle command to enable or disable tee-ing the process output to disk. This state persists across restarts and is respected by the underlying recording manager.

features.name: List Workers
features.rationale: Provides visibility into available worker sessions.
features.description: Returns a list of currently connected and registered worker agents.

behaviors.rationale: Enumerates live worker connections.
behaviors.summary: Lists all active workers registered with the hub.
behaviors.detail: Returns a list of worker identifiers that are currently online and registered with the BridgeEngine.

features.name: Send Work Order
features.rationale: Primary mechanism for driving remote worker processes.
features.description: Delivers a message/work order to a specific worker and returns an event ID.

behaviors.rationale: Routes execution context to target worker.
behaviors.summary: Sends a message to a worker and returns an event ID.
behaviors.detail: Accepts a worker identifier and message payload, enqueues the work via the BridgeEngine, and returns a unique event_id.

features.name: tm_wait_for_activity
features.rationale: Enables orchestrators to synchronously wait for worker output.
features.description: Blocks execution until a reply or update arrives for a given worker since a specific event.

behaviors.rationale: Synchronizes orchestration loop with worker execution.
behaviors.summary: Waits for activity from a worker since a specified event ID.
behaviors.detail: Blocks until new events arrive for the target worker since the given event_id, then returns the latest event.

features.name: Refresh Tools
features.rationale: Allows dynamic tool set updates without restart.
features.description: Rebuilds the available tool list after server reconfiguration.

behaviors.rationale: Updates tool availability without restart.
behaviors.summary: Reinitializes available tools after a rebuild.
behaviors.detail: Instructs the MCP server to reload its tool registry to reflect new registrations or changes.

features.name: get_instructions
features.rationale: Provides usage context and workflow guidance.
features.description: Returns the server's operational instructions for the client.

behaviors.rationale: Discovers server usage context.
behaviors.summary: Returns the current server instructions.
behaviors.detail: Returns a string containing the server's operational instructions and usage workflow.

capabilities.name: Worker Terminal
capabilities.rationale: Core primitive for direct agent management and session control.
capabilities.description: Provides a command-line interface to view, interact with, and terminate local agent workers.

features.name: Worker Session
features.rationale: Enables real-time command execution and output streaming for active workers.
features.description: Establishes an interactive terminal session with a running agent worker.

behaviors.rationale: Enables immediate inspection and control of worker execution context.
behaviors.summary: Opens a live terminal session attached to a specific worker process.
behaviors.detail: The tool connects the client to the worker's stdout/stdin via a WebSocket stream, allowing the user to send shell commands and view immediate output. The session persists as long as the connection is active and the worker is running.

features.name: WebSocket Connection
features.rationale: Allows real-time updates and interactions with the terminal environment.
features.description: Maintains a persistent WebSocket connection for streaming terminal data.

behaviors.rationale: Enables real-time interaction with the terminal content.
behaviors.summary: Manages WebSocket connections for streaming terminal data efficiently.
behaviors.detail: The system manages the WebSocket connection to ensure that terminal data is streamed in real-time without latency or loss. It handles ping responses and manages the connection state to ensure that the user sees up-to-date content.

features.name: Worker Terminal
features.rationale: Direct control of the worker's shell.
features.description: Integrated terminal pane with keybindings and pop-out support.

behaviors.rationale: Access worker shell.
behaviors.summary: Connects to worker PTY via WebSocket.
behaviors.detail: The terminal pane establishes a WebSocket connection to the worker's PTY endpoint. It multiplexes read, write, and resize events over a single socket. The session uses ticket-exchange for authentication.

behaviors.rationale: Standard terminal interaction.
behaviors.summary: Supports keybindings.
behaviors.detail: The terminal supports standard shell keybindings including Shift+Enter for new line, Ctrl+C for copy, Ctrl+V for paste, and zoom shortcuts. Selection-aware copy and paste ensure clipboard data transfers correctly.

behaviors.rationale: Flexible workspace layout.
behaviors.summary: Handles pop-out windows.
behaviors.detail: Users can open the terminal in a separate pop-out window. The pop-out window adjusts its size to match the manager's PTY grid. Each pop-out is an independent client multiplexed to the same session.

behaviors.rationale: Graceful degradation for legacy agents.
behaviors.summary: Shows fallback when manager is silent.
behaviors.detail: If no PTY bytes arrive within 4 seconds of connection, the UI displays a card instructing the user to reconnect or refresh. This handles older managers that ignore pty_attach events.

capabilities.name: Developer Loopback
capabilities.rationale: Improves developer experience by simplifying local testing setup.
capabilities.description: Provides a loopback-only mechanism to skip the authentication gate during local development.

features.name: Dev Bootstrap
features.rationale: Enables seamless local development without manual token pasting.
features.description: Returns the bearer token for local browser clients on the same machine.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces friction for local development workflows.
behaviors.summary: Returns the bearer secret to localhost clients.
behaviors.detail: The endpoint accepts requests only from loopback addresses (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost). It returns the configured secret key, allowing the local frontend to bypass the auth gate initially.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures security boundary for sensitive keys.
behaviors.summary: Rejects non-localhost requests.
behaviors.detail: Any request originating from a non-loopback IP address is immediately rejected with a 403 Forbidden status, regardless of the user's identity.

capabilities.name: CLI
capabilities.rationale: Inherit terminal ergonomics — a thin wrapper over MCP tools so power users stay in the shell.
capabilities.description: Command-line interface. Thin wrapper — all logic lives in MCP tools.

features.name: Bus Execution
features.rationale: Simplifies access for automation scripts.
features.description: Executes commands defined in the MCP tools from the terminal.

behaviors.rationale: Acts as a shell for the MCP engine.
behaviors.summary: Users run management commands via the CLI.
behaviors.detail: The CLI translates commands into MCP tool invocations on the backend.

features.name: Worker List
features.rationale: Provides immediate feedback on the fleet state via command line.
features.description: Displays a textual list of connected workers in the terminal.

behaviors.rationale: Quick status check for terminal-native workflows.
behaviors.summary: Executes a request to the MCP tool and prints the response to stdout.
behaviors.detail: The CLI wrapper invokes the MCP server's list function and pipes the JSON response to the user. The output is formatted for readability.

features.name: Command Dispatcher
features.rationale: Allows scripting and automation of worker tasks directly from bash.
features.description: Sends raw commands to the worker's MCP tool endpoint from the terminal.

behaviors.rationale: Enables automation and scripting of remote tasks.
behaviors.summary: Transmits a serialized command object to the worker's MCP tool.
behaviors.detail: The CLI parses the user input and constructs the JSON payload required by the backend. It then sends the request and streams the result to the user.

features.name: Tool Invocation
features.rationale: Enables scripting and automation workflows.
features.description: Executes MCP tools directly from the shell.

behaviors.rationale: Bridges shell scripts to MCP logic.
behaviors.summary: Invokes underlying MCP tools from the command line.
behaviors.detail: Parses CLI arguments and forwards them to the underlying MCP service, returning JSON output or streamable logs.

features.name: Command Execution
features.rationale: Integrates management tasks into existing shell workflows.
features.description: Allows sending commands to agents or checking their status via shell scripts.

behaviors.rationale: Bridges the gap between human operators and automated execution.
behaviors.summary: Executes management commands on a specific worker or the whole fleet.
behaviors.detail: The CLI wrapper maps user commands to the underlying MCP tools, sending them to the hub for processing and returning the result to the terminal.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains consistency between CLI and backend logic.
behaviors.summary: Runs CLI commands using the MCP backend.
behaviors.detail: When a user runs a CLI command, the system forwards the request to the corresponding MCP tool and displays the output.

features.name: Command Wrapper
features.rationale: Provides a thin shell around the core backend logic.
features.description: Executes management commands by invoking underlying MCP tools.

behaviors.rationale: Enables scriptable and terminal-based management.
behaviors.summary: Translates CLI arguments into MCP tool calls.
behaviors.detail: Given a valid CLI command, When the user executes the command, Then the system calls the corresponding MCP tool and returns the result.

features.name: Command Invocation
features.rationale: Enables automation and scripting of agent management tasks.
features.description: Executes MCP tool calls via the command line interface.

behaviors.rationale: Bridges human command-line usage with programmatic tool interfaces.
behaviors.summary: Accepts commands and outputs JSON-RPC responses from MCP tools.
behaviors.detail: The CLI parses commands and passes them to the MCP server, printing the raw or formatted JSON response.

features.name: Status Command
features.rationale: Provides a lightweight alternative to the UI dashboard.
features.description: Quickly prints the current state of the fleet to the terminal.

behaviors.rationale: Fast feedback loop for command-line users.
behaviors.summary: The CLI outputs the current fleet status to stdout.
behaviors.detail: The command invokes the monitoring MCP tool and formats the JSON response into a readable terminal output.

features.name: Restart Manager
features.rationale: Simplifies maintenance tasks compared to manual process killing.
features.description: Provides a quick command to restart the local agent host process.

behaviors.rationale: Streamlines recovery from stuck agents.
behaviors.summary: The CLI triggers a restart of the local worker host.
behaviors.detail: The command requests the restart MCP tool to be invoked, which sends a signal to the host process to clean up and reboot.

features.name: Status Check
features.rationale: Allows admins to verify hub health.
features.description: Displays the current list of active worker sessions and their connection states.

behaviors.rationale: Provides quick operational visibility.
behaviors.summary: Lists worker sessions and their connection states.
behaviors.detail: When the user runs the CLI command without arguments, it queries the hub for active sessions, formats the output as a table, and displays worker IDs, connection counts, and last heartbeat timestamps.

features.name: Reset Handler
features.rationale: Resolves deadlocks or stale connections.
features.description: Triggers a manual reset of a specific worker session or the entire hub state.

behaviors.rationale: Enables manual recovery of stuck workers.
behaviors.summary: Resets a specific worker session by reopening its channel.
behaviors.detail: When the user specifies a worker ID, the CLI closes the existing connection for that worker, clears its buffer, and re-establishes the channel. This allows recovery from hung tasks or protocol errors.

features.name: Remote Management
features.rationale: Extends management capabilities to terminal users.
features.description: Commands to list workers, check status, and control recording.

behaviors.rationale: Provides terminal access to the service.
behaviors.summary: CLI commands query the hub API to perform management tasks.
behaviors.detail: Commands like listing workers or toggling recording wrap the HTTP API. They parse responses and output human-readable data to the terminal.

features.name: CLI Command Injection
features.rationale: Enables direct control over the terminal UI state of the agent from a remote operator.
features.description: Injects keyboard commands into the running Claude process to manipulate its state.

behaviors.rationale: Allows state changes via standard terminal commands.
behaviors.summary: Types commands like /compact, /clear, /rename into the active terminal.
behaviors.detail: When the manager receives a request to compact, clear, or rename context, it injects the corresponding text into the pseudo-terminal master file.

capabilities.gherkin: Rule: CLI commands must map 1:1 to MCP tool calls with no additional business logic.

capabilities.name: Command Line Interface
capabilities.rationale: Provides a local touchpoint for operators to manage the hub directly.
capabilities.description: A thin wrapper tool for local administration and configuration.

features.name: Hub Administration
features.rationale: Simplifies operational tasks without requiring direct API access.
features.description: Executes commands to start, stop, or inspect the hub service.

behaviors.rationale: Enables local service management via standard tools.
behaviors.summary: Starts the TubeMail hub service.
behaviors.detail: The CLI tool launches the hub process and validates that the configuration files are present before starting the server.

features.name: Status Query Command
features.rationale: Allows quick checks of worker availability without opening the main UI.
features.description: Executes a command that retrieves and formats the current status of specified workers.

behaviors.rationale: Provides a lightweight way to verify agent state via CLI.
behaviors.summary: The CLI tool fetches the current state of a worker from the hub API.
behaviors.detail: When a user runs the status command with a worker ID, the CLI sends a request to the HTTP endpoint. It then formats the response to show 'idle' or 'busy' along with the timestamp of the last known state change.

capabilities.name: Permission Inbox
capabilities.rationale: Addresses the primary pain of permission fan-out by centralizing authorization decisions.
capabilities.description: Aggregates permission requests from agents into a single interface for rapid review and approval.

features.name: Request Approval
features.rationale: Centralizes permission fan-out to solve acute authorization pain.
features.description: Enables operators to review, approve, or deny permission requests received from agents.

behaviors.rationale: Enables fast, single-action authorization to reduce fan-out friction.
behaviors.summary: Displays pending permission requests and allows the operator to grant access.
behaviors.detail: The Inbox presents incoming permission requests in a clear list, highlighting which agent requested access and the nature of the request. The operator can click a request to view details and execute an approval action that updates the agent's state via the underlying control bus.

features.name: Permission Fan-out
features.rationale: Enables agents to act on behalf of the operator immediately after authorization.
features.description: Distributes required execution permissions to target workers upon request.

behaviors.rationale: Resolves pending permission states in under 2 keystrokes.
behaviors.summary: Broadcasts permission grants to active workers to enable immediate execution capabilities.
behaviors.detail: When a user approves a request, the system propagates the permission grant state to the relevant worker processes. This resolves permission denial errors and allows the worker to continue executing without interruption.

features.name: Permission Grant
features.rationale: Controls access granularity to prevent unauthorized agent interactions.
features.description: Assigns specific access rights to agents or users for target workers.

behaviors.rationale: Core security mechanism for multi-host delegation.
behaviors.summary: Creates a new permission allowing a specific agent to access workers.
behaviors.detail: The system accepts a request to grant a subject (agent/user) access to a set of objects (workers). This creates an entry in the authorization store that the bus enforces during every request.

features.name: Inbox List
features.rationale: Eliminates the need to check individual worker terminals for pending actions.
features.description: A consolidated view of all pending tool permission requests sorted by source agent.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces operational overhead for high-volume permission cycles.
behaviors.summary: Groups pending requests by tool name and allows bulk allow/deny actions.
behaviors.detail: Requests are grouped so the operator can approve or deny all pending actions for a specific tool category in a single interaction. Only one-shot bulk actions are supported; persistent 'always allow' rules are excluded from v1.

features.name: Unified pending list
features.rationale: Prevents operators from missing requests scattered across different tabs.
features.description: Aggregates all open permission requests from every worker in one scrollable list.

behaviors.rationale: Single source of truth for all pending security actions.
behaviors.summary: Displays all pending permission requests from every worker, grouped by worker ID.
behaviors.detail: Given N workers have pending permissions, When the inbox loads, Then list all N requests sorted by worker, grouping them visually to separate concerns.

features.name: Keyboard Approval
features.rationale: Enables high-speed approval workflows required for high-volume agent fleets.
features.description: Allows operators to accept or deny requests using a single key press (Y/N).

behaviors.rationale: Reduces approval friction to a single keystroke.
behaviors.summary: Accepts a pending request when Y is pressed while that row is focused.
behaviors.detail: Given a row is focused in the inbox, When the operator presses the Y key, Then execute the allow command and remove the row.

features.name: Bulk Allow
features.rationale: Efficiently handles scenarios where specific tools (like Bash) are trusted by default.
features.description: Allows instant approval of all pending requests for a specific tool type.

behaviors.rationale: Batches identical requests to save operator time.
behaviors.summary: Approves all pending requests for a specific tool name without storing rules.
behaviors.detail: Given the inbox has K pending requests for a specific tool, When the operator triggers bulk-allow, Then run the allow command for all K requests without persisting a rule.

features.name: Pending Requests
features.rationale: Prevents unauthorized actions until a human operator explicitly grants access.
features.description: Shows incoming requests waiting for manual approval or denial.

behaviors.rationale: Centralizes security decisions in one location.
behaviors.summary: Displays a list of incoming requests with allow/deny buttons.
behaviors.detail: When a request arrives, the UI renders a card showing the requesting agent, the tool involved, and the current state, allowing the user to take immediate action.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents stale counts and missed access requests.
behaviors.summary: Fetches and displays pending permissions.
behaviors.detail: The system retrieves the count and list of pending permission requests via the API. This updates the inbox badge and lists available actions for each request.

features.name: Bulk Actions
features.rationale: Speeds up workflow when handling many requests of the same type.
features.description: Allows filtering and managing requests by tool name or category.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces repetitive clicking for high-volume tool groups.
behaviors.summary: Users can bulk allow or deny requests filtered by a specific tool.
behaviors.detail: When a filter is applied by tool name, all matching requests are selected, allowing the user to approve or reject them with a single click.

features.name: Permission Inbox
features.rationale: Provides centralized management of shell access requests for security.
features.description: Shows pending permission requests from external agents requiring user approval.

behaviors.rationale: Streamlines secure access delegation for external agents.
behaviors.summary: Displays Bash permission prompts for quick approval in the inbox.
behaviors.detail: The permission inbox shows requests from external agents needing Bash access. Approvals can be granted in two keystrokes by selecting the request and clicking the approve button. The system maintains a record of all granted and denied permissions for audit purposes.

behaviors.rationale: Provides a safety checkpoint for sensitive operations.
behaviors.summary: Holds high-privilege actions pending operator approval.
behaviors.detail: When a worker requests a permission (e.g., network access, file system write), the request is paused and displayed in the inbox UI until the operator grants or denies it.

behaviors.rationale: Automates enforcement of security rules.
behaviors.summary: Denies access automatically based on policy.
behaviors.detail: Evaluates incoming requests against defined security policies and automatically rejects those that violate them without human intervention.

behaviors.rationale: Enables manual security gatekeeping.
behaviors.summary: Displays pending access requests and approval buttons.
behaviors.detail: Lists incoming delegation requests from other agents, showing the requester identity and requested scope, allowing the user to click 'Approve' or 'Deny'.

behaviors.rationale: Closes the loop on security operations efficiently.
behaviors.summary: Renders pending requests with action buttons.
behaviors.detail: Fetches pending permission objects from the backend and presents them in a card layout with clear 'Approve' and 'Deny' buttons.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents rubber-stamp security errors
behaviors.summary: Requires explicit focus before allowing a single permission request.
behaviors.detail: The page does not auto-focus a row on load. The user must tab or use arrow keys to select a row before pressing Y to allow. This prevents rubber-stamping when the agent requests a permission immediately after launch.

behaviors.rationale: Allows second-guessing without re-entry
behaviors.summary: Queues actions with a short undo window for safety.
behaviors.detail: When the user presses Y, an action is queued and an undo toast appears at the bottom. The action is not sent until 3 seconds pass or the user presses Esc. This allows correction of accidental approvals.

behaviors.rationale: Supports high-speed batch operations
behaviors.summary: Stacks undo toasts and queues multiple rapid approvals.
behaviors.detail: If the user approves several requests in quick succession, each action gets its own toast and timer. Up to three toasts stack at the bottom, each independently cancellable with Esc.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures nothing is missed during correction
behaviors.summary: Highlights incoming rows visually during the undo window.
behaviors.detail: If a new permission request arrives while one is in the undo window, the UI flashes the new row to ensure the operator notices it despite being in the undo period.

behaviors.rationale: Adds friction to bulk actions to prevent mistakes
behaviors.summary: Bulk-allow actions require a confirm dialog.
behaviors.detail: Pressing the bulk allow button triggers a confirmation dialog that must be explicitly confirmed. This prevents accidental bulk approval by sticky modifier keys or reflexive typing.

features.name: Request Retrieval
features.rationale: Provides the list of actions requiring operator attention.
features.description: Fetches the current list of pending permission requests from the system.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the operator always sees the current state of permission requests.
behaviors.summary: Loads and displays the list of pending permission requests on mount.
behaviors.detail: On initial mount and when visibility changes, the component fetches the list of pending permissions and updates the internal state. It calculates the age of each request relative to the current time to display urgency indicators.

features.name: Action Queueing
features.rationale: Prevents accidental permission grants/denials by adding a safety buffer.
features.description: Allows operators to approve or deny requests, queuing the action with a short delay to permit undoing mistakes.

behaviors.rationale: Allows the operator to confirm their decision before it is irreversible.
behaviors.summary: Queues an action request to a server and removes the request from the pending list.
behaviors.detail: When an operator selects a request (e.g., via keyboard 'y'/'n' or button), the action is queued locally with a 3-second timer. If the operator changes their mind within the timer window, they can cancel the queued action. Once the timer expires, the action is sent to the worker hub, and the request is removed from the inbox.

behaviors.rationale: Provides a safety mechanism to reverse accidental selections.
behaviors.summary: Removes a queued action if the timer is cancelled before expiry.
behaviors.detail: The operator can undo a queued action using a shortcut (e.g., Escape) or by waiting for the timer to fire. This ensures that only intentional actions are executed against the system.

capabilities.name: Worker Roster
capabilities.rationale: Mitigates chronic orchestration visibility pain and context switching.
capabilities.description: A persistent, always-on view of the active agent fleet status and activity history to prevent context loss.

features.name: Agent Session List
features.rationale: Provides immediate context on what sessions are doing without alt-tabbing.
features.description: Displays active worker connections with time-since-inbound counters to visualize current fleet state.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents context loss by keeping fleet state visible.
behaviors.summary: Updates the roster list to reflect current agent connection status and recent activity.
behaviors.detail: The UI renders a list of all known workers in the fleet, showing their current operational state (e.g., active, idle, disconnected). The list updates in near-real-time as agents connect to or disconnect from the control bus, ensuring the operator always has an accurate mental model of the fleet.

behaviors.rationale: Visualizes latency uncertainty to aid decision making.
behaviors.summary: Displays current state of an agent derived from the internal state machine.
behaviors.detail: The roster renders a badge for each worker reflecting its current operational state (e.g., idle, busy, error). It includes a countdown timer for agents in the busy state, showing how long they have been processing a request without returning control.

features.name: Worker Discovery
features.rationale: Provides the foundational list of agents that the system can monitor and manage.
features.description: Scans the network to identify and list active worker processes.

behaviors.rationale: Fundamental requirement for any operator to know what exists in the fleet.
behaviors.summary: Retrieves and displays a list of all currently running workers with their status.
behaviors.detail: The system queries internal registration data to populate a roster of workers. Each entry includes the worker ID, host, current state (idle, busy, terminal), and a brief description or command history.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the operator sees the current operational reality of the fleet.
behaviors.summary: Handles state transitions and busy indicators effectively.
behaviors.detail: The roster updates dynamically as workers transition states. The system distinguishes between temporary busy states and potential stale states, ensuring the list remains accurate for decision making.

features.name: State Display
features.rationale: Replaces manual tab-checking with a consolidated fleet view.
features.description: Shows worker status badges and computed offline indicators derived from backend events.

behaviors.rationale: Differentiates between crashes and intentional exits.
behaviors.summary: Displays computed offline status when workers disconnect cleanly.
behaviors.detail: If the SSE stream is lost and the last event was `exited_cleanly`, the UI marks the worker as offline with a Grey badge. If the exit was unclean, a Red badge is shown. This status is computed locally by the UI from the SSE stream rather than being returned by the hub.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces anxiety about whether a worker has stuck on a permission request.
behaviors.summary: Busy Duration Counter
behaviors.detail: Shows a live counter for how long a worker has been processing inbound work.

features.name: Worker Detail Pane
features.rationale: Allows deep inspection and management of individual agents.
features.description: Navigates to a focused view of a specific worker containing its terminal and permission controls.

behaviors.rationale: Consolidates context for a specific agent in one view.
behaviors.summary: Opens a dedicated pane for a selected worker showing its terminal and pending permissions.
behaviors.detail: Given an operator clicks a roster row, When navigation executes, Then render a full-height pane containing the integrated terminal and permission subpanes for that specific worker.

features.name: Live Status List
features.rationale: Gives the operator immediate visibility into which agents are online and ready.
features.description: Lists all active workers and updates their connection state in real-time.

behaviors.rationale: Operators need accurate, real-time fleet visibility.
behaviors.summary: The list updates to reflect the current number of connected workers.
behaviors.detail: The system retrieves the initial roster via HTTP and then listens for streaming updates via SSE to refresh the list when workers join or leave.

features.name: Worker Listing
features.rationale: Core visibility into fleet state.
features.description: Displays active workers with state badges and project grouping.

behaviors.rationale: Visualize fleet status at a glance.
behaviors.summary: Lists workers with dynamic status badges.
behaviors.detail: The roster displays a live list of workers. Each row shows a status badge indicating idle, busy, waiting for permission, or offline states. The UI computes the 'online' flag to distinguish between disconnected sessions and cleanly exited workers.

behaviors.rationale: Ease of finding specific workers.
behaviors.summary: Sorts roster columns dynamically.
behaviors.detail: All seven columns in the roster table are sortable. Users can click headers to cycle between ascending, descending, and off. The primary sort cycles independently of secondary sorts to prevent confusion.

behaviors.rationale: Monitor resource constraints proactively.
behaviors.summary: Shows context usage percentage.
behaviors.detail: The roster includes a column displaying the current percentage of the context window being used by the worker. This metric is derived from the manager's status report and posted to the API.

behaviors.rationale: Enable post-mortem session debugging.
behaviors.summary: Toggles recording status.
behaviors.detail: Each roster row includes a toggle switch for enabling or disabling session recording. This switch updates the worker state in the backend, allowing post-mortem debugging.

behaviors.rationale: Prevent false positive busy states.
behaviors.summary: Decays busy status automatically.
behaviors.detail: If a worker processes work but receives no inbound events for 600 seconds, the system automatically decays its status from 'busy' to 'idle' to prevent false positive alerts.

features.name: Real-Time Status Sync
features.rationale: Provides an accurate reflection of agent availability to the operator.
features.description: Updates the roster view immediately when the backend receives a state change event.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the UI reflects the true state of the agent in real-time.
behaviors.summary: The UI updates to show a worker as busy when the backend receives a real-time active state signal.
behaviors.detail: Upon receiving an SSE event indicating a worker is actively processing, the UI refreshes the worker's row to display 'busy'. This updates instantly without waiting for the next polling cycle, providing a responsive experience.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents the user from seeing stale 'busy' indicators.
behaviors.summary: The UI updates to show a worker as idle when the backend confirms no recent activity.
behaviors.detail: When the backend determines a worker is idle (either via signal or decay), the UI updates the row to show 'idle'. This includes cases where a 'busy' timer has expired or a signal explicitly confirms the agent has stopped.

features.name: Grouping
features.rationale: Clusters related workers for easier scanning.
features.description: Organizes the roster table rows by project directory name.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces scrolling overhead for large fleets.
behaviors.summary: Groups worker rows in the roster table under a collapsible section header for each project directory.
behaviors.detail: The interface identifies each worker by its 'cwd' field. Unique cwd values are aggregated into sections, while workers sharing a directory (e.g., manager and client) appear together in that section.

features.name: Sorting
features.rationale: Enables quick filtering by state or name.
features.description: Allows reordering roster columns by clicking headers.

behaviors.rationale: Flexibility in data view.
behaviors.summary: Sorts rows by a selected column; clicking a header cycles through ascending, descending, and unsorted modes.
behaviors.detail: Clicking a column header toggles between ascending and descending order. Clicking the same header again removes the sort order.

features.name: Stale Detection
features.rationale: Ensures operators work on consistent versions of AI models.
features.description: Marks workers as 'Stale' if they differ from the Hub's canonical Git commit.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains fleet consistency.
behaviors.summary: Displays a 'Stale' badge on workers running an older Git commit than the Hub.
behaviors.detail: The system compares the Hub's canonical commit (from /health) against each worker's current commit. A badge indicates divergence, prompting a restart.

features.name: List Workers
features.rationale: Provides essential visibility into the agent fleet.
features.description: Retrieves a list of all known workers with their current state.

behaviors.rationale: Fundamental requirement for any management interface.
behaviors.summary: Returns the current roster of all workers.
behaviors.detail: The endpoint queries the engine for all registered workers, filtering for currently online workers by default and providing state information for each. The response includes the worker name and its current operational status.

features.name: Roster Management
features.rationale: Operational visibility into the fleet of workers.
features.description: View and manage active and historical agent states.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures visual consistency and predictability in the UI.
behaviors.summary: Displays a list of agents with consistent iconography for state and action.
behaviors.detail: The roster uses a single Lucide React library for all icons with a consistent stroke weight and size (12-16px). It utilizes specific icons like 'FolderOpen' and 'Trash2' for roster actions, and 'Circle' variants for recording states.

behaviors.rationale: Visualizes fleet status.
behaviors.summary: Renders a table of connected workers with status indicators.
behaviors.detail: The interface fetches worker data from the MCP registry and renders a table showing worker IDs and current states.

behaviors.rationale: Provides the primary view for monitoring agents.
behaviors.summary: Dashboard renders the list of registered workers and their current state.
behaviors.detail: The UI displays the worker name, working directory, context percentage, and active/busy/idle status. It reflects the authoritative state from the backend.

capabilities.name: Roster View
capabilities.rationale: Provides immediate fleet health overview at a glance
capabilities.description: Displays a dense, one-line-per-worker view of active agents with status indicators and version info.

features.name: Worker Status Badges
features.rationale: Instantly communicates agent readiness and issues
features.description: Displays visual indicators for idle, busy, offline, or permission-waiting states.

behaviors.rationale: Visualizes active computation time and state
behaviors.summary: Shows a Lucide icon and color-coded badge representing the current agent state.
behaviors.detail: The UI renders a Lucide icon inside a colored chip that matches the state token (e.g., green for idle, amber for busy, red for offline). The icon rotates or changes shape to indicate activity or error conditions.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents timeout errors in long-running tasks
behaviors.summary: Updates timestamps globally via SSE to reflect elapsed busy time.
behaviors.detail: Instead of polling, the roster listens to a global SSE stream that updates a shared clock, ensuring all rows reflect the accurate time elapsed since the last inbound event without performance overhead.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces noise by hiding panic for normal stops
behaviors.summary: Handles clean exit state to distinguish from unexpected errors.
behaviors.detail: When a worker exits cleanly, the UI renders a desaturated gray badge with a dashed circle icon to indicate normal termination rather than a crash.

features.name: Worker Listing
features.rationale: Aggregates worker metadata into a scannable, sortable interface.
features.description: Presents a comprehensive grid of online agents showing version, state, and directory location.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the operator can verify fleet scale at a glance.
behaviors.summary: Displays active workers with metadata and allows sorting by any column header.
behaviors.detail: The interface renders a responsive table where columns such as Worker Name, State, and Context are sortable. It filters out offline agents and truncates long names with a tooltip to maintain layout integrity.

behaviors.rationale: Adapts layout constraints without losing essential status data.
behaviors.summary: Handles tablet and mobile viewports by hiding non-critical columns.
behaviors.detail: On tablet devices, the version and trash columns are hidden to prioritize state and context. On mobile, the grid collapses into a card layout showing only the most critical status indicators.

features.name: State Indicators
features.rationale: Instantly communicates agent health and output capture status to the user.
features.description: Visual badges and dots representing agent idle/busy/offline states and recording activity.
