behaviors.rationale: Alerts operators to agents that need attention or are stuck.
behaviors.summary: Differentiates between idle, busy, and offline states using color-coded badges.
behaviors.detail: Green dots indicate an idle agent. Amber pills indicate a busy agent, turning red if busy for over 5 minutes. Red dots indicate offline or errored agents. Tooltips show the precise duration of the current state.

behaviors.rationale: Confirms that telemetry is being captured as expected.
behaviors.summary: Visualizes active recording sessions with pulsing indicators.
behaviors.detail: A red 'REC' dot appears when an agent is actively recording events. If recording is active but no data is captured for 30 seconds, the indicator turns amber to warn the operator.

features.name: Context View
features.rationale: Provides the necessary scope information to understand what each agent is doing.
features.description: Displays the current project directory and shell context for each agent.

behaviors.rationale: Enables understanding of the environment where the agent operates.
behaviors.summary: Shows the working directory path for every connected agent.
behaviors.detail: The Context column displays the current shell path (e.g., /home/user/project). Long paths are truncated but remain accessible via a hover tooltip or mobile expansion.

behaviors.rationale: Makes abstract backend states visible to humans.
behaviors.summary: The interface renders the current status of all workers.
behaviors.detail: The UI fetches connection data from the backend and renders cards showing agent health, current task, and latency.

features.name: Project Grouping
features.rationale: Organizes the roster by logical workspace boundaries for better scannability.
features.description: Collapses workers running under the same project header.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces visual clutter by consolidating related workers.
behaviors.summary: Indents workers that share a parent project directory.
behaviors.detail: The UI uses indentation and collapsible arrows to group workers by their 'leanspecs' or other parent directories. Headers show session counts to indicate how many workers are in that group.

features.name: Worker Row
features.rationale: Provides fundamental information visibility for every managed agent.
features.description: Displays a single worker instance including its name, current process, and status indicators.

behaviors.rationale: Provides complete visibility into active fleet status.
behaviors.summary: Shows active worker details and status indicators in the roster table.
behaviors.detail: Each row represents a worker instance with columns for name, status, and recording activity. The recording column uses a red dot when recording is active, while the manager indicator uses a green dot. Columns are sortable to prioritize workers by name or state.

features.name: Sortable Headers
features.rationale: Enables operators to customize the view to prioritize relevant information.
features.description: Allows reordering of roster columns by name or state for better data presentation.

behaviors.rationale: Facilitates quick location of specific workers.
behaviors.summary: Clicking a column header sorts workers by that column's value.
behaviors.detail: Users can click the name or status column header to sort the roster list. This helps locate specific workers or group them by state when managing large fleets. The current sort order is indicated by the header style.

features.name: Roster View
features.rationale: Visualizes fleet availability for operators.
features.description: Displays the list of connected workers with status.

behaviors.rationale: Validates UI rendering of worker data.
behaviors.summary: Renders a list of workers with live status badges.
behaviors.detail: Updates badges via SSE stream when worker state changes.

behaviors.rationale: Enables efficient filtering and ordering of data.
behaviors.summary: Renders a sortable list of workers with status, context usage, and name.
behaviors.detail: The UI renders a table where columns can be sorted by name, status, or context percentage. Sorting handles null values by placing them last and uses the agent name as a tiebreaker. The context percentage is updated via periodic polling.

capabilities.name: Management Controls
capabilities.rationale: Offers a direct, high-level interface to control the fleet without CLI access.
capabilities.description: Provides interactive buttons to manage the lifecycle of agents, including recording and restart.

features.name: Recording Toggle
features.rationale: Enables audit trails and post-mortem analysis of agent sessions.
features.description: Allows operators to enable or disable session recording for a specific agent from the UI.

behaviors.rationale: Direct control over audit capabilities from the dashboard.
behaviors.summary: Toggles recording for a worker and displays feedback on active capture.
behaviors.detail: When the operator clicks the toggle, the system updates the recording state. If recording is active, the UI confirms the active file name and indicates if output is being captured.

features.name: Bearer Auth
features.rationale: Prevents unauthorized access to management endpoints.
features.description: Validates client identity using bearer tokens.

behaviors.rationale: Validates security gate logic.
behaviors.summary: Rejects requests without valid bearer tokens.
behaviors.detail: Returns 401 for missing or invalid tokens.

features.name: Path Traversal Protection
features.rationale: Stops requests targeting files outside the container.
features.description: Sanitizes inputs to prevent directory navigation attacks.

behaviors.rationale: Validates security hardening logic.
behaviors.summary: Blocks requests containing path traversal sequences.
behaviors.detail: Rejects worker names with dots-slash patterns.

features.name: Recording Controls
features.rationale: Gives operators control over telemetry capture scope.
features.description: Settings to enable, disable, or adjust recording thresholds for fleet agents.

behaviors.rationale: Establishes a clear baseline for agent visibility.
behaviors.summary: Manages global recording state for all connected agents.
behaviors.detail: The page provides inputs to toggle recording on/off globally. It displays a summary of active recordings and captured volume. Changes are applied instantly via live-save.

features.name: Navigation Controls
features.rationale: Offers essential lifecycle management for the terminal pane.
features.description: Provides buttons to pop out the terminal, reconnect the session, or close the specific pane.

behaviors.rationale: Allows viewing terminal output on a separate screen or full screen.
behaviors.summary: Opens the terminal in a new browser window.
behaviors.detail: The pop-out button triggers the creation of a new browser window. This window contains the terminal as the full viewport with a back-to-hub button and identical chrome strip functionality.

behaviors.rationale: Returns focus to the primary orchestration interface.
behaviors.summary: Closes the pop-out window and restores focus to the main hub.
behaviors.detail: The back-to-hub button closes the current pop-out window and navigates the active tab back to the main session view.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents accidental clicks on unnecessary UI elements.
behaviors.summary: Hides the reconnect button when the connection is healthy.
behaviors.detail: The system monitors the WebSocket connection state. If the connection is active, the reconnect button (rotate-cw icon) is hidden. It only appears when a disconnect event is detected.

behaviors.rationale: Allows cleanup of specific views without losing worker context.
behaviors.summary: Closes the current terminal pane without disconnecting the worker.
behaviors.detail: The close button closes the UI pane representing the terminal. The underlying worker process and its connection to the bus remain active for other panes or future reconnection.

capabilities.name: Navigation
capabilities.rationale: Groups all navigation logic into one thin layer to improve code reuse across projects.
capabilities.description: Provides a configurable sidebar to organize and access different application views like Workers and Settings.

features.name: Navigation Shell
features.rationale: Organizes complex management functions into digestible sections.
features.description: Provides the layout and navigation structure for the management UI.

behaviors.rationale: Essential for moving between different management contexts.
behaviors.summary: Renders the main application layout with accessible navigation tabs.
behaviors.detail: The UI presents tabs for the worker roster, permission inbox, saved flows, and settings. Users can switch between these views to manage different aspects of the fleet.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures consistent access to all features regardless of screen size.
behaviors.summary: Displays a persistent sidebar with active tab indicators and responsive collapse.
behaviors.detail: The sidebar acts as the primary navigation, using a blue left border to indicate active tabs. It supports sticky positioning and collapses to a horizontal nav on mobile devices. A footer is omitted, though a version identifier is present.

features.name: Keyboard Navigation
features.rationale: Accelerates the review process for operators managing many workers.
features.description: Enables rapid selection of requests using arrow keys and direct approve/deny keys.

behaviors.rationale: Efficient navigation for high-volume review workflows.
behaviors.summary: Focuses the next request in the list using the Down arrow key or 'j'.
behaviors.detail: The operator uses the Down arrow key or the letter 'j' to move the focus to the next permission request in the list. The focused item is highlighted, allowing the operator to quickly review multiple requests in sequence.

behaviors.rationale: Efficient navigation for high-volume review workflows.
behaviors.summary: Focuses the previous request in the list using the Up arrow key or 'k'.
behaviors.detail: The operator uses the Up arrow key or the letter 'k' to move the focus to the previous request in the list. This allows easy correction of navigation errors or quick jumping back to previously reviewed items.

behaviors.rationale: Enables high-speed approval workflows.
behaviors.summary: Approves the focused request using the 'y' key.
behaviors.detail: When the operator presses 'y', the focused request is selected for approval, triggering the queueing mechanism described in the Action Queueing capability. This allows for a rapid, muscle-memory-based approval workflow.

behaviors.rationale: Enables high-speed denial workflows.
behaviors.summary: Denies the focused request using the 'n' key.
behaviors.detail: When the operator presses 'n', the focused request is selected for denial, triggering the queueing mechanism. This allows for a rapid, muscle-memory-based denial workflow.

features.name: Grouping and Navigation
features.rationale: Organizes the fleet view by ownership or project scope
features.description: Groups workers by project and allows collapsing/expanding rows to manage dense lists.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces clutter by hiding irrelevant sections
behaviors.summary: Groups workers visually and allows collapsing headers.
behaviors.detail: Workers are grouped under collapsible headers corresponding to their project name. Clicking the header expands or collapses that section, maintaining a clean layout for large fleets.

features.name: Navigation and Layout
features.rationale: Provides structure and discoverability for different application sections.
features.description: Sidebar navigation with active indicators and responsive collapsing.

behaviors.rationale: Persistent navigation reduces clicks to return to specific areas.
behaviors.summary: Displays sidebar navigation with active route indicators.
behaviors.detail: The sidebar serves as the navbar, showing the active route with a blue left-border. It is sticky and collapses on mobile devices.

capabilities.name: Live Roster & State
capabilities.rationale: Operators need immediate visibility into fleet status without manual refreshing.
capabilities.description: Provides a real-time dashboard displaying active agents, their health, and operational states.

features.name: Agent State Monitor
features.rationale: Enables instant recognition of busy, idle, or failed agents.
features.description: Displays a persistent, live-updated list of all connected workers with their current status indicators.

behaviors.rationale: Eliminates the need for polling or manual refresh, reducing cognitive load.
behaviors.summary: Updates the roster UI in real-time when a worker changes state.
behaviors.detail: The system polls the agent registry or relies on WebSocket events to refresh the agent list immediately upon connection changes, ensuring the UI always reflects the actual fleet state.

features.name: Busy Duration Indicator
features.rationale: Helps operators identify agents stuck in long-running tasks or blocked states.
features.description: Visualizes how long an agent has been in a 'busy' state, distinguishing normal work from potential hangs.

behaviors.rationale: Provides immediate context on whether 'busy' implies work or a blockage.
behaviors.summary: Escalates visual warning for agents busy beyond a configurable threshold.
behaviors.detail: Agents marked as 'busy' for less than a standard duration appear with a neutral color, while those exceeding a longer threshold (e.g., 1 hour) display a bold, high-contrast warning.

features.name: Live state rendering
features.rationale: Eliminates need for manual polling by reacting to server-side events.
features.description: Automatically updates worker status badges (idle, busy, offline) as events arrive.

behaviors.rationale: Visual urgency helps operators prioritize workers currently being processed.
behaviors.summary: Displays an amber badge when a worker is busy and shows the time since the last status update.
behaviors.detail: Given a worker has an active request, When the roster component renders, Then display an amber 'busy' badge and increment a visual timer to indicate duration of inactivity.

behaviors.rationale: Differentiates between crash and graceful shutdown to guide recovery actions.
behaviors.summary: Shows a red or grey badge when SSE connection is lost, distinguishing between crash and clean exit.
behaviors.detail: Given no SSE events have arrived for over 5 seconds, When the UI refreshes, Then render the worker as offline. If the worker exited cleanly, display grey; otherwise, display red.

capabilities.name: Terminal Emulation
capabilities.rationale: Provides a familiar interface for command-line users to interact with the backend.
capabilities.description: Browser-based terminal interface for interacting with AI workers.

features.name: xterm.js Integration
features.rationale: Leverages existing terminal standards and user familiarity.
features.description: Embeds xterm.js to provide a terminal-like experience in the browser.

behaviors.rationale: Terminal emulation is the primary interface for CLI-centric workflows.
behaviors.summary: Displays output and accepts commands in a terminal pane.
behaviors.detail: The terminal pane renders output and accepts input using xterm.js, mimicking a native terminal. Scrollback is supported.

capabilities.name: Terminal View
capabilities.rationale: Core interface for executing and monitoring worker commands directly in the browser.
capabilities.description: Provides a real-time, interactive command-line interface for local AI workers within the browser.

features.name: Bidirectional Streaming
features.rationale: Eliminates latency inherent in polling mechanisms by using WebSocket binary frames.
features.description: Enables full duplex communication where keystrokes and output are streamed instantly between the browser and the worker process.

behaviors.rationale: Binary framing ensures efficient transmission of terminal data without unnecessary overhead.
behaviors.summary: Establishes a persistent WebSocket connection to stream binary data for input and output.
behaviors.detail: The terminal pane opens a WebSocket connection to the pty bridge URL. It listens for binary ArrayBuffer data representing raw stdout/stderr and sends keystrokes as binary frames. The connection maintains a 'connected' state until the WebSocket closes.

behaviors.rationale: Resizing based on canonical frames prevents race conditions and visual tearing.
behaviors.summary: Synchronizes terminal window dimensions with the worker process.
behaviors.detail: Upon connection, the terminal pane waits for a control message from the manager containing the canonical process dimensions (cols and rows). The xterm instance is resized to match this canonical size to prevent visual artifacts.

behaviors.rationale: Clear status feedback distinguishes between connecting, silent, and disconnected states.
behaviors.summary: Displays user interface feedback during connection states.
behaviors.detail: The UI displays a 'Connecting...' overlay while waiting for the first byte. It hides this overlay once a size message or any byte arrives. If silence persists after 4 seconds, a hint suggests restarting the worker.

behaviors.rationale: Respects browser security constraints while providing a seamless copy experience.
behaviors.summary: Handles clipboard operations for text selection and copying.
behaviors.detail: When the user selects text via mouse or Shift-Arrow, the system checks for a secure context to use the Clipboard API for copying. If unavailable, it falls back to the default xterm SIGINT behavior.

features.name: Web Terminal View
features.rationale: Allows process interaction without switching to an external terminal client.
features.description: Renders a persistent terminal session within the browser tab for command execution.

behaviors.rationale: Enables local debugging and control via the web interface.
behaviors.summary: Opens a functional terminal pane linked to a specific worker's process.
behaviors.detail: The terminal pane connects to the backend process group via a secure channel, allowing the operator to type commands and view output as if they were in a local terminal. If the WebAssembly or terminal bridge encounters an error, the view degrades to a read-only mode displaying the last known output.

capabilities.name: Saved Flow Editor
capabilities.rationale: Prepares the platform for future Quartermaster integration with persistent saved flows.
capabilities.description: A UI editor for creating and viewing named sequences of commands or scripts (flows).

features.name: Flow Sequence
features.rationale: Prepares architecture for future Quartermaster integration.
features.description: Visualizes and edits a chain of commands or scripts associated with a specific worker.

behaviors.rationale: Enables complex, repeatable automation sequences.
behaviors.summary: Displays a visual editor for editing a sequence of automation commands.
behaviors.detail: The editor allows the user to name a flow and edit the list of commands (MCP calls) that define the automation logic. Changes are persisted to server-side storage at `/data/flows/*.json`, ensuring data survives browser restarts.

features.name: Flow Editor
features.rationale: Provides the detailed context required to define agent interaction sequences.
features.description: Full-featured pane for editing flow logic, saving changes, and managing run history.

behaviors.rationale: Separating the list view from the editor provides sufficient workspace for complex definitions.
behaviors.summary: Loads flow definition into the main content area replacing the terminal.
behaviors.detail: Clicking 'Manage...' or navigating to an existing flow loads the detailed editor view into the main content pane. This view displays the flow's metadata (name, target worker) and a body area for defining the message/step sequence.

behaviors.rationale: Operators need to persist their work immediately after defining logic.
behaviors.summary: Saves the current flow definition.
behaviors.detail: The Save button persists the current flow configuration. Keyboard shortcut Ctrl+S triggers this action.

behaviors.rationale: Immediate execution capability allows for ad-hoc testing and debugging.
behaviors.summary: Executes the flow immediately.
behaviors.detail: The Run now button initiates the flow execution against the configured target worker. It uses the primary 'Send' style, is keyboard accessible via Ctrl+Enter.

behaviors.rationale: Operators need the ability to remove outdated or incorrect workflows.
behaviors.summary: Deletes a saved flow.
behaviors.detail: The Delete button permanently removes the flow definition from the system.

behaviors.rationale: Recent execution history provides immediate feedback on workflow stability.
behaviors.summary: Displays execution logs for the last few runs.
behaviors.detail: A run log section shows the last 5 executions with timestamps, status, duration, and a link to view full details.

behaviors.rationale: Keyboard-first interaction aligns with terminal user expectations.
behaviors.summary: Navigates flow list with keyboard.
behaviors.detail: Arrow keys navigate the flow list; Enter loads the editor; Ctrl+S saves; Ctrl+Enter runs the flow.

behaviors.rationale: Allows customization of workflow template identity.
behaviors.summary: The user can edit the flow name and default worker in the draft.
behaviors.detail: The editor provides input fields for the flow name and default worker. The name field is disabled if the flow was loaded from the hub (editing existing).

behaviors.rationale: Enables targeting specific workers for automated execution.
behaviors.summary: The user can edit the default worker for a flow.
behaviors.detail: The editor allows setting a default worker ID in the draft. This is used when running the flow if not explicitly specified.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents saving incomplete or invalid workflow templates.
behaviors.summary: The user can validate the flow before saving.
behaviors.detail: The save operation validates that the name and body are not empty. If empty, the save fails silently without changing the draft state.

behaviors.rationale: Creates persistent workflow templates for later reuse.
behaviors.summary: The user saves the current flow to the hub.
behaviors.detail: When name and body are valid, the draft is persisted to the hub and the editor updates to show the flow as saved and existing.

behaviors.rationale: Validates UI interaction with flow API.
behaviors.summary: Provides a form to define and save new flows.
behaviors.detail: Saves via API and lists available flows for selection.

behaviors.rationale: Facilitates maintenance of complex orchestration logic.
behaviors.summary: Opens a visual editor allowing steps to be appended, deleted, or reordered.
behaviors.detail: Given a flow, When the operator opens the editor, Then allow appending, deleting, or reordering steps. Each step is a worker and message pair.

features.name: Empty State Handling
features.rationale: Provides clear entry point for new users to save their first workflow.
features.description: Guidance and onboarding when no flows are saved yet.

behaviors.rationale: Guidance is essential for new users to discover the save feature.
behaviors.summary: Displays a centered icon and message instructing to save first flow.
behaviors.detail: If no flows exist, the editor shows a centered bookmark icon and text explaining how to save the current message as a flow using the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Shift+M. A link to documentation is included.

features.name: Flow Visualization
features.rationale: Makes the delegation graph visible for audit and design.
features.description: Renders the topology of agent-to-agent delegation paths.

behaviors.rationale: Provides a single source of truth for delegation logic.
behaviors.summary: Renders the active flow configuration.
behaviors.detail: The editor fetches the current flow definition from the backend and renders nodes and edges representing agents and their delegation relationships.

features.name: Flow List
features.rationale: Enables discovery and selection of existing workflow templates.
features.description: Displays a persisted list of saved workflow templates with names, last run timestamps, and creation controls.

behaviors.rationale: Handles empty state gracefully to guide user action.
behaviors.summary: The user sees an empty list until flows are created.
behaviors.detail: When no flows exist, the UI displays a placeholder message instructing the user to click the plus button to create their first flow.

behaviors.rationale: Allows initialization of new workflow templates.
behaviors.summary: The user can create a new empty flow template.
behaviors.detail: The user can click the plus button to create a new, unsaved flow draft, resetting the name and body to empty strings.

behaviors.rationale: Allows reuse and inspection of different workflow templates.
behaviors.summary: The user can navigate between existing saved flows.
behaviors.detail: Clicking a list item selects a previously saved flow, loading its name and body into the editor and resetting the run log view.

behaviors.rationale: Allows management of workflow template inventory.
behaviors.summary: The user can delete a saved flow from the list.
behaviors.detail: The user can delete a flow from the list, with a confirmation dialog that notes past run logs are preserved despite the flow deletion.

features.name: Run Flow
features.rationale: Triggers the orchestration of a defined workflow sequence on workers.
features.description: Executes a saved flow, polls for results, and displays the run log to the user.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures only validated workflows are executed.
behaviors.summary: The user can run a saved flow from the UI.
behaviors.detail: The user can initiate a run for a saved flow. If the flow is new (unsaved), the run is rejected until it is saved first.

behaviors.rationale: Provides visibility into the execution progress and results.
behaviors.summary: The user sees the run log while the flow executes.
behaviors.detail: Upon running, the UI polls the run log every 2 seconds until completion or a user timeout of 10 minutes. The log displays events and final results.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents UI freeze during extended worker operations.
behaviors.summary: The user handles long-running flow executions gracefully.
behaviors.detail: If a flow runs for over 10 minutes without a trailing outbound event, polling stops automatically to avoid freezing the UI.

capabilities.name: State Escalation
capabilities.rationale: Alerts users to prolonged system activity or idle states.
capabilities.description: Visual feedback for long-running processes or states.

features.name: Busy Cues
features.rationale: Helps operators identify potential bottlenecks or stuck agents.
features.description: Indicates when an agent has been busy for an extended period.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents silent failures by making long-running states visible.
behaviors.summary: Escalates visual cues for agents busy for more than 5 minutes.
behaviors.detail: The system should apply visual escalation for agents that remain busy beyond 5 minutes. This involves adding a CSS rule or conditional className to highlight the status, preventing silent timeout failures.

features.name: Recording Feedback
features.rationale: Indicates active recording without new data flow.
features.description: Shows when an agent is recording but currently silent.

behaviors.rationale: Alerts the user that recording is active but paused.
behaviors.summary: Displays an amber dot or tooltip when recording is active but no data is flowing.
behaviors.detail: If an agent is recording but has no bytes in the last 30 seconds, the system should display a warning indicator (amber dot) and a tooltip explaining the silent state.

features.name: Hot Reload
features.rationale: Ensures operators always see the latest UI and backend logic.
features.description: Mechanism to invalidate frontend caches upon server deployment without manual intervention.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces downtime and frustration after updates.
behaviors.summary: Invalidates the frontend asset cache when new code is deployed.
behaviors.detail: On a new deploy, invalidate the cache for the frontend. This ensures the operator sees the new UI without clearing browser history.

features.name: Disconnected Banner
features.rationale: Guides operators when their specific worker connection is severed.
features.description: Visual indicator when the pty connection is lost with a manual reconnect option.

behaviors.rationale: Clear communication of system state.
behaviors.summary: Displays a banner indicating the connection is lost and allows manual reconnection.
behaviors.detail: When the pty is disconnected, show a banner with a 'Reconnect' button. Clicking this requests a fresh ticket and reattaches the terminal.

capabilities.name: Clipboard Copy
capabilities.rationale: Enables sharing of logs and agent output to external tools.
capabilities.description: Mechanism for copying terminal output and flow results to clipboard.

features.name: Clipboard API Fallback
features.rationale: Ensures copy functionality is always available regardless of browser security flags.
features.description: Reliable copy function using Ctrl+Shift+C that works in all security contexts.

behaviors.rationale: The primary contract must be robust against browser security restrictions.
behaviors.summary: Copies selection to clipboard using Ctrl+Shift+C.
behaviors.detail: The primary copy shortcut Ctrl+Shift+C utilizes the Clipboard API or legacy execCommand fallback to copy selected text. This works in self-signed and standard HTTPS contexts.

features.name: Secure Context Enhancement
features.rationale: Allows users with valid certs to enjoy standard Ctrl+C copy behavior.
features.description: Optional improved copy behavior when running under a valid certificate.

behaviors.rationale: Secure contexts allow native OS copy behavior which feels more seamless.
behaviors.summary: Uses Ctrl+C to copy when running on valid HTTPS.
behaviors.detail: When the application detects a secure context (valid certificate) and a selection exists, Ctrl+C triggers the Clipboard API copy action. If not secure or no selection, Ctrl+C performs standard SIGINT.

features.name: Security Status Indicator
features.rationale: Informs operators of the current security mode and copy availability.
features.description: Visual indicator showing certificate status and copy method.

behaviors.rationale: Transparency helps operators understand why Ctrl+C might not copy on some machines.
behaviors.summary: Displays security status pill in the status bar.
behaviors.detail: A small pill in the status bar shows an icon and text indicating 'trusted' or 'self-signed' along with the required shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+C). Clicking it shows help docs.

capabilities.name: Notification Toast
capabilities.rationale: Allows operators to respond to requests even when the application is in the background.
capabilities.description: Desktop notifications that alert the operator when a new permission request arrives.

features.name: Browser Alert
features.rationale: Ensures permission requests are noticed without tab focus.
features.description: Triggers a system toast notification when a permission event is received.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces latency between request generation and human response.
behaviors.summary: Fires a browser notification when a permission request lands.
behaviors.detail: When the backend detects a `permission_request` event for a known agent, the frontend sends a notification via the Browser Notifications API. A toast appears on the screen indicating a new request is waiting for review in the inbox.

features.name: Notification Support
features.rationale: Enables one-way communication for events like cancellation or logging.
features.description: Sends asynchronous notifications without expecting a response, optionally including parameters.

behaviors.rationale: Allows fire-and-forget events like agent cancellation.
behaviors.summary: Sends a notification to the transport.
behaviors.detail: Constructs a message with jsonrpc version and method name; if provided, appends a params dictionary to the message before dispatching it.

capabilities.name: Integrated Terminal
capabilities.rationale: Provides an alternative to CLI for local process interaction and debugging.
capabilities.description: An embedded terminal interface within the web UI to inspect and control agent processes directly.

features.name: Reconnect Strategy
features.rationale: Ensures continuity of the session while accepting that scrollback is live-only.
features.description: Reattaches the terminal to a fresh session with a blank scrollback upon reconnection.

behaviors.rationale: Restores the live stream; historical output is not replayed.
behaviors.summary: Reconnects the terminal to a live pty with a blank screen after the client renews its ticket.
behaviors.detail: Given a WebSocket disconnect, When the client requests a new ticket and reconnects, Then reattach the terminal to the live pty and clear the client-side scrollback.

features.name: Shift+Enter
features.rationale: Enables complex scripts to be written in a single flow without manual line breaks.
features.description: Processes hard newlines to allow multi-paragraph command entry.

behaviors.rationale: Crucial for entering scripts with multiple logical paragraphs.
behaviors.summary: Sends a hard newline to the pty when Shift+Enter is pressed, preventing submission.
behaviors.detail: Given focus in the terminal, When the operator presses Shift+Enter, Then send the modifier-held newline sequence so Ink reads it as a line break, not a command submit.

features.name: Smart Ctrl+C
features.rationale: Respects standard OS copy-paste expectations while maintaining terminal control.
features.description: Selects text to clipboard when Ctrl+C is pressed if text is selected, otherwise sends interrupt.

behaviors.rationale: Leverages existing selection state to improve UX.
behaviors.summary: Copies selected text to the OS clipboard and skips interrupt signal; otherwise sends interrupt.
behaviors.detail: Given a selection exists, When Ctrl+C is pressed, Then write the selection to the OS clipboard. Given no selection, send the interrupt signal.

features.name: Input Handling
features.rationale: Enables the user to interactively control the agent as if connected via SSH.
features.description: Accepts user keystrokes and multi-line commands to execute on the remote worker.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents accidental line breaks in code blocks.
behaviors.summary: The terminal accepts a Shift+Enter sequence to submit the current line without corruption.
behaviors.detail: When the user holds Shift and presses Enter, the system interprets this as a command submit event rather than a new line break, ensuring multi-line input is handled correctly.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures code integrity during paste operations.
behaviors.summary: The terminal handles pasted text without corruption.
behaviors.detail: When the user pastes a large block of text or code into the terminal, the system accepts the bracketed paste or raw input and displays it exactly as pasted.

features.name: Resizing Support
features.rationale: Maintains the illusion of a connected Pseudo-Terminal device regardless of window size.
features.description: Dynamically adjusts the terminal layout when the application window or tab resizes.

behaviors.rationale: Provides a responsive and flexible user experience.
behaviors.summary: The terminal window resizes smoothly when the browser window changes size.
behaviors.detail: When the user resizes the TubeMail window, the system sends the new window size to the worker process and updates the internal grid to fit the new dimensions.

features.name: Terminal Streaming
features.rationale: Provides real-time visual feedback of agent execution in the browser.
features.description: Sends raw terminal bytes and control messages from the worker manager to attached browser clients.

behaviors.rationale: Delivers raw terminal content instantly to all viewing clients.
behaviors.summary: Streams binary terminal output frames to attached browser clients.
behaviors.detail: The system receives binary data from the manager side and fans it to every registered client queue associated with a specific worker. Frames are dispatched as binary WebSocket events for immediate rendering in the xterm-like terminal emulator.

behaviors.rationale: Informs UI of state changes without disrupting the streaming session.
behaviors.summary: Delivers control messages as JSON text frames to clients.
behaviors.detail: System control events, such as terminal size updates or manager exit notices, are serialized into JSON and sent via text WebSocket frames. This allows the UI to update metadata without requiring new connections.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures resources are allocated only when clients are actively viewing.
behaviors.summary: Manages client attachment and detachment for streaming workers.
behaviors.detail: When a browser connects, the system registers a new client queue for that worker. When the browser disconnects, the client queue is removed. The system tracks the count of attached clients to determine if the worker stream should continue.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures audit trails and history are captured without manual client intervention.
behaviors.summary: Supports persistent recording by treating a recorder as a client.
behaviors.detail: If a recorder is configured for a worker, the system treats it as an active consumer. Even if no browser clients are attached, the recorder ensures the stream continues, preventing the manager from stopping output prematurely.

behaviors.rationale: Protects the session from failure on slow or unresponsive clients.
behaviors.summary: Buffers output to avoid overwhelming slow browser clients.
behaviors.detail: Each client queue has a maximum size limit. When the queue is full, the system drops new binary frames but sends a soft-close signal. This prevents the connection from being flooded with backlogged data that might be discarded.

features.name: Client Queue Management
features.rationale: Prevents cross-talk between multiple concurrent terminal sessions.
features.description: Maintains separate queues per worker and client to isolate streaming streams.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures isolation and data integrity for concurrent users.
behaviors.summary: Associates a unique queue with each client per worker.
behaviors.detail: The registry maintains a dictionary mapping workers to a list of client queues. Each queue is an asyncio.Queue specifically for one client instance, ensuring that output sent to one user does not interfere with another.

behaviors.rationale: Gracefully handles backpressure from slow consumers.
behaviors.summary: Drops excess frames when a client buffer is full.
behaviors.detail: If a client cannot consume data fast enough, the queue fills. The system attempts to send new frames via put_nowait. If that fails, it logs a warning and attempts to send an empty buffer to signal a soft close before failing again.

features.name: Recorder Integration
features.rationale: Provides a backup and audit mechanism for terminal sessions.
features.description: Optionally routes terminal chunks to a recording manager for persistent storage.

behaviors.rationale: Preserves session history independently of client availability.
behaviors.summary: Writes terminal chunks to the recording manager when active.
behaviors.detail: Before or during fan-out to browser clients, the system optionally writes binary chunks to a recording manager. This ensures that even if all browser clients detach or drop frames due to buffer limits, the historical record remains intact on disk.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains primary functionality despite auxiliary subsystem failures.
behaviors.summary: Fails safely if the recorder is unavailable.
behaviors.detail: If writing to the recorder fails, the system logs a warning but continues to fan output to browser clients. This ensures that a slow or broken recorder does not interrupt the live viewing experience.

capabilities.name: Flow Shell
capabilities.rationale: Stores common operational patterns as reusable named flows.
capabilities.description: UI editor and manager for saving, editing, and replaying multi-step orchestration flows.

features.name: Flow CRUD
features.rationale: Allows operators to persist complex sequences for easy reuse.
features.description: Create, read, update, and delete named flow definitions stored on the hub.

behaviors.rationale: Encapsulates operational knowledge into reusable assets.
behaviors.summary: Persists a new flow definition to the hub and makes it available for execution.
behaviors.detail: Given a flow body and a name, When saved, Then persist the data on the hub under the name key. Then it appears in the UI dropdown and MCP tool output.

behaviors.rationale: Automates repetitive multi-step tasks.
behaviors.summary: Executes a saved flow against a target worker and logs the run history.
behaviors.detail: Given a saved flow name and a target worker, When invoked, Then deliver the flow body to the worker. Persist a run log on the hub.

features.name: Run Log Viewer
features.rationale: Provides auditability for completed automation runs.
features.description: Displays the chronological history of events from a past flow execution.

behaviors.rationale: Helps debug why a flow succeeded or failed.
behaviors.summary: Shows the timeline of events for a specific flow run.
behaviors.detail: Given a past run, When the operator opens it, Then display the timeline of inbound and reply events per step with timestamps.

features.name: SPA Mounting
features.rationale: Presents the main UI interface to users.
features.description: Mounts the single-page application via FastAPI.

behaviors.rationale: Provides user interface layer.
behaviors.summary: Serves the SPA UI over HTTP.
behaviors.detail: Mounts the SPA at the root path with FastAPI.

capabilities.name: Live-Reload
capabilities.rationale: Accelerates iteration cycles by reducing time cost for multi-week UI builds and state sync.
capabilities.description: Automatically refreshes the UI to reflect recent state changes without manual page refresh.

features.name: State Synchronization
features.rationale: Eliminates stale data and manual refresh actions.
features.description: Pushes updated worker states to the UI immediately when events occur in the backend.

behaviors.rationale: Materially changes the time-cost of UI iteration cycles.
behaviors.summary: Updates the UI view when the underlying state changes due to new events.
behaviors.detail: The system listens for hub events and updates the local DOM. This ensures the UI always reflects the current status of workers, even if the user is away or the page has been idle.

capabilities.name: Management UI
capabilities.rationale: Operators need a GUI to visualize status and manage the fleet.
capabilities.description: Visual interface to monitor workers, manage sessions, and configure settings.

features.name: Terminal Session Manager
features.rationale: Allows operators to view and control worker terminals visually.
features.description: Manages attachment to and detachment from interactive PTY sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Operators need to know if a terminal is in use.
behaviors.summary: Shows badge indicating number of clients attached to a worker.
behaviors.detail: The UI fetches the count of active PTY clients for each worker and displays it as a badge. It updates this count whenever a client attaches or detaches.

capabilities.name: Recording Console
capabilities.rationale: Allows deep inspection of agent behavior and debugging of specific sessions.
capabilities.description: Provides a specialized view to inspect and replay recorded agent sessions.

features.name: Session Playback
features.rationale: Enables review of past agent interactions for debugging or training.
features.description: Displays recorded command logs and agent outputs in a scrollable console.

behaviors.rationale: Brings the recording data from storage into the user's workflow.
behaviors.summary: Retrieves and displays the contents of a recording file for the user.
behaviors.detail: The operator can request a specific recording file; the system reads the data and renders the command logs and agent responses in a text-based console view.

capabilities.name: Responsive Layout
capabilities.rationale: Ensures usability on mobile and tablet devices.
capabilities.description: Adaptation of the interface to different screen sizes.

features.name: Device Adaptation
features.rationale: Optimizes space usage for various form factors.
features.description: Adjusts layout for mobile, tablet, and desktop.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures all critical data remains visible and accessible.
behaviors.summary: Collapses roster data on mobile to prevent off-screen content.
behaviors.detail: On mobile and tablet, the roster collapses to a card layout. Tablet views may cut off specific columns like context if not adjusted, requiring media queries to handle responsive constraints effectively.

capabilities.name: Settings
capabilities.rationale: Centralized control over system behavior and resource usage.
capabilities.description: Global configuration page for managing recording defaults and storage limits.

features.name: Config Management
features.rationale: Allows tuning of system behavior to match operator workflows.
features.description: Manages persistent settings for the hub, including recording defaults.

behaviors.rationale: Enables customization of the tool environment.
behaviors.summary: Saves user preferences that affect all future operations.
behaviors.detail: Changes to recording defaults, storage limits, or other behaviors are stored in a key-value store and read by the service on startup or on-demand.

features.name: Session Lifecycle
features.rationale: Ensures workers eventually disconnect to save resources.
features.description: Controls for managing worker session timeouts and cleanup policies.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains resource efficiency by cleaning up stale connections.
behaviors.summary: Configures idle timeout for worker sessions.
behaviors.detail: An input field allows the operator to define how long a session lasts after the last event. This prevents 'ghost' sessions from consuming resources indefinitely.

features.name: Recording Toggle
features.rationale: Allows operators to control the verbosity of the logging stream.
features.description: Enables or disables the default recording behavior for new sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Default settings apply automatically to new sessions.
behaviors.summary: Changes the default state for recording new sessions.
behaviors.detail: The system updates the global preference to enable or disable recording for subsequent workers.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures consistent recording behavior for new workers while respecting legacy configurations.
behaviors.summary: Newly registered workers automatically start recording if the global default is enabled.
behaviors.detail: If recording_enabled_by_default is true, all new workers begin recording immediately upon registration. Existing workers retain their individual per-worker settings regardless of this global flag.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents unintended recording when global defaults are turned off, respecting explicit overrides.
behaviors.summary: Workers retain individual recording settings if the global default is disabled.
behaviors.detail: If recording_enabled_by_default is false, new workers start with recording disabled unless an explicit per-worker setting overrides it.

features.name: Global Settings
features.rationale: Tune system behavior.
features.description: Configure recording defaults and user preferences.

behaviors.rationale: Set default recording policy.
behaviors.summary: Configures recording defaults.
behaviors.detail: The settings page allows operators to set a global toggle for default recording on new workers, along with file size and retention limits.

behaviors.rationale: End user session securely.
behaviors.summary: Manages user session.
behaviors.detail: The settings page provides a sign-out function to clear the bearer token from local storage.

behaviors.rationale: Permits runtime configuration adjustments.
behaviors.summary: Users can view and modify configuration settings.
behaviors.detail: The settings page exposes configuration options for the control bus.

behaviors.rationale: Manages preferences.
behaviors.summary: Shows and saves configuration options for the hub.
behaviors.detail: The interface presents editable fields for hub settings and persists changes to the local or remote configuration store.

features.name: Recording Settings
features.rationale: Enables operators to manage recording behavior and disk usage efficiently.
features.description: Configures default recording state, maximum file size per record, and retention count.

behaviors.rationale: Provides flexible recording configuration for diverse use cases.
behaviors.summary: Sets default recording state and file management policies.
behaviors.detail: The settings page includes three knobs for recording defaults: enable by default, maximum file size, and number of files to keep. When files reach the size limit, the oldest files are garbage collected automatically. These settings persist across hub restarts in the hub configuration file.

features.name: Hub Settings
features.rationale: Supports deployment-specific customizations.
features.description: Edits hub configuration and appearance preferences.

behaviors.rationale: Simplifies operational maintenance.
behaviors.summary: Retrieves and saves hub configuration.
behaviors.detail: The user can modify hub settings like the Git SHA for versioning or other display metadata. Changes are persisted and reflect immediately in the UI.

features.name: Settings Tab
features.rationale: Ensures critical configuration options are always reachable regardless of other tab states.
features.description: Pins the Settings tab to the bottom of the sidebar for permanent visibility.

behaviors.rationale: Distinguishes permanent tools from temporary navigation items.
behaviors.summary: Renders the Settings tab in a fixed position at the bottom of the sidebar.
behaviors.detail: The component accepts a separate array for bottom tabs. These items are rendered below a spacer, visually distinct from the main navigation group.

features.name: Recording File Rotation Size
features.rationale: Prevents excessive memory or disk usage by capping individual recording file sizes.
features.description: Defines the maximum file size before recording data is rotated to a new file.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures consistent file sizes for easier storage management and playback.
behaviors.summary: Recording files are rotated when they exceed the configured maximum bytes.
behaviors.detail: The hub monitors active recording files and creates a new file when the current one surpasses recording_max_bytes_per_file.

features.name: Recording File Retention Count
features.rationale: Controls disk usage by limiting the number of historical recording files stored per worker.
features.description: Specifies the maximum number of recording files retained per worker before deletion.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents disk exhaustion by enforcing a hard limit on retained recording files.
behaviors.summary: Excess recording files are deleted when the retention limit is reached.
behaviors.detail: The hub enforces a per-worker cap on recording file retention, deleting the oldest files when the count exceeds recording_keep_files.

features.name: Settings Panel
features.rationale: Customizes the experience to user preference and environment needs.
features.description: Global configuration for the UI shell, including theme and connection settings.

behaviors.rationale: Improves comfort for long-duration usage.
behaviors.summary: Allows modification of global preferences like theme and debug flags.
behaviors.detail: The panel stores configuration in local storage. Changes are applied immediately without reloading the page.

behaviors.rationale: Allows operators to tune the system to their specific needs.
behaviors.summary: Displays and allows editing of platform configuration.
behaviors.detail: The UI shows current settings like timeouts, retry policies, and allows modification of these values.

behaviors.rationale: Centralizes administration of the control bus.
behaviors.summary: The interface allows modification of system-wide settings.
behaviors.detail: The UI provides a form to input values for timeouts, retry policies, and worker limits, which are then pushed to the backend config.

capabilities.name: Web UI
capabilities.rationale: Inherit the cross-cutting browser shell — navigation, settings, shared chrome that isn't tied to one backend cap.
capabilities.description: Product-specific cross-cutting UI shell + settings. Distinct from the UI-mirror caps at ui:1/2/3 which each mirror a single mcp cap.

features.name: Status Monitor
features.rationale: Allows quick verification of fleet integrity without logs.
features.description: Displays real-time list of active workers and their health status.

behaviors.rationale: Essential for operator situational awareness.
behaviors.summary: Queries the backend for a list of active processes and renders them as cards.
behaviors.detail: The UI fetches the current state of the control bus and polls for updates. Each worker is displayed with its connection status, process ID, and a heartbeat indicator.

features.name: Log Viewer
features.rationale: Enables debugging of remote sessions directly in the browser.
features.description: Renders the terminal output stream from a selected worker session.

behaviors.rationale: Makes remote debugging intuitive for humans.
behaviors.summary: Binds a terminal pane to the WebSocket stream of a specific worker.
behaviors.detail: Clicking on a worker in the list focuses the output pane on that session. The pane renders text output with syntax highlighting, handling long lines and scrolling.

features.name: Branding
features.rationale: Establishes the tool identity.
features.description: Text-based wordmark logo and minimal visual identity.

behaviors.rationale: Provides simple, effective identification for the tool.
behaviors.summary: Uses a text-based 'tubemail' wordmark in the header without a graphical logo.
behaviors.detail: The application relies on the text wordmark 'tubemail' in the sidebar for branding. While it works on light and dark backgrounds, a favicon is currently missing, leaving browser tabs indistinguishable.

features.name: Dashboard
features.rationale: Gives the operator a quick view of the entire fleet status.
features.description: Displays the roster of managed workers and their current states.

behaviors.rationale: The roster is the central navigation hub for the operator.
behaviors.summary: Lists active workers and their status indicators.
behaviors.detail: The UI generates a row for each worker, displaying connection status and activity levels.

features.name: Status Visualization
features.rationale: Offers a quick visual summary of fleet health.
features.description: Renders the current state of all connected workers.

behaviors.rationale: Quick check for fleet health at a glance.
behaviors.summary: Displays the online/offline status of workers.
behaviors.detail: Given the backend reports worker status, When the page renders, Then the UI shows a list of workers with their current status indicators.

features.name: Fleet Overview
features.rationale: Gives operators instant visibility into system health.
features.description: Displays real-time status of all connected workers.

behaviors.rationale: Satisfies the need for immediate situational awareness.
behaviors.summary: Lists active workers with their current state.
behaviors.detail: Polls the underlying MCP servers and renders a table showing worker IDs, connection status, and last known activity.

features.name: Terminal Panel
features.rationale: Allows direct interaction with agent environments.
features.description: Provides an integrated terminal for command execution.

behaviors.rationale: Validates xterm.js integration.
behaviors.summary: Displays and accepts text input in a terminal pane.
behaviors.detail: Supports copy, hard-newlines, and zoom controls.

features.name: Task Queue
features.rationale: Shows operator visibility into backlogs.
features.description: Displays a live view of tasks waiting in the worker queues.

behaviors.rationale: Helps prioritize high-priority work.
behaviors.summary: Renders a table of queued tasks with estimated wait times.
behaviors.detail: The UI polls the hub for pending tasks in the event loop, displays them in a scrollable table, and indicates which workers are blocked or processing the longest tasks.

capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Shell-level UI actions must call an MCP tool — no server-side logic outside MCP.

capabilities.name: Interactive Interface
capabilities.rationale: Provides a visual layer for managing agents via a web interface.
capabilities.description: A UI mirror that reflects the capabilities of the MCP backend tools.

features.name: Visual Agent Status
features.rationale: Makes the state of the fleet visible to human operators.
features.description: Displays the current status and health of managed agent workers.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures operators always see real-time information.
behaviors.summary: Updates the UI to reflect agent status changes.
behaviors.detail: When an agent's state changes, the UI automatically updates to show the new status without manual refresh.

features.name: Interactive Reconnection
features.rationale: Automates recovery of disconnected sessions.
features.description: Executes keyboard simulations to reconnect agents to the main stream without manual intervention.

behaviors.rationale: Automates the manual recovery steps for operators.
behaviors.summary: Navigates and interacts with the agent's TUI to perform a reconnection sequence.
behaviors.detail: The tool simulates keystrokes (arrow keys and Enter) based on screen parsing. It monitors for specific text matches in the TUI, such as the 'Reconnect' option. It validates cursor movement after each arrow press to ensure correct navigation and detects the correct menu option dynamically rather than assuming a fixed order. It handles connection timeouts by extending wait times if the dialog does not appear immediately.

features.name: Interactive Shell
features.rationale: Enables automation scripting and quick manual checks for engineers.
features.description: A command-line interface that accepts text commands and displays formatted output.

behaviors.rationale: CLI users expect immediate stdout feedback for parsing.
behaviors.summary: Dispatches a fleet status command to the MCP server.
behaviors.detail: The CLI parses the user input, constructs the appropriate RPC call, sends it to the control bus, and prints the JSON response to stdout.

behaviors.rationale: Provides low-latency direct access to worker execution.
behaviors.summary: Launches a WebSocket-connected terminal pane.
behaviors.detail: The UI loads the xterm.js library and establishes a WebSocket connection to the target worker's console, forwarding output and accepting input streams.

features.name: Interactive Input
features.rationale: Enables users to run arbitrary commands on the local worker context.
features.description: Allows users to type commands and interact directly with the remote shell process.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures every keystroke is transmitted reliably to the running process.
behaviors.summary: Captures and transmits keyboard input to the worker process.
behaviors.detail: Keystrokes captured by xterm are encoded into terminal bytes and sent through the WebSocket connection. The worker process receives these bytes and processes them as if the user were typing on a local terminal.

behaviors.rationale: Long scrollback allows operators to audit command history without re-running commands.
behaviors.summary: Maintains persistent scrollback for command history.
behaviors.detail: The terminal retains a scrollback buffer of 5000 lines. Users can scroll back through the output history to review previous commands and outputs without losing context.

behaviors.rationale: Preserves user preference for readability across different browser sessions.
behaviors.summary: Adjusts font size based on user preferences.
behaviors.detail: The terminal font size defaults to 14 but reads a stored preference from localStorage. The user can adjust this setting, which is saved and restored for subsequent sessions.

capabilities.name: UI Rendering
capabilities.rationale: Presents backend worker states to end users visually.
capabilities.description: Web UI components that render worker status badges.

features.name: State Badge Component
features.rationale: Encapsulates logic to display worker state consistently.
features.description: A reusable UI component that renders the status badge for a worker.

behaviors.rationale: Simple inputs yield the correct visual output.
behaviors.summary: Renders badge with label and icon.
behaviors.detail: The component takes the worker state and busy duration as props. It renders a text label alongside a selected icon based on the current state.

behaviors.rationale: CSS classes allow for efficient state management.
behaviors.summary: Applies conditional CSS classes.
behaviors.detail: The component applies specific CSS classes based on the worker state to style the badge appropriately, such as changing colors or opacity.

features.name: Terminal Output Rendering
features.rationale: Provides visual feedback of the agent's execution state.
features.description: Transmits binary terminal output bytes from the manager to the browser client for rendering.

behaviors.rationale: Enables real-time monitoring.
behaviors.summary: Streams binary output frames from the manager to the browser for immediate rendering.
behaviors.detail: The system receives binary frames from the manager. These frames contain raw pseudo-terminal output which is sent over the WebSocket to the browser. The browser uses xterm.js to render these bytes, displaying the agent's logs and output in real time.

behaviors.rationale: Users expect standard terminal styling.
behaviors.summary: The terminal correctly renders text, colors, and cursor movements within the UI frame.
behaviors.detail: The system accepts raw terminal escape sequences and maps them to DOM updates, supporting color palettes, bold text, and cursor positioning within the visible viewport.

features.name: TUI Rendering
features.rationale: Delivers an immersive experience that mimics the native terminal environment for users.
features.description: Renders a high-fidelity terminal environment within the UI.

behaviors.rationale: Critical for maintaining a consistent and usable terminal experience.
behaviors.summary: Renders terminal output with proper colors, cursors, and resizing support.
behaviors.detail: The system ensures that colors and cursor positions are correctly rendered and tracks them accurately across different screen sizes. It supports alternate screen modes and handles resize events to ensure the terminal content adapts seamlessly to the user's view.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures that user input is captured and executed as intended.
behaviors.summary: Handles keyboard input including enter and paste operations.
behaviors.detail: The system supports sending key combinations like Shift+Enter to submit commands and handles bracketed paste mode for bulk input. It ensures that input is captured accurately and processed without corruption or loss of data.

features.name: Sidebar Rendering
features.rationale: Centralizes navigation state management to reduce redundancy in the main application code.
features.description: Displays a structured navigation menu with labels, badges, and version info based on provided configuration.

behaviors.rationale: Provides visual feedback for navigation state and item counts.
behaviors.summary: Renders a vertical navigation sidebar with active state indicators and count badges.
behaviors.detail: The component accepts a list of main tabs and bottom tabs, rendering them with distinct styling. It highlights the currently active tab and displays optional numeric badges for pending items if the count is greater than zero.

behaviors.rationale: Allows users to verify which software version is currently running.
behaviors.summary: Fetches and displays the application version number in the footer.
behaviors.detail: On mount, the component fetches the health check endpoint. If successful, it extracts the version string from the JSON response and displays it below the main navigation list.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures navigation state is consistent across the entire application boundary.
behaviors.summary: Delegates tab switching actions to parent callbacks.
behaviors.detail: Instead of managing tab state internally, the component triggers the parent's onTabChange handler when a user clicks a tab item.

capabilities.name: Chrome Strip
capabilities.rationale: Concise control surface for worker context and state management.
capabilities.description: A sticky top-bar component providing metadata, status indicators, and navigation controls for the active terminal workspace.

features.name: Worker Identity
features.rationale: Keeps the operator aware of the active worker identity at all times.
features.description: Displays the name of the currently active worker and allows navigation to the roster upon clicking.

behaviors.rationale: Enables easy switching between workers via navigation.
behaviors.summary: Renders the active worker name in the strip.
behaviors.detail: The component receives the active worker ID from the core MCP. It renders a text label with the worker name. Clicking this label triggers a navigation event to the roster view.

features.name: Session Status
features.rationale: Provides immediate visibility into worker load and duration.
features.description: Shows the current state badge (e.g., busy) and the elapsed time since the session started.

behaviors.rationale: Communicates worker activity to the operator.
behaviors.summary: Updates the state badge to reflect the worker's current state.
behaviors.detail: The system subscribes to state updates from the worker. If the worker is processing a task, the badge displays 'busy' with a timer. If idle, it shows 'idle' (if implemented) or remains quiet.

features.name: Attachment Counter
features.rationale: Indicates the scope of the current orchestration context.
features.description: Displays a counter for attached workers when multiple workers are linked to the session.

behaviors.rationale: Clarifies multi-worker context without noise when unnecessary.
behaviors.summary: Shows the count of attached workers when greater than one.
behaviors.detail: The system tracks the number of workers attached to the current bus session. The indicator 'N attached' is rendered only if N > 1. If N <= 1, the indicator is hidden to avoid clutter.

capabilities.name: Pop-out Window
capabilities.rationale: Enables full-screen terminal access and cross-device usage.
capabilities.description: A full-screen terminal view opened in a separate browser window with minimal chrome.

features.name: Full Viewport Terminal
features.rationale: Maximizes available space for command input and output reading.
features.description: Renders the terminal as the entire viewport within the new window without sidebars or navigation.

behaviors.rationale: Optimizes space for the primary task of viewing output.
behaviors.summary: Displays the terminal in full width and height.
behaviors.detail: The pop-out window removes all non-terminal components. The layout consists solely of the chrome strip at the top and the xterm.js terminal filling the remaining space.

features.name: Persistent Zoom Profile
features.rationale: Ensures consistent readability across different terminal contexts.
features.description: Shares font size settings between embedded and pop-out views for the same worker.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces cognitive load by maintaining user preferences.
behaviors.summary: Applies the saved zoom setting for a specific worker to the pop-out.
behaviors.detail: The system reads the zoom setting stored in localStorage for the specific worker name. When opening a pop-out, it applies this setting. The value persists across sessions for that worker.

capabilities.name: Terminal Pane
capabilities.rationale: Mirrors the raw output of the agent to the user for immediate interaction.
capabilities.description: A UI component that mounts the remote agent's terminal interface directly in the browser.

features.name: Remote Mount
features.rationale: Brings the agent's stdout directly to the operator's view.
features.description: Establishes a view of the remote agent's terminal within the browser tab.

behaviors.rationale: Visualizing the terminal is the primary interaction model.
behaviors.summary: Displays the remote agent's output stream.
behaviors.detail: The UI renders the text output from the remote process, updating in real-time as the agent executes.

features.name: Terminal Pane Background
features.rationale: Provides a familiar, comfortable coding environment
features.description: Uses a dark terminal color calibrated for GitHub to reduce eye strain in dark environments.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces eye fatigue during long sessions
behaviors.summary: Renders output with a dark background and light text.
behaviors.detail: The terminal pane uses a dark gray background (#0d1117) with light gray text (#c9d1d9) to match industry standards for code viewers, ensuring readability in low-light settings.

behaviors.rationale: Enables direct command interaction from the UI.
behaviors.summary: Opens a terminal interface connected to a worker's shell process.
behaviors.detail: Opening the terminal pane connects the browser to the worker's PTY session. Users can paste multi-paragraph work orders using Shift+Enter to create new lines. The terminal remains connected during orchestration tasks, allowing continuous monitoring.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures smooth workflow continuation without session conflicts.
behaviors.summary: Closes non-web terminals to allow full orchestration workflows.
behaviors.detail: Non-web terminal sessions can be closed while keeping the orchestration capability intact. This prevents interference with other management operations while maintaining visibility into worker states.

capabilities.name: Background Notifications
capabilities.rationale: Breaks the "sit on the browser tab" assumption and allows monitoring of idle agents.
capabilities.description: Alerts the operator to critical events occurring when the tab is not active.

features.name: Desktop Alerts
features.rationale: Ensures the operator is aware of issues even when not actively watching the UI.
features.description: Sends system-level notifications for important events like critical errors or timeouts.

behaviors.rationale: Closes the practical gap in the "sit on the browser tab" assumption.
behaviors.summary: Triggers a desktop notification when a critical event occurs outside the active tab.
behaviors.detail: The backend detects critical events (e.g., `status_state=busy` timeout). If the UI tab is inactive, a native desktop notification is pushed to the OS.

capabilities.name: UI Dashboard
capabilities.rationale: Provides the interface for operators to manage the fleet.
capabilities.description: Visualizes worker roster, context limits, and permission queues.

features.name: Permission Queue
features.rationale: Prevents unauthorized tool usage visually.
features.description: Shows pending tool approval requests requiring operator action.

behaviors.rationale: Enables rapid security decisions.
behaviors.summary: Dashboard displays pending permission requests for review.
behaviors.detail: The UI lists pending permission requests with tool details and inputs. Operators can approve or deny these directly from the interface.

capabilities.name: UI Mirrors
capabilities.rationale: Visualizes backend functionality in the user interface.
capabilities.description: Frontends that directly mirror the capabilities of the backend MCP tools.

features.name: Task Console
features.rationale: Complements the Task Dispatch MCP tool for debugging.
features.description: Allows users to view logs and history of dispatched tasks.

behaviors.rationale: Enables post-mortem analysis of agent actions.
behaviors.summary: The interface displays the history and logs of recent tasks.
behaviors.detail: The UI queries the task database and presents a scrollable list of executed commands and their resulting outputs.

capabilities.name: Browser SSE
capabilities.rationale: Allows direct browser connectivity where custom headers are not allowed.
capabilities.description: Supports SSE streams in browsers using query-string tokens for compatibility.

features.name: Query Token Auth
features.rationale: Works around browser security restrictions on custom headers.
features.description: Accepts tokens via query string specifically for browser-based EventSource connections.

behaviors.rationale: Enables browser dashboards to subscribe to live updates.
behaviors.summary: Accepts a Bearer token from a query string parameter for browser SSE.
behaviors.detail: Browser-based clients use the EventSource API, which does not support custom headers. The system accepts a '?token=<token>' parameter in the URL to provide authentication context. This is used only on the hub-wide SSE endpoint where browsers connect directly. The token is processed identically to a header token for validation.

capabilities.name: Media Assets
capabilities.rationale: Makes the abstract 'orchestrator drives worker' concept concrete.
capabilities.description: Visual assets like screencasts that demonstrate the product flow.

features.name: Demo Screencast
features.rationale: Visually demonstrates the core dynamic that screenshots cannot show.
features.description: Short video showing a command sent in one window executing in another.

behaviors.rationale: Increases conversion by showing the product working.
behaviors.summary: Plays a narrated video of the orchestrator-to-worker flow.
behaviors.detail: The video shows a terminal window and a web UI. The voiceover explains the steps. The video is autoplayed or embedded in the README.

capabilities.name: Risk Communication
capabilities.rationale: Positions the product confidently against Anthropic's offerings.
capabilities.description: Sections in the README that pre-emptively answer questions about competitors and risks.

features.name: Competitor Comparison
features.rationale: Helps users choose the right tool for their use case.
features.description: Clarifies the difference between in-process and out-of-process orchestration.

behaviors.rationale: Clarifies product positioning early.
behaviors.summary: States that Anthropic Agent Teams is for in-process, TubeMail is for out-of-process.
behaviors.detail: The text explains the architectural distinction. It clarifies that TubeMail allows remote management from another host, while Agent Teams runs inside the harness.

capabilities.name: Health Dashboard
capabilities.rationale: Aggregates metrics inline to avoid a dedicated dashboard page.
capabilities.description: Visualizes system resource usage and health metrics for the fleet.

features.name: Resource Metrics
features.rationale: Provides immediate context for resource bottlenecks.
features.description: Inline display of CPU and memory usage for active agents.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents over-commitment of system resources.
behaviors.summary: Renders gauges or charts for CPU and memory of the active process.
behaviors.detail: The system queries the agent manager for current resource consumption. These values are displayed inline within the roster row so users can assess resource contention without leaving the main view.

features.name: Health Checks
features.rationale: Ensures the UI stays in sync with the backend reality.
features.description: Monitors git SHA and network connectivity.

behaviors.rationale: Provides accurate real-time status without user intervention.
behaviors.summary: Refreshes hub health status periodically.
behaviors.detail: The app calls the /health endpoint on mount and via SSE. It updates the version badge and handles redeploy events seamlessly.

behaviors.rationale: Enables automated failover logic.
behaviors.summary: Returns a 200 OK status if the forwarder is running and ready.
behaviors.detail: The health endpoint validates that the underlying channel plugin and event loop are operational, and returns a simple JSON response indicating the service is healthy or a 503 error if the connection is lost.

features.name: Health Check
features.rationale: Enables external monitoring and self-healing logic.
features.description: Provides a lightweight endpoint to check if the hub service is responsive.

behaviors.rationale: Verifies connectivity without exposing sensitive data.
behaviors.summary: Returns the current health status and version of the hub.
behaviors.detail: The endpoint returns a JSON object with status, service name, and build information without requiring authentication.

behaviors.rationale: Immediate data return is required to monitor fleet status effectively.
behaviors.summary: Returns aggregated KPIs and worker statistics via a dedicated endpoint.
behaviors.detail: The system exposes a JSON response containing active worker counts, pending permissions, and other key performance indicators to support operational monitoring.

features.name: Service Status Report
features.rationale: Provides immediate visibility into whether the hub is running correctly.
features.description: Reports the operational state, version, and deployment consistency of the hub service.

behaviors.rationale: Allows clients to confirm successful initialization.
behaviors.summary: The health endpoint returns a status indicator and version number.
behaviors.detail: Returns the service name, current version string, and operational status. When the service is not ready or encounters an internal error, the status reflects this state to the caller.

features.name: Deployment Consistency Check
features.rationale: Ensures operators are running the correct code version.
features.description: Verifies that the running code matches the expected deployment by comparing git commit hashes.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents deployment of stale or mismatched code.
behaviors.summary: The endpoint identifies the git SHA of the running codebase.
behaviors.detail: Reads the current git commit hash from the host environment, allowing operators to verify they are running the intended release. If the host lacks git or a valid directory is missing, it returns an empty string to trigger fallback logic.

features.name: Uptime Calculation
features.rationale: Helps operators identify recently restarted or flapping services.
features.description: Tracks how long the service has been running since its last start.
