behaviors.rationale: Allows monitoring of service stability and restart frequency.
behaviors.summary: The endpoint calculates and reports uptime in human-readable format.
behaviors.detail: Subtracts the start time from the current timestamp to determine uptime. The result is formatted as hours and minutes, or minutes and seconds, depending on magnitude.

features.name: Disk Usage Check
features.rationale: Helps operators detect storage exhaustion early.
features.description: Estimates storage consumption by summing file sizes in the data directory.

behaviors.rationale: Provides early warning of storage constraints.
behaviors.summary: The endpoint reports available disk space usage in megabytes.
behaviors.detail: Scans the root data directory, sums file sizes, and converts the total to megabytes with one decimal precision.

features.name: Busy State Detection
features.rationale: Allows clients to implement backoff strategies or rate limiting.
features.description: Indicates if the service is currently processing requests to prevent overload.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents triggering updates during high load.
behaviors.summary: The endpoint reports whether the service is currently busy.
behaviors.detail: Checks the busy flag provided by the service context. If busy, it indicates 'safe_to_restart' is false, signaling other components to wait or trigger updates.

features.name: Health Monitoring
features.rationale: Provides visibility into hub uptime and worker health.
features.description: Reports the system status and resource metrics.

behaviors.rationale: Matches /health endpoint spec.
behaviors.summary: Returns current system health and uptime metrics.
behaviors.detail: Includes disk usage, worker counts, and restart safety flags.

features.name: Manager Health & Rollback
features.rationale: Enables rapid recovery from stuck connections or silent failures.
features.description: Provides tools to diagnose agent connectivity issues and restart the local manager process.

behaviors.rationale: Provides actionable steps to restore connectivity quickly.
behaviors.summary: Displays specific error cards and offers a button to restart the manager.
behaviors.detail: When an agent is silent, the UI displays a 'Roll manager' card after a short delay, providing a clear path to resolve connection gaps without restarting the entire fleet.

features.name: Health Control
features.rationale: Provides a toggle mechanism to test system robustness.
features.description: API endpoints that simulate server failures and recovery for testing purposes.

behaviors.rationale: Validates the system's ability to detect and report failures.
behaviors.summary: Breaks the MCP endpoint to simulate a failure.
behaviors.detail: The '/control/break' endpoint sets an internal flag that causes all incoming requests to the '/mcp' path to return a 503 error with a recovery hint.

behaviors.rationale: Validates the system's recovery mechanisms.
behaviors.summary: Heals the MCP endpoint to restore normal operation.
behaviors.detail: The '/control/heal' endpoint clears the internal break flag and resets the break count, allowing MCP requests to proceed normally again.

features.name: Health Verification
features.rationale: Confirms the hub is functional before considering provisioning complete.
features.description: Polls the hub's health endpoint to confirm it is responding correctly.

behaviors.rationale: Validates the hub is serving traffic.
behaviors.summary: Polls the health endpoint until success or timeout.
behaviors.detail: The system repeatedly attempts to connect to the hub's health check URL. It retries the request at set intervals for a specified duration. If the endpoint returns a successful status, it reports success. If the timeout is reached, it reports failure.

behaviors.rationale: Provides visibility into startup failures.
behaviors.summary: Reports failure if health check times out.
behaviors.detail: If the health endpoint does not respond within the timeout period, the system gathers diagnostic logs from the container and reports a failure state to the user.

features.name: tm_health
features.rationale: Enables quick visual monitoring of the fleet.
features.description: Visualizes active agents, their health, and current task queues.

behaviors.rationale: Provides at-a-glance fleet visibility.
behaviors.summary: Displays a list of connected agents with health indicators.
behaviors.detail: Shows each connected agent's status (idle, busy, error) and allows filtering by host or agent type.

capabilities.name: Process Control
capabilities.rationale: Manual process management is a legacy requirement; automated via UI buttons.
capabilities.description: Provides buttons to start, stop, or restart specific agent processes.

features.name: Process Buttons
features.rationale: Enables manual intervention in agent life cycles.
features.description: Control panel elements to issue lifecycle commands to running agents.

behaviors.rationale: Allows quick recovery or maintenance operations.
behaviors.summary: Triggers a signal to the agent manager to start or stop the process.
behaviors.detail: Clicking a 'Start' button invokes the underlying MCP tool to launch a new process instance. Clicking 'Stop' sends a termination signal. These actions are exposed as simple buttons above the terminal chrome.

features.name: Process Lifecycle Management
features.rationale: Provides basic functionality to keep agents alive and restartable after normal or abnormal exits.
features.description: Controls the running, restarting, and stopping of Claude worker processes based on exit codes and signals.

behaviors.rationale: Continues work after a deliberate, clean stop request.
behaviors.summary: Restarts the process when it exits cleanly upon receiving a restart signal.
behaviors.detail: If the process exits with code 0 and the manager receives a restart signal, the manager types '/exit' into the pty and immediately restarts the process with the '--continue' flag.

behaviors.rationale: Recovers automatically from unexpected failures.
behaviors.summary: Restarts the process after a crash (non-zero exit code).
behaviors.detail: If the process exits with a non-zero exit code indicating a crash, the manager initiates a recovery by restarting the process with the '--continue' flag.

behaviors.rationale: Allows operators to terminate agents immediately.
behaviors.summary: Stops the process when explicitly commanded to exit.
behaviors.detail: When the manager receives a 'force_stop' signal, it types '/exit' into the pseudo-terminal and ensures the process terminates without restarting.

capabilities.name: Message Composer
capabilities.rationale: Parity feature for chat-based agent interaction; deferred until v1.5.
capabilities.description: Drafts and sends messages to specific workers or agents within the UI shell.

features.name: Draft Editor
features.rationale: Facilitates direct communication with the AI worker.
features.description: A text area for composing prompts or instructions to send to agents.

behaviors.rationale: Provides an alternative input method for agents.
behaviors.summary: Submits composed text to the agent as a new input message.
behaviors.detail: The system takes the user's input and injects it into the agent's context window. If the user is connected to a live terminal, they should prefer typing directly there; this UI route is secondary.

capabilities.name: Orchestration Library
capabilities.rationale: Automation feature; deferred until v1.5.
capabilities.description: Manages workflows and saved flow configurations for agents.

features.name: Flow Manager
features.rationale: Stores reusable patterns for agent behavior.
features.description: Repository for saved agent interaction patterns.

behaviors.rationale: Encourages reuse of proven agent patterns.
behaviors.summary: Allows users to save and load configurations for agent orchestration.
behaviors.detail: Users define a sequence of tools and conditions, save it as a 'Flow', and apply it to a worker. This feature is currently out of scope for v1 to focus on core management.

capabilities.name: Timeline Viewer
capabilities.rationale: Historical analysis capability; deferred until v1.5.
capabilities.description: Visualizes the sequence of events and actions taken by an agent over time.

features.name: Event Graph
features.rationale: Helps debug timing issues and sequence errors.
features.description: A visual representation of agent activity history.

behaviors.rationale: Aids in forensic analysis of agent failures.
behaviors.summary: Displays a scrollable history of events from the event log.
behaviors.detail: The viewer maps timestamps from the underlying event log to a visual timeline. It filters events by type (e.g., heartbeat, tool call, error) to allow focused debugging.

capabilities.name: Security Enforcement
capabilities.rationale: Security controls are non-negotiable and invisible to users but critical for trust.
capabilities.description: Implicit safeguards ensuring the platform cannot be attacked via pty or web routes.

features.name: Credential Rotation
features.rationale: Minimizes window of opportunity for attackers.
features.description: Short-lived tickets and rate limiting prevent long-term credential exposure.

behaviors.rationale: Expiry prevents attackers from using stolen tokens long-term.
behaviors.summary: Automatically invalidates tokens and limits issuance rate.
behaviors.detail: Tokens expire after TTL, and rate limits prevent mass issuance. If a token is used, it is immediately deleted to prevent reuse.

features.name: TLS Requirement Check
features.rationale: Prevents unencrypted transmission of sensitive agent keystrokes.
features.description: Determines if TLS is required based on the presence of server certificate and key files.

behaviors.rationale: Enforces encryption for production.
behaviors.summary: Rejects non-TLS connections if TLS certificates and keys are present on the server.
behaviors.detail: The system checks for the existence of /data/server.crt and /data/server.key. If both exist, TLS is considered required. If a connection attempt arrives via HTTP, the connection is refused immediately. If these files are missing, plain HTTP is allowed (suitable for local development).

features.name: Origin Validation
features.rationale: Protects agent sessions from malicious cross-origin attacks.
features.description: Validates the Origin header against an allowlist to prevent cross-site WebSocket hijacking.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents cross-origin hijacking.
behaviors.summary: Validates the Origin header and rejects connections from unlisted origins.
behaviors.detail: Upon connection attempt, the system reads the Origin header. If it does not match the configured allowlist (derived from TUBEMAIL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS environment variable or defaults), the connection is closed. This prevents a malicious page in another tab from hijacking a valid session.

capabilities.name: Session Recording
capabilities.rationale: Enables post-mortem analysis and replay without impacting runtime performance.
capabilities.description: Captures and persists terminal sessions for debugging, replay, and analysis.

features.name: Cast File Generation
features.rationale: Allows replay with standard asciinema tools.
features.description: Writes full-fidelity terminal recording to ASCII cast format.

behaviors.rationale: Provides standard metadata for the asciinema player.
behaviors.summary: Writes ASCII cast file with header.
behaviors.detail: On session start, a JSON header is written to the .cast file containing version, dimensions, timestamp, and worker title. The file remains open for append-only writes.

features.name: Frame Extraction
features.rationale: Enables programmatic parsing without terminal emulator dependencies.
features.description: Writes time-stamped, ANSI-stripped text frames to JSONL.

behaviors.rationale: Allows easy grep and slicing by time using standard tools.
behaviors.summary: Writes stripped text frames to JSONL.
behaviors.detail: Every write to the terminal stream is converted to UTF-8 text by stripping ANSI escape sequences and appended as a JSON object with a timestamp to the .frames.jsonl file.

features.name: Session Rotation
features.rationale: Prevents unbounded disk growth and ensures files fit into standard buffers.
features.description: Rotates files when size limits are exceeded to control disk usage.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures files remain small enough for efficient I/O and management.
behaviors.summary: Rotates to new session on file size limit.
behaviors.detail: When the active .cast file exceeds max_bytes_per_file, the current session is closed and a new one is opened with a new filename and fresh file handles.

behaviors.rationale: Protects the backend control bus from unauthorized access.
behaviors.summary: Validates and manages the active session token.
behaviors.detail: On load, the app attempts to retrieve a bearer token. If missing, it tries to bootstrap a temporary session. If valid, the user is granted access to the dashboard.

features.name: File Cleanup
features.rationale: Keeps total per-worker storage bounded by max_bytes_per_file * keep_files.
features.description: Garbage collects old recording files to stay within storage quota.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains storage quota compliance automatically.
behaviors.summary: Removes old files to meet size limits.
behaviors.detail: At initialization or rotation, the manager removes old .cast and .frames.jsonl files such that the total size of remaining files does not exceed the configured retention limit.

features.name: Ansi Stripping
features.rationale: Makes content readable in standard text viewers without a terminal emulator.
features.description: Removes control sequences to produce plain text.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures readability without vt100 dependencies.
behaviors.summary: Strips ANSI escape sequences from data.
behaviors.detail: Incoming pty bytes are scanned for ANSI CSI, OSC, or single-char escapes using a compiled regex and these bytes are removed before decoding to UTF-8.

features.name: Worker Purge
features.rationale: Prevents resource leaks from dead workers.
features.description: Removes stale worker connections exceeding age thresholds.

behaviors.rationale: Reclaims resources from dead sessions.
behaviors.summary: Purges workers offline beyond threshold.
behaviors.detail: Checks worker registry for connections exceeding max_age_s and removes them.

features.name: Ticket Management
features.rationale: Tracks transient operations with TTL.
features.description: Handles ticket-based state tracking with automatic expiration.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains transient state hygiene.
behaviors.summary: Manages ticket lifecycles with auto-expiration.
behaviors.detail: Creates and tracks tickets with TTL, sweeping expired ones periodically.

features.name: Session Recording
features.rationale: Allows operators to capture session history without interfering with real-time execution.
features.description: Enables or disables recording of terminal output for a specific worker session.

behaviors.rationale: Provides data for post-mortem analysis of execution issues.
behaviors.summary: Starts capturing the output of a worker's terminal to a persistent file.
behaviors.detail: The system writes the stdout/stderr of a connected session to a configured storage location. The recording continues until the session ends or is explicitly stopped.

behaviors.rationale: Persist session data.
behaviors.summary: Streams PTY output to files.
behaviors.detail: When enabled, the system streams PTY output to two parallel files: an asciinema cast and a JSONL frame index. Files rotate based on size limits and are garbage collected after a set count.

behaviors.rationale: Allows retrospective analysis of agent behavior.
behaviors.summary: The system streams session events for browser-less workers.
behaviors.detail: A recording stream captures all relevant log events and agent outputs, making them available for playback.

behaviors.rationale: Supports post-mortem analysis and transparency.
behaviors.summary: Streams terminal output to a secure log buffer.
behaviors.detail: Monitors the stdout/stderr of worker pty bridges and streams the output in real-time, allowing the UI or other agents to replay the session later.

capabilities.name: Secure WebSocket Auth
capabilities.rationale: Solves browser header limitations while keeping secrets out of logs.
capabilities.description: Manages the lifecycle of short-lived access tickets that bridge browser clients and hub backends.

features.name: Issue One-Use Ticket
features.rationale: Ensures tokens are worthless after expiration or single use.
features.description: Generates a unique, time-bound token scoped to a specific worker for WebSocket authentication.

behaviors.rationale: Provides the initial access credential required by the browser.
behaviors.summary: The system generates a new ticket token for a worker and returns it to the caller.
behaviors.detail: Upon receiving a request for a worker ticket, the system generates a cryptographically secure random token, associates it with the specified worker, and sets an expiration time of 30 seconds.

features.name: Validate Ticket Scope
features.rationale: Prevents lateral movement by rejecting tickets from other workers.
features.description: Verifies that a presented ticket is unexpired, valid, and scoped to the requested worker.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures strict worker isolation and ticket expiration enforcement.
behaviors.summary: The system validates a ticket against the worker ID and expiration time before allowing access.
behaviors.detail: When a client presents a ticket to open a WebSocket connection, the system checks if the ticket exists, is within the 30-second window, and matches the requested worker ID exactly.

features.name: Clean Up Expired Tickets
features.rationale: Keeps the store lightweight and prevents stale entries from being accidentally used.
features.description: Automatically removes tickets that have passed their expiration time to prevent memory growth.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains system health by removing obsolete credentials.
behaviors.summary: The system sweeps the store to identify and remove tickets that have expired.
behaviors.detail: A background task periodically checks all stored tickets and removes any where the current monotonic time exceeds the expiration timestamp.

features.name: Secure Transport Auth
features.rationale: Ensures only authorized forwarders can access the hub.
features.description: Validates and applies Bearer token for all HubClient interactions.

behaviors.rationale: Enforces security on all hub interactions.
behaviors.summary: All HTTP requests include a Bearer token for authorization.
behaviors.detail: The HubClient initializes an httpx.AsyncClient with a Bearer token header containing the TUBEMAIL_SECRET. Every request (POST, GET) automatically includes this header. If the token is invalid or revoked, the hub rejects the request with an HTTP 401 Unauthorized error.

capabilities.name: Hub Connectivity
capabilities.rationale: Requires secret handshake to join the fleet control bus
capabilities.description: Establishes and maintains a secure connection to the central TubeMail management hub.

features.name: Secure Hub Join
features.rationale: Enforces fleet access control via bearer secrets
features.description: Validates worker identity against the central hub before accepting commands.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents unauthorized worker registration
behaviors.summary: Initiates secure connection using hub URL and secret.
behaviors.detail: The worker reads the TUBEMAIL_HUB_URL and TUBEMAIL_SECRET environment variables. If the secret is missing, the worker refuses to start to prevent unauthorized access. Upon successful validation, the worker registers itself with the hub for the current working directory.

features.name: Dynamic Worker Naming
features.rationale: Enables unique identification across a fleet of local agents
features.description: Automatically detects the worker identity based on the current working directory.

behaviors.rationale: Provides default identity when not explicitly configured
behaviors.summary: Resolves worker name from environment override or current path.
behaviors.detail: The system first checks for the TM_WORKER_NAME environment variable. If set, it overrides the default. Otherwise, it uses the basename of the current working directory (cwd). If the cwd is empty or unspecified, it defaults to the generic name 'worker'.

capabilities.name: Hub Provisioning
capabilities.rationale: Guarantees a ready-to-use hub without manual intervention.
capabilities.description: Automates the initialization and verification of the TubeMail hub environment to ensure readiness for operation.

features.name: Environment Setup
features.rationale: Prevents runtime errors caused by missing configuration.
features.description: Ensures configuration files exist and contains required secrets for secure operation.

behaviors.rationale: Enables first-time bootstrapping of the system.
behaviors.summary: Creates a secret key if the configuration file is missing.
behaviors.detail: The system checks for an environment file. If missing, it creates one with a freshly generated secure secret token. If the file exists but lacks the secret, it appends the secret to the file.

behaviors.rationale: Safely restores missing security credentials.
behaviors.summary: Updates configuration if the secret is missing.
behaviors.detail: If the configuration file exists but does not contain the required secret key, the system appends the key to the existing file without removing other content.

features.name: Container Management
features.rationale: Automatically brings the service online when ready.
features.description: Verifies the Docker container is running and starts the hub if necessary.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the latest hub code is compiled.
behaviors.summary: Builds the Docker image if not present.
behaviors.detail: The system queries the container registry for the hub image. If the image is missing, it triggers the Docker build process to compile the hub image from the project.

behaviors.rationale: Restores service availability instantly.
behaviors.summary: Starts the container if not running.
behaviors.detail: If the image is built but the container is not running, the system initiates the container using detached mode to keep the hub operational in the background.

capabilities.name: Infrastructure State Model

capabilities.description: Internal logic determining worker availability signals from timeline events.

features.name: Busy Detection
features.rationale: Ensures status signals accurately reflect processing state.
features.description: Logic that determines if a worker is busy based on its event timeline.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents orchestrators from prematurely terminating long-running tasks.
behaviors.summary: Reports busy when the latest event is an unanswered inbound.
behaviors.detail: The logic checks the most recent event in the worker's timeline; if it is an 'inbound' kind event, the state is reported as 'busy'. If it is an 'outbound', it returns 'idle'.

behaviors.detail: The installer checks if the target settings file exists; if not, it logs a message and skips. It loads the existing settings, creates a 'hooks' object if missing, and adds a 'Stop' entry containing the specific command to run the post_stop_relay script.

capabilities.description: Handles the loading, saving, and validation of Hub configuration files.

features.description: Loads and validates the configuration from a local JSON file.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures system operability despite config errors.

behaviors.detail: The system reads the configuration file. If the file exists and is valid, its settings are applied. If the file is missing or malformed, the system logs a warning, reverts to default settings, and proceeds to allow operation. The configuration contains simple types like booleans and integers, avoiding complex encryption or environment overrides.

behaviors.rationale: Enforces access control boundaries.

features.name: Localhost Gating
features.rationale: Mitigates network exposure risks.
features.description: Optionally limits the server to localhost only for development or low-trust scenarios.

behaviors.rationale: Reduces attack surface.
behaviors.summary: Restricts network binding to the loopback interface.
behaviors.detail: When configured, the server binds to 127.0.0.1 instead of 0.0.0.0, preventing external network connections.

capabilities.name: Permission Bridge
capabilities.rationale: Facilitates secure human-in-the-loop decision making
capabilities.description: Manages a shared approval exchange for handling sensitive operations requiring user consent.

features.name: Unix Socket Server
features.rationale: Provides a safe socket for the approval handshake to occur
features.description: Runs a local server to expose the approval exchange to the PreToolUse hook.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures service continuity despite infrastructure issues
behaviors.summary: Starts a hook server for approval exchange.
behaviors.detail: The HookServer starts a background process on a local Unix socket. This socket allows the PreToolUse hook (which runs within the LLM context) to communicate with the worker's approval exchange logic. If the server fails to start, the worker continues running in a degraded mode but stops accepting high-risk commands.

features.name: Approval Exchange
features.rationale: Ensures consistency even if the user approves before the tool fires
features.description: Coordinates approval requests between the channel and the hook server.

behaviors.rationale: Handles timing discrepancies between UI and agent layers
behaviors.summary: Synchronizes approval status between hook and channel.
behaviors.detail: The exchange object maintains a buffer of pending requests. It handles race conditions where the hook might approve an action before the channel-side notification is emitted. It ensures both sides see a consistent state of what is approved and what is pending.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures no request is lost when the hook decision precedes the notification.
behaviors.summary: Accepts permission requests from the notification channel and stores them until an approval decision is made.
behaviors.detail: When a tool use is initiated but blocked pending a hub decision, the system stores the request with a unique ID and timestamp. If the channel notification arrives before the local hook resolves, the stored request is immediately forwarded to the hub. If the hook resolves first, the system stores the approval decision for later matching.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents data loss when notifications arrive before local decisions.
behaviors.summary: Accepts permission requests from the notification channel and stores them until an approval decision is made.
behaviors.detail: When a channel notification arrives indicating a permission request, the system checks if a matching approval decision is already waiting in the buffer. If a matching approval exists, it consumes it and prepares the request for forwarding. If no approval is waiting, the request is stored with its ID and timestamp for later processing.

behaviors.rationale: Completes the delegation loop by forwarding approved actions to the hub.
behaviors.summary: Relays matched approval requests to the hub for final resolution.
behaviors.detail: When an approval decision is matched with a pending request, the system constructs a complete payload containing both the tool call details and the approval status. This payload is then sent to the hub's permission-response endpoint. The system waits for the hub to confirm receipt before cleaning up the local buffer entries.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents buffer exhaustion from stale or unresponsive requests.
behaviors.summary: Clean up expired entries to maintain buffer integrity.
behaviors.detail: The system periodically reviews pending buffer entries and removes those that have exceeded their time-to-live threshold. This prevents memory leaks and ensures that stale entries do not interfere with active requests. Entries that are cleaned up are logged for monitoring purposes.

behaviors.rationale: Allows local auto-approvals to bypass the hub when appropriate.
behaviors.summary: Handles cases where approvals wait indefinitely without matching requests.
behaviors.detail: If an approval decision is stored in the buffer but no corresponding request notification ever arrives, the approval is kept in the buffer until its TTL expires. This allows for scenarios where a tool is auto-approved locally without ever triggering the hub notification mechanism.

behaviors.rationale: Improves performance by skipping unnecessary hub calls for safe operations.
behaviors.summary: Provides read-only tool approvals without hub interaction.
behaviors.detail: Certain tools classified as read-only (such as file listing, search, and web fetching) are automatically approved by the local hook without requiring hub interaction. This bypass mechanism is configured via a whitelist of approved tools and a regex pattern matching safe shell commands.

behaviors.rationale: Preserves state history.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains security posture.

behaviors.detail: The system uses HTTPS for web interfaces and validates tokens for MCP calls, ensuring data integrity.

capabilities.name: Relay Outbound
capabilities.rationale: Ensures every assistant output reaches the timeline for downstream consumption.
capabilities.description: Automatically posts assistant messages to the timeline when a Claude Code session stops, even if the agent didn't explicitly call the reply tool.

features.name: Stop Event Relay
features.rationale: Completes the record chain when the optional reply tool was skipped.
features.description: Captures and forwards the assistant's final message text to the hub upon session termination.

behaviors.rationale: Captures best-effort text from stop payload.
behaviors.summary: Relays the last assistant message to the hub on stop.
behaviors.detail: When a Claude Code worker stops, this hook reads the conversation payload or transcript file to extract the assistant's final prose content. It then POSTs this text to the designated outbound endpoint so the message is recorded as a timeline event regardless of whether the agent invoked the reply tool.

behaviors.rationale: Fail-open to prevent blocking the stop process.
behaviors.summary: Handles transcript files robustly.
behaviors.detail: The hook attempts to read an inline messages array if present, falling back to a JSONL transcript file on disk. It is tolerant of varying Claude Code schema versions by trying multiple dictionary access patterns.

behaviors.rationale: Excludes structured events to send only prose output.
behaviors.summary: Filters irrelevant content blocks.
behaviors.detail: The parser ignores tool-use and tool-result blocks, concatenating only 'text' and 'thinking' blocks to reconstruct the full assistant response including any reasoning fences.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents false positives on external systems.
behaviors.summary: Skips execution outside of sessions.
behaviors.detail: The hook checks for the TM_WORKER_NAME environment variable and exits immediately if not set, ensuring it only runs within a valid tubemail-channel context.

behaviors.rationale: Signals event origin for downstream filtering.
behaviors.summary: Tags events for deduplication.
behaviors.detail: The POSTed payload includes a meta.kind field set to 'stop_relay'. This tag allows downstream consumers to identify and potentially deduplicate entries if the LLM also fired the reply tool.

behaviors.rationale: Uses standard HTTP to push data to the bus.
behaviors.summary: Sends POST requests to the hub.
behaviors.detail: The hook constructs the correct outbound URL and uses a standard HTTP POST client to send the JSON body. It defaults to localhost:8001 but allows configuration for other hubs.

behaviors.rationale: Essential for debugging and monitoring system behavior.
behaviors.summary: Records events like ticket issuance and WebSocket bridge operations.
behaviors.detail: The system logs key events such as when a ticket is issued, when a WebSocket bridge is opened or closed, and when API requests are rejected. These logs are stored in a centralized logging system for later review.

capabilities.name: PTY Bridging
capabilities.rationale: Enables headless control for CI or script-based workflows.
capabilities.description: Supports optional pseudo-terminal (PTY) attachment for interactive sessions without UI.

features.name: Conditional Pty Detach
features.rationale: Avoids orphaned streams when a user is already watching.
features.description: Decides whether to detach a PTY stream based on concurrent browser clients.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents resource leaks.
behaviors.summary: Fires pty_detach only when no browsers are viewing.
behaviors.detail: When recording or bridging changes, the engine checks active browser clients; if none exist, it detaches the PTY.

features.name: PTY Bridging
features.rationale: Enables interactive debugging of agent processes remotely.
features.description: Streams terminal output and accepts keyboard input for a specific worker.

behaviors.rationale: Critical for observing low-level agent interaction.
behaviors.summary: Streams terminal bytes to the browser session.
behaviors.detail: Given a worker is attached to a PTY session, When the terminal outputs bytes, Then the browser receives the byte stream in real-time.

capabilities.name: Infrastructure Backbone
capabilities.rationale: Provides the stable, secure foundation required for running local agents.
capabilities.description: Docker-based runtime and security layers that power the worker and control plane.

features.name: Secure Bridge
features.rationale: Critical for preserving the interactive experience without privilege escalation.
features.description: Pty bridge that safely relays terminal input and output between containers.

behaviors.rationale: Core requirement for terminal emulation.
behaviors.summary: Establishes a secure pseudoterminal connection between the control plane and worker.
behaviors.detail: The infrastructure manages the PTY allocation and I/O forwarding. It ensures that only authorized processes can read or write to the terminal buffers.

features.name: Audit Gate
features.rationale: Ensures no uncommitted audit work is visible to the public.
features.description: Quality control layer that verifies codebase state before public exposure.

behaviors.rationale: Protects product integrity on Day 1.
behaviors.summary: Blocks the launch if uncommitted audit changes are detected.
behaviors.detail: The gate checks the repository state and commits required audit work. It prevents the public flip until quality is assured.

features.name: PyPI Stub
features.rationale: Prevents squatting and ensures a clean namespace for the official release.
features.description: Placeholder package that reserves the namespace before the official release.

behaviors.rationale: Defensive measure against squatting.
behaviors.summary: Publishes a minimal package that points to the real implementation later.
behaviors.detail: The stub package is published to PyPI. It contains metadata pointing to the final package. Once ready, the stub is replaced by the full distribution.

features.name: Security Hardening
features.rationale: Addresses critical vulnerabilities in the worker management protocol.
features.description: Implementation of security mitigations for path traversal and timing attacks.

behaviors.rationale: Mitigates critical security vulnerability.
behaviors.summary: Implements constant-time string comparison and path sanitization.
behaviors.detail: The infrastructure patches the bearer token comparison logic and validates file paths. This prevents timing attacks and directory traversal.

capabilities.name: Intake
capabilities.rationale: Gate external change requests — triage, sharpen, dedup, classify; nothing graduates without a Kano level.
capabilities.description: Incoming spec change requests from external modules (iris-qa, quartermaster, other agents). Requests land here for triage (sharpen + dedup + kano classification) before promotion into Caps 1-4. See skill create-spec-item.

features.name: Spec Change Handling
features.rationale: Ensures smooth integration with upstream modules.
features.description: Processes incoming change requests from external modules like iris-qa.

behaviors.rationale: Automates integration workflows from external sources.
behaviors.summary: Ingests change requests from external systems.
behaviors.detail: When an external module sends a change request, the system processes it and updates the relevant configuration.

capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Every intake item names its source agent, proposed Kano level, and target cap before promotion.

capabilities.name: Live Development
capabilities.rationale: Improves developer productivity by enabling fast iteration.
capabilities.description: Supports hot-reloading of code during development without affecting production safety.

features.name: Hot Reload
features.rationale: Allows developers to see changes instantly without manual restarts.
features.description: Automatically restarts the application when source code changes are detected.

behaviors.rationale: Enables rapid development cycle without manual intervention.
behaviors.summary: Monitors source directory and restarts on change.
behaviors.detail: The application server watches the source directory for file modifications. When a change is detected, it triggers an automatic restart process. This allows developers to iterate on features quickly.

capabilities.name: KPI Calculation
capabilities.rationale: Distill how numbers on dashboards get made — KPI pipelines are abstract; document them here, not in the UI.
capabilities.description: KPI derivation specs. Not Kano-rated (abstract benefit, no direct customer satisfaction).

features.name: KPI Calculation
features.rationale: Abstracts raw data into meaningful benefits for stakeholders.
features.description: Internal logic used to derive high-level performance metrics.

behaviors.rationale: Transforms raw logs into actionable insights.
behaviors.summary: The system calculates aggregate metrics from agent telemetry.
behaviors.detail: The backend engine sums up individual worker latencies and success rates to produce fleet-wide KPIs.

capabilities.gherkin: Rule: Every KPI has a behavior documenting its source data, formula, and refresh cadence.

capabilities.name: Input Validation
capabilities.rationale: Prevents injection attacks and ensures data integrity in all operations.
capabilities.description: Validates all input parameters like flow names and run IDs to ensure security and consistency across the system.

features.name: Flow Name Validation
features.rationale: Prevents path traversal and ensures consistent naming across all components.
features.description: Validates flow names against a regex pattern to ensure safe filesystem paths.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents filesystem corruption and security vulnerabilities.
behaviors.summary: Flow names are validated against a specific regex pattern on all operations.
behaviors.detail: The system checks that flow names start with an alphanumeric character and contain only allowed characters. Path traversal attempts using .. are rejected immediately.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures filesystem compatibility and operational efficiency.
behaviors.summary: Flow names must be non-empty and within length limits for safe storage.
behaviors.detail: The validation ensures names are within acceptable length bounds to prevent filesystem issues and maintain readability in logs and interfaces.

features.name: Run ID Validation
features.rationale: Ensures only legitimate run IDs can be used to track executions.
features.description: Validates run IDs to ensure they are secure random tokens and cannot be forged by external callers.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents security exploits through malformed identifiers.
behaviors.summary: Run IDs must match a strict pattern of alphanumeric characters and hyphens.
behaviors.detail: The system checks that run IDs are between 16 and 64 characters long and contain only allowed characters. This prevents injection of malicious paths or identifiers.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures all run IDs, regardless of source, are secure.
behaviors.summary: Run IDs generated internally follow the same validation rules for consistency.
behaviors.detail: Even internally generated run IDs pass through the validation logic to ensure they are safe. This ensures that the system's own output is always valid.

features.name: Worker Name Regex
features.rationale: Ensures worker names can be safely used as filesystem paths.
features.description: Enforces a regex pattern on worker names to allow alphanumeric characters and limited symbols.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains security and filesystem integrity.
behaviors.summary: Rejects worker names containing '..' or characters outside the allowed set.
behaviors.detail: Before processing any endpoint call, the system validates the worker name against _WORKER_NAME_RE. This regex allows alphanumeric start characters and a limited set of punctuation. It explicitly rejects any name containing '..' to prevent directory traversal attacks. Invalid names result in a 400 Bad Request error.

capabilities.name: Persistent Storage Layer
capabilities.rationale: Provides reliable persistence for all application state without requiring a database.
capabilities.description: Implements a flat-file storage system for flows and run logs using atomic write operations to ensure reliability during crashes or interruptions.

features.name: Directory Structure
features.rationale: Separates templates from execution logs for maintainability and clarity.
features.description: Organizes data into separate directories for flows and runs under a base data path.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the storage system is ready for immediate use.
behaviors.summary: The system creates the necessary data directories if they do not exist.
behaviors.detail: On initialization, the system creates the flows and runs directories with their parents if needed. This ensures a consistent directory structure for all storage operations.

features.name: Atomic File Operations
features.rationale: Prevents partial writes from corrupting persistent state.
features.description: Uses temporary files and rename operations for all writes to ensure data integrity even during failures.

behaviors.rationale: Guarantees data integrity for all persisted files.
behaviors.summary: All file writes use an atomic pattern to guarantee data consistency.
behaviors.detail: The system writes to a temporary file first, then renames it to the final path. This atomic operation is guaranteed by the operating system to be all-or-nothing, even if interrupted.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures readers never see partial or corrupted data.
behaviors.summary: If a write operation fails mid-process, no corrupted file is left behind.
behaviors.detail: If the write fails or is interrupted, the temporary file is removed or left as-is without affecting the original file. The rename operation ensures that only complete writes are visible to readers.

features.name: Persistent State Storage
features.rationale: Prevents data loss on engine restarts.
features.description: Stores worker state as JSON files on the local disk for durability and recovery.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures state integrity on write.
behaviors.summary: Writes state changes to atomic temporary files.
behaviors.detail: Before saving a state update, the engine writes to a temporary file and then atomically renames it to prevent corruption during crashes.

behaviors.rationale: Allows graceful restarts without downtime.
behaviors.summary: Recovers state from JSON files on startup.
behaviors.detail: On initialization, the engine scans the workers directory and loads all valid JSON files into memory, ignoring invalid filenames.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains partial availability after corruption.
behaviors.summary: Skips corrupted or invalid state files.
behaviors.detail: If a JSON file cannot be parsed or has an invalid name, the engine logs a warning but continues loading other valid files.

capabilities.name: Data Serialization
capabilities.rationale: Enables human readability and interoperability of stored data.
capabilities.description: Converts data structures to JSON format for storage and deserializes them on retrieval.

features.name: JSON Serialization
features.rationale: Provides a standard, portable format for data persistence.
features.description: Converts Flow and RunLog objects to JSON strings for persistent storage.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures data is stored in a readable and standard format.
behaviors.summary: Flow objects are serialized to JSON with indentation for readability.
behaviors.detail: When a Flow object is saved, it is converted to a JSON string with two-space indentation. This makes debugging and manual inspection easier for operators.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures logs are stored in a consistent and readable format.
behaviors.summary: Run logs are also serialized to JSON with consistent formatting.
behaviors.detail: RunLog objects are serialized in the same manner, ensuring consistency across all stored logs. This uniformity simplifies parsing and inspection.

features.name: JSON Deserialization
features.rationale: Enables programmatic access to stored data.
features.description: Converts stored JSON files back to Flow and RunLog objects on retrieval.

behaviors.rationale: Enables access to stored flow definitions for inspection.
behaviors.summary: Stored JSON files are parsed into Flow objects on retrieval.
behaviors.detail: When a flow is retrieved, the system reads the JSON file and deserializes it into a Flow object. Any parsing errors are logged, and the system handles invalid files gracefully.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures the system is resilient to data corruption.
behaviors.summary: Run logs are also deserialized on retrieval with error handling.
behaviors.detail: If a run log file is corrupted or invalid, the system logs a warning but continues to return a null value for that specific run. This ensures the system remains operational despite data issues.
